title: Adana yogurtlu kebab
instructions: Prepare the chicken marinade – combine yogurt, garlic, paprika, cumin, onion, lemon zest and juice, olive oil, coriander, salt, and pepper. Cut chicken into 3cm cubes and add to marinade, then leave in the fridge for at least two hours.

Meanwhile, prepare the sauce. Chop the onion and pepper, and cook with a little olive oil for 5-6 minutes until soft. Add the garlic and chilli and cook for a few more minutes, then add the tomatoes, salt and pepper. Bring to a simmer and cover, then cook for at least 1.5 hours. Season to taste.

While the sauce is cooking, prepare the spiced butter. Add the butter and chill flakes to a small pan and place oer a low heat. Cook until the butter starts to brown, then remove from the heat and set aside.
Grill or barbecue the chicken as required, and set aside.
Assemble the dish – place a few small hunks of pide in a bowl and top with yoghurt. Add some chicken, then pour the sauce over, Top with more yoghurt and the spiced butter.
notes: This is a Turkish-style preparation of chicken thigh kebabs with a tomato sauce, bread, and yoghurt. It needs some Turkish pide.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Aioli

ingredients.text: 2 garlic cloves, minced or mashed to a paste

instructions: Whisk garlic paste, egg yolk, mustard, and lemon juice together in a bowl.
Drizzle in oil a few drops at a time while whisking constantly, until it starts to thicken.
Continue drizzling in remaining oil in a thin stream, whisking, until thick and glossy.
Season with salt and refrigerate until serving.
notes: Mediterranean garlic mayonnaise, traditionally served with vegetables, seafood, or fries.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Alfredo Sauce

ingredients.text: Salt and black pepper to taste

instructions: Melt butter in a saucepan and sauté garlic 1 minute until fragrant.
Add cream and bring to a gentle simmer.
Whisk in Parmesan a little at a time until melted and smooth.
Season with salt, pepper, and nutmeg if using.
Toss immediately with hot pasta.
notes: American-Italian steakhouse-style version of the simple Roman butter-and-cheese sauce.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Amritsari Dal
instructions: Cook both dals together until smooth.
Sauté onion in butter until deep golden.
Add ginger-garlic paste and tomatoes; cook 8 minutes.
Stir in garam masala and dal.
Simmer 10 minutes; top with fresh ginger.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Ants Climbing a Tree
instructions: Soak vermicelli 10 minutes.
Brown pork with garlic and doubanjiang.
Add broth, soy sauce, and wine; bring to simmer.
Add vermicelli; cook until broth is absorbed.
Garnish with scallions.
notes: Sichuan minced pork over glass noodles.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Apple Cinnamon Buckwheat Porridge
instructions: Simmer buckwheat with milk until creamy.
Cook apple with cinnamon in a small pan until soft.
Serve porridge with warm apples and almond butter.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Apple Crisp

ingredients.text: 1/2 cup, cold and cubed unsalted butter

instructions: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees.
Peel the apples, core them, and slice about 1/4 inch thick.
Toss the slices with the granulated sugar, cinnamon, nutmeg, and lemon juice.
Spread the seasoned apple slices evenly in the baking dish.
In a separate bowl, combine the oats, flour, brown sugar, and salt.
Scatter the crumble topping evenly over the apples.
Bake for 35-40 minutes until the topping is deep golden brown and the juices are bubbling.
Let it cool for 10-15 minutes before serving.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Apple Sauce (for Pork)
instructions: Combine apples and water in a saucepan.
Cover and simmer 12 minutes, stirring occasionally, until apples break down.
Mash to desired texture with a fork or blend for a smooth sauce.
Stir in sugar, butter, and lemon juice.
notes: Classic sharp-sweet English accompaniment to roast pork.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Arancini (Stuffed Rice Balls)

ingredients.text: 5 mozzarella cheese sticks, cut into 2–2.5 cm pieces

instructions: Mash rice/risotto to a soft paste (warm briefly if cold) so it binds.
Sauté onion and bell pepper in 1 tbsp of the oil over medium heat until soft; season with a pinch of salt and red pepper flakes. Cool slightly.
Combine mashed rice, sautéed vegetables, 1/4 cup (15–20 g) bread crumbs, 2 tbsp flour, and 1 tbsp corn starch; mix until cohesive. Adjust seasoning (salt/pepper).
Divide and form 5 balls (or smaller), inserting a mozzarella piece in the center; seal well.
Battering: In a bowl whisk 3 tbsp flour, 2 tbsp corn starch, salt, pepper with enough water (≈60 ml) to form a thick, clinging batter. Put remaining bread crumbs in a separate shallow dish.
Coat each ball in batter (wet hand) then roll in bread crumbs (dry hand). Arrange on a tray. Freeze 10–15 minutes to firm (optional) or freeze longer for later.
Air Fry: Preheat to 180°C / 360°F for 3 minutes. Lightly mist or brush balls with remaining oil. Cook 6 minutes, shake/turn, then another 5–6 minutes until deep golden and crisp.

Deep Fry: Heat 5 cm (2 inches) oil to 175–180°C (350–355°F). Fry 2–3 balls at a time 3–4 minutes, turning, until uniformly golden and cheese just melting. Drain on paper or a rack; season lightly with salt while hot.
author: Marcus Baw (pacharanero/recipes)

title: Asian Sesame Cabbage Slaw
instructions: Shred cabbage and carrot finely.
Whisk rice vinegar, sesame oil, and soy sauce.
Toss vegetables with dressing.
Rest 10 minutes for flavors to meld.
Garnish with sesame seeds and scallions.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Asian Sesame Noodle Salad
instructions: Cook the noodles according to package directions. Drain, rinse under cold water until completely cool, and toss with a splash of sesame oil to prevent sticking.
Cook 1 1/2 cups frozen edamame according to package directions (usually 3–4 minutes in boiling water). Drain and cool.
Julienne the cucumber and thinly shred 2 cups of red cabbage.
Make the dressing: whisk together soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, honey, grated ginger, garlic, lime juice, and sriracha if using.
In a large bowl, combine the cold noodles, edamame, cucumber, shredded carrots, and red cabbage.
Pour the dressing over everything and toss thoroughly to coat.
Top with sliced green onions and a generous sprinkle of sesame seeds.
Serve cold or at room temperature.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Asian Slaw with Rice Vinegar
instructions: Combine cabbage, carrot, and apple.
Whisk vinegar, oil, ginger, honey, and salt.
Massage slaw with dressing 1 minute.
Rest 15 minutes.
Serve chilled or at room temperature.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Avocado Herb Cottage Toast
instructions: Toast the sourdough.
Mix cottage cheese with herbs, lemon, salt, and pepper.
Spread avocado on toast, top with cottage cheese, and finish with chili flakes.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Baked Apples with Oat Crumble
instructions: Halve and core the apples.
Mix oats, almond flour, fat, maple syrup, and cinnamon.
Top apples with crumble and bake at 190°C until tender.
Serve warm.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Baked Cod with Tomatoes
instructions: Place cod in a baking dish with tomatoes and garlic.
Drizzle with olive oil; season.
Bake at 200°C for 18 minutes until fish flakes.
Scatter capers and parsley before serving.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Baked Falafel Bowls with Herb Sauce
instructions: Pulse chickpeas, garlic, cumin, parsley, and oat flour into a coarse mix.
Shape into small patties and bake at 210°C until crisp.
Serve over bulgur with yogurt herb sauce and salad.
Add lemon wedges to finish.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Baked Mac and Cheese
instructions: Preheat your oven to 375°F (190°C). Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil.
Cook the elbow macaroni for 1 minute less than the package directions. You want it just slightly underdone since it will keep cooking in the oven. Drain and set aside.
In the same pot, melt 4 tablespoons of butter over medium heat. Once it's foaming, add the flour and whisk constantly for about 1 minute to cook out the raw flour taste. This is your roux.

Slowly pour in the milk and heavy cream while whisking. Keep whisking to prevent lumps. Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer and cook for 3-4 minutes until it thickens enough to coat the back of a spoon.
Remove from heat. Add the mustard powder, garlic powder, smoked paprika, cayenne, salt, and pepper. Stir to combine.
Add the shredded cheddar in three batches, stirring after each addition until fully melted and smooth. Reserve about 1/2 cup of cheese for the top.
Fold the drained macaroni into the cheese sauce until every noodle is coated.
Pour into a greased 9x13 baking dish and spread evenly.
In a small bowl, toss the panko breadcrumbs with 1 tablespoon of melted butter. Scatter the breadcrumbs and remaining shredded cheese over the top.
Bake uncovered for 25-30 minutes until the edges are bubbly and the breadcrumb topping is golden brown.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Baked Oatmeal with Berries
instructions: Whisk oats, milk, eggs, baking powder, cinnamon, and syrup.
Pour into a greased baking dish.
Top with berries.
Bake at 180°C for 30 minutes until set.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Baked Oatmeal with Pear and Hazelnut
instructions: Mix oats, pears, hazelnuts, and cinnamon in a baking dish.
Whisk milk, egg, and maple syrup and pour over.
Bake at 190°C for 25 minutes until set.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Baked Ziti
instructions: Preheat your oven to 375°F (190°C). Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil.
Cook the penne for 2 minutes less than the package directions -- it will finish cooking in the oven. Drain and set aside.

While the pasta cooks, heat a tablespoon of olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the ground beef, breaking it up with a wooden spoon. Cook until browned and no pink remains, about 7-8 minutes. Drain any excess grease.
Add the minced garlic, Italian seasoning, and red pepper flakes to the beef. Cook for another minute until fragrant.
Pour in the marinara sauce and stir to combine. Let it simmer for 3-4 minutes, then season with salt and pepper.
In a separate bowl, mix the ricotta cheese, egg, half of the shredded mozzarella, and the parmesan. Stir until smooth.
Combine the drained pasta with the meat sauce and toss until everything is coated.
Spread half of the pasta-meat mixture in a greased 9x13 baking dish. Drop spoonfuls of the ricotta mixture evenly across the top. Add the remaining pasta on top and spread it out.
Cover with the remaining mozzarella cheese.
Cover the dish tightly with foil and bake for 25 minutes. Remove the foil and bake for another 10 minutes until the cheese is golden and bubbly.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Basic Vegan Nut Roast
instructions: Fry onions in a little oil over medium heat until translucent (≈5 minutes).
Add carrot, tomatoes, breadcrumbs, and stock; cook gently 15–20 minutes until thick.
Remove from heat; stir in ground nuts. Preheat oven to 200°C (392°F).
Line or grease a loaf tin; pack mixture in evenly.
Bake 25–30 minutes until set and lightly browned. Rest 5–10 minutes before slicing.
author: Marcus Baw (pacharanero/recipes)

title: Béarnaise Sauce
instructions: Simmer vinegar, wine, shallot, and half the tarragon until reduced to about 1 tbsp. Strain and cool slightly.
Whisk egg yolks with the reduction in a heatproof bowl over simmering water until pale and thickened.
Remove from heat and slowly drizzle in melted butter, whisking until emulsified.
Stir in remaining tarragon, salt, and pepper.
Serve warm over grilled steak.
notes: Hollandaise's herbal cousin, the classic steakhouse sauce for filet and rib-eye.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Beef brisket chilli
instructions: Place the Ancho chillies in a bowl and pour over the coffee. Set aside.
Trim the brisket to remove all fat and skin. This is a pretty gnarly job and always takes longer than you think. Cut into 3cm cubes, against the grain.

Heat the olive oil in the pan over a low heat. Add the spices – cumin, paprika, oregano, bay leaves, and the onions. Cook until the onion has softened and just starting turning brown – about 10 minutes.
Slice the rehydrated chillies, and add to the onion mixture along with half of the fresh chillies, the garlic, cocoa powder, and some salt and pepper. Stir to combine.

Pour in the coffee, tinned tomatoes, and the molasses. Break the tomatoes up a little with a spoon, then add the brisket and cover. Leave for about three hours, simmering gently and stirring occasionally.
When the meat is cooked, it should basically be falling apart. Take two forks, and gently pull apart the chunks.
Add the bell peppers, then drain and add the beans. Stir to combine, then leave simmering uncovered for about 30 minutes.
Add the lime juice, then have a taste and add additional seasoning as required. Serve with rice or tortillas, along with sour cream, guacamole, cheese, and all the usual fixins.
notes: This is a from-scratch chilli made with pulled beef brisket rather than mince – the texture is wonderful. You can use a variety of different kinds of beans, but you should usually include at least some kidney beans. If you have any liquid smoke, a couple of teaspoons can add a nice smoky undertone.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Beef Lo Mein
instructions: Toss beef with cornstarch.
Cook noodles; drain.
Stir-fry beef in hot oil until browned; remove.
Stir-fry pepper, snow peas, and garlic.
Return beef with noodles, soy sauce, and hoisin; toss 2 minutes.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Beef Stew
instructions: Toss chuck roast cubes with flour, salt, and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a skillet over high heat and sear beef in batches until browned on all sides. Transfer to slow cooker.
Add potatoes, carrots, onions, and garlic to the slow cooker.
Pour in chicken broth, tomato paste, Worcestershire sauce, thyme, and rosemary. Stir to combine.
Cover and cook on LOW for 8 hours or HIGH for 4 hours, until beef is fork-tender and vegetables are soft.
Taste and adjust seasoning before serving.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Bengali Masoor Dal
instructions: Boil masoor dal with bay leaf until soft.
Heat mustard oil until smoking lightly; add panch phoron and chili.
Add ginger and tomato; cook 5 minutes.
Mix into dal and simmer 8 minutes.
Garnish with cilantro.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Berry Beet Recovery Smoothie
instructions: Blend beetroot, berries, banana, kefir, and oats until smooth.
Serve cold.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Berry Biryani
instructions: First, start the onions. Heat the vegetable oil over a medium hear, then slice each onion in half, then into fine slices. Add the onion to the hot oil and allow to cook until golden brown. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on kitchen paper.

Rinse the rice by putting it in a large bowl and covering with water. Gently swirl the rice around to wash off the starch, then pour off the water. Repeat a couple of times, then cover with water and leave to one side to soak for 1 hour.

Prepare the ingredients for the base, starting with a garlic and ginger paste. Peel the ginger; split into two portions. Cut one half into fine matchsticks and add to the biryani pot, and add the other half to a food processor or mortar and pestle. Peel the garlic and add that too, then blend/grind into a fine paste and add to the pot.
Slice each chilli into strips and add to the pot, along with the spices, herbs, lime juice, oil, and yoghurt. Add two-thirds of the fried onions as well, keeping one third aside.
Cut the thighs into three or four pieces each, and add to the pot. Mix everything thoroughly and set aside to marinate for a while.
Add the saffron to 30ml of boiling water and leave to one side. Melt the butter and cream together, and set aside also.
After the rice has soaked, part-cook it. Start bringing two litres of water to a boil in a pan; add the salt and lime juice.
Pre-heat the oven to 200℃. Place the biryani pot over a medium heat and start to warm the base ingredients through while the rice is cooking.
Drain the rice and add to the water. Boil for 4-5 minutes until slightly cooked – it should be slightly firm. Drain the rice, leaving a little bit of water to cling to it.

Add the rice to the biryani pot on top of the base ingredients, and shake to flatten. Trickle the warm butter and cream over the top, followed by the saffron. Scatter with the dried cranberries and the remaining fried onions.
notes: This is a biryani recipe derived from the Dishoom version that's widely shared. I usually make it with chicken thighs, but that can be subbed out for fried paneer or jackfruit for a veggie version. To make it with paneer, just lightly fry the cheese before adding to the marinade. For jackfruit, it's also worth coating with a little e.g. garam masala and frying first, then using in place of the chicken.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Berry Chia Overnight Oats
instructions: Mix oats, chia, milk, and maple syrup in a jar.
Refrigerate overnight.
Top with yogurt and berries before serving.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Berry Crumble

ingredients.text: 6 tbsp, cold and cubed unsalted butter

instructions: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees. No need to thaw the berries — frozen is actually better here because they release their juices gradually as they bake.

Toss the frozen berries with the granulated sugar, cornstarch, and vanilla in a large bowl. The cornstarch is what thickens the juices into a syrupy sauce instead of a watery mess. Spread the berry mixture into a 9x13-inch baking dish or a large cast iron skillet.

In a separate bowl, combine the flour, oats, brown sugar, cinnamon, and salt. Add the cold cubed butter and work it in with your fingers, pinching and squeezing until you get a shaggy, clumpy mixture with pea-sized pieces of butter still visible. Those butter chunks are what make the topping crispy.
Scatter the crumble topping evenly over the berries. Don't pack it down — you want it loose and craggy so it gets golden and crunchy.

Bake for 35-40 minutes, until the topping is deep golden brown and the berry juices are bubbling up around the edges. If the top is browning too fast, tent it loosely with foil for the last 10 minutes.
Let it cool for at least 15 minutes before serving. The juices need time to thicken — if you dig in too early, it'll be soupy.
Serve warm with a generous scoop of Kirkland vanilla ice cream on top.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Berry Protein Pancakes

ingredients.text: 2 cups mix kodiak protein pancake mix

instructions: Mix Kodiak pancake mix, milk, eggs, Greek yogurt, vanilla, and cinnamon in a large bowl. Stir until just combined — lumps are fine and actually preferred. Overmixing makes tough pancakes.
Gently fold in frozen berries. No need to thaw them first; they'll warm through while cooking and create little jammy pockets.
Heat a griddle or large nonstick skillet over medium heat. Add a small pat of butter.
Pour about 1/3 cup batter per pancake. Cook until bubbles form on the surface and the edges look set — about 2–3 minutes.
Flip and cook 1–2 minutes more until golden brown and cooked through.
Serve stacked with extra berries, a dollop of Greek yogurt, and maple syrup.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Berry Smoothie
instructions: Add frozen berries, Greek yogurt, bananas, honey, and milk to a blender.
Blend on high for 60 seconds until smooth and creamy.
If it's too thick, add a splash more milk. Too thin, add a handful of ice or more frozen berries.
Pour into glasses and serve immediately.
Feel virtuous about your life choices for at least 20 minutes.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Beurre Blanc

ingredients.text: Salt and white pepper to taste

instructions: Simmer vinegar, wine, and shallot until reduced to about 1 tbsp.
Reduce heat to low and whisk in cold butter, a few cubes at a time, until fully emulsified.
Remove from heat as soon as the last butter is incorporated.
Season with salt and white pepper.
Strain if a smooth sauce is preferred, and serve immediately.
notes: Delicate French butter sauce for poached or pan-seared fish; keep the heat gentle so it never fully melts to oil.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Biang Biang Noodles
instructions: Knead dough; rest 30 minutes.
Roll and slap into wide belt noodles.
Boil noodles until chewy.
Whisk chili oil, soy, vinegar, and garlic.
Toss noodles with sauce, bok choy, and scallions.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Blue Cheese Dressing
instructions: Mash half the blue cheese into the mayonnaise and sour cream until mostly smooth.
Whisk in buttermilk and vinegar to loosen.
Fold in remaining crumbled blue cheese for texture.
Season with salt and pepper, and chill before serving.
notes: Classic dip for buffalo wings, also great on wedge salads.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Blue Cheese & Gnocchi Bake
instructions: Heat oven to 200°C (fan 180°C / gas 6). Cook the broccoli in boiling water 4-5 minutes until just tender.
Mix the soft cheese, milk and Stilton in a bowl and season well with black pepper.
Lift the broccoli out with a slotted spoon (reserve the water). Cook the gnocchi according to pack instructions in the same pan, then drain.
Put the gnocchi and broccoli in an ovenproof dish. Pour over the cheese mixture and coat everything. Scatter over the Parmesan.
Bake 15-20 minutes until bubbling and golden.
author: Marcus Baw (pacharanero/recipes)

title: Braised red cabbage
instructions: Cut the cabbage into quarters and core it. Shred it using a food processor (or a knife). Peel and slice the onion.

To a large pan add the cabbage and onion, along with the rest of the ingredients. Season and bring to a soft simmer. Cover and cook for about 90 minutes, then remove the lid and cook for a further 30 minutes or so until tender.
notes: I like this with a roast – we quite often have it at Christmas. You need a cabbage that's maybe about 1kg.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Broad Bean Sauce

ingredients.text: Fresh young broad beans , strings removed, sliced 2–3 cm pieces

instructions: Heat olive oil in a wide pan over medium heat; gently fry onion 4–5 minutes until translucent. Add garlic; cook 1 minute.
Add sliced broad beans, coriander, salt, and pepper. Cover and simmer gently 5–8 minutes, stirring occasionally, until beans are tender and mixture forms a loose sauce.
Adjust seasoning. Serve hot over rice, couscous, or pasta; optionally top with a spoon of yogurt.
author: Marcus Baw (pacharanero/recipes)

title: Broccoli Parmesan Soup
instructions: Cook leek in olive oil until soft.
Add potato, broccoli, and stock
simmer until tender.
Blend smooth, then stir in milk and parmesan.
Season generously with pepper.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Brown Rice and Black Bean Bowl
instructions: Cook brown rice.
Warm beans with cumin and salt.
Assemble bowls with rice, beans, corn, and avocado.
Finish with lime juice and cilantro.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Buffalo Chicken Wraps

ingredients.text: 1/3 cup Frank's RedHot or your favorite buffalo sauce
2 cups shredded iceberg or romaine lettuce

instructions: Pull about half the meat off the rotisserie chicken. Use two forks and go with the grain — dark meat from the thighs shreds easiest.
Place the shredded chicken in a medium bowl and toss with the buffalo sauce until everything is evenly coated. Start with 1/4 cup and add more if you like it hot.
Warm the tortillas: stack them between two damp paper towels and microwave for 20-30 seconds. This makes them pliable and less likely to crack.
Lay out a tortilla on a clean surface. Think of it as a blank canvas for spicy art.
Lay down a line of shredded lettuce across the center, leaving about 2 inches on each side.
Add a generous portion of the buffalo chicken on top of the lettuce.
Sprinkle with cheese, add diced celery if using, and lay a few avocado slices across.
Drizzle with ranch dressing. Be generous — the ranch is doing important cooling work here.
Fold in both sides of the tortilla, then roll tightly from the bottom up, tucking the filling in as you go.
Slice in half on a diagonal if you want it to look restaurant-worthy.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Bulgogi Noodle Bowl
instructions: Marinate beef with soy sauce, sugar, and sesame oil 15 minutes.
Stir-fry beef until caramelized.
Boil glass noodles; drain.
Blanch spinach and carrot.
Toss noodles with vegetables and beef; garnish with sesame seeds.
notes: Korean BBQ beef over glass noodles.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Burmese Mohinga (Fish Noodle Soup)
instructions: Simmer fish with lemongrass and turmeric; flake meat.
Thicken broth with rice flour slurry.
Blanch noodles.
Assemble with fish broth, banana stem, and egg.
Top with fritters, fish sauce, and lime.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Burnt Garlic Dal
instructions: Cook toor dal with turmeric until soft and creamy.
Fry garlic slices in oil until deep golden and crisp.
Remove half the garlic; add cumin and chilies to oil.
Pour tempering over dal.
Top with remaining crispy garlic and cilantro.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Butter Bean Tomato Basil Stew
instructions: Cook onion and garlic in olive oil until sweet.
Add tomatoes, butter beans, and chili.
Simmer 15 minutes until thick.
Stir in basil just before serving.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Butternut Squash Soup
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F. Toss the pre-cut butternut squash with olive oil, salt, and pepper on a sheet pan.
Roast for 25–30 minutes until the squash is fork-tender and caramelized on the edges.
While the squash roasts, melt butter in a large pot over medium heat. Sauté the onion for 5 minutes until softened, then add the garlic and cook 1 minute more.
Add the roasted squash and 4 cups of chicken broth to the pot. Bring to a simmer and cook for 5 minutes.
Use an immersion blender (or transfer in batches to a blender) and blend until completely smooth.
Stir in 1/2 cup heavy cream and the nutmeg. Season with additional salt and pepper to taste.
Serve hot, with an extra drizzle of cream on top if you're feeling fancy.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Cabbage and Apple Slaw
instructions: Combine cabbage, apple, and carrot.
Whisk vinegar, oil, honey, and salt.
Toss and rest 10 minutes before serving.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Caesar Dressing
instructions: Mash anchovy and garlic to a paste in a bowl.
Whisk in egg yolk, mustard, and lemon juice.
Slowly drizzle in olive oil while whisking until emulsified.
Stir in Parmesan and black pepper.
Toss with romaine lettuce and croutons immediately.
notes: Restaurant-style dressing for classic Caesar salad, invented in Tijuana in the 1920s.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Calentita (Chickpea Flour Bake)
instructions: Whisk chickpea flour, water, salt, and pepper until smooth. Rest (covered) at least 1 hour, preferably overnight (re-whisk before baking).
Heat oven to 175°C / 350°F. Add a thin layer of olive oil to a 23×15 cm (9×6 in) tin; place in oven to heat. Swirl or brush hot oil up the sides.
Pour batter into hot tin and bake ~55–65 minutes until set in center and lightly golden.
Cool briefly, slice, and serve warm (pepper to finish).
author: Marcus Baw (pacharanero/recipes)

title: Caprese Salad
instructions: Slice the mozzarella and Roma tomatoes into 1/4-inch rounds.
Arrange alternating slices of tomato and mozzarella on a platter, overlapping slightly. Tuck whole basil leaves between the slices.
Drizzle generously with extra-virgin olive oil.
Drizzle balsamic vinegar over the top, or serve it on the side for dipping.
Finish with flaky sea salt and freshly cracked black pepper.
Serve immediately at room temperature for the best flavor.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Carnitas

ingredients.text: Cilantro, diced white onion, and lime wedges for serving

instructions: Preheat oven to 300°F. Pat the pork shoulder dry with paper towels.
Mix the cumin, oregano, smoked paprika, black pepper, and salt in a small bowl. Rub the spice mixture all over the pork shoulder, pressing it into the meat and any crevices.

Place the pork fat-side up in a large Dutch oven or deep roasting pan. Scatter the quartered onion, smashed garlic, bay leaves, and cinnamon stick around the meat. Pour the orange juice, lime juice, and water around (not over) the pork.
Cover tightly with a lid or two layers of aluminum foil. Roast for 3.5–4 hours, until the pork is completely tender and shreds easily with a fork. Internal temperature should be around 200–205°F.
Remove from oven and transfer the pork to a large sheet pan. Discard the bay leaves and cinnamon stick. Reserve the braising liquid.
Using two forks, shred the pork into bite-sized pieces, discarding any large pieces of fat or the bone. Spread the meat out in an even layer on the sheet pan.

Spoon about 1/2 cup of the braising liquid over the shredded pork. Set your oven to broil on high. Place the sheet pan on the upper rack and broil for 4–6 minutes until the edges of the pork get crispy and caramelized. Watch it closely — it can go from perfect to burnt fast.
Remove from the broiler. Squeeze fresh lime juice over the top. Serve on warm tortillas with cilantro, diced onion, salsa, and more lime wedges.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Cauliflower, Potato & Cheddar Soup

ingredients.text: Salt and black pepper, to taste

instructions: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat. Sauté onion ~7 minutes until soft; add garlic for final minute.
Add potatoes, cauliflower, stock (or water), and milk. Bring to a boil; reduce to a gentle simmer, cover, and cook 15 minutes until vegetables are tender.
Blend soup smooth (immersion blender or in batches) and return to pot.
Stir in cheddar, dry mustard, salt, pepper, and nutmeg until cheese melts.
Add cream, warm gently (do not boil). Adjust seasoning and serve.
author: Marcus Baw (pacharanero/recipes)

title: Cauliflower & Stilton Soup

ingredients.text: 1 cauliflower, trimmed and cut into small florets
1 vegetable stock cube, made up to 900 ml

instructions: Mist a large pan with cooking spray and fry the shallots over a medium-high heat 5 minutes until starting to soften. Add the oregano and cook 1 minute.
Add the cauliflower and stock. Cover and bring to the boil, then reduce the heat and simmer 15 minutes until the cauliflower is tender.
Transfer half of the cauliflower to a bowl using a slotted spoon. Add half the Stilton to the soup, then use a stick blender to blitz until smooth. Season to taste.
Return the reserved cauliflower to the soup with most of the parsley. Divide between bowls and scatter over the remaining Stilton and parsley. Serve with the toast.
author: Marcus Baw (pacharanero/recipes)

title: Chana Dal Fry
instructions: Pressure-cook or simmer chana dal with salt until tender but holding shape.
Heat oil; add cumin and onion; cook until browned.
Add ginger-garlic paste and chili powder; cook 1 minute.
Stir in tomato puree and simmer 8 minutes.
Mix dal into masala, finish with garam masala and cilantro.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Chapatis - Flatbreads - Tortillas

ingredients.text: 290 g whole wheat flour, plus more for shaping

instructions: Put the water and salt in a medium saucepan, bring to a rolling boil, and remove from the heat.
Add the flour all at once and stir vigorously with a wooden spoon to integrate.
Cover the pot with a lid and let the mixture sit for 2 minutes to let the flour fully hydrate.
Transfer the flour mixture to the bowl of a stand mixer fitted with a dough hook. Mix on low until the dough is smooth and doesn't stick to your hands when you touch it, about 4 minutes.
Transfer the dough to a lightly floured work surface and knead lightly until the dough is smooth, about a minute.
Roll the dough into a thick rope and use a bench scraper to cut the dough into 12 equal pieces (each should weigh about 57g/2 oz).
Roll each piece into a ball on the work surface. Press each ball into a 2-inch disk.
With a floured rolling pin, roll each disk into a thin round measuring 6 inches in diameter.
Meanwhile, heat a large griddle or cast iron skillet over medium high heat.
Line a basket with a clean kitchen towel.
author: Marcus Baw (pacharanero/recipes)

title: Char Kway Teow
instructions: Stir-fry garlic and shrimp in hot wok.
Push aside; scramble eggs.
Add noodles, dark soy, and fish sauce; toss over high heat.
Fold in bean sprouts and chives.
Serve immediately from the wok.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Chermoula
instructions: Combine cilantro, parsley, garlic, cumin, paprika, and chili flakes in a bowl.
Stir in lemon juice.
Whisk in olive oil until combined.
Let rest 10 minutes before using as a marinade or sauce.
notes: Moroccan herb marinade, classic for grilled or baked fish.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Chicago-Style Italian Beef

ingredients.text: 1 jar Giardiniera, hot or mild, 16 oz — this is non-negotiable
4-5 Pepperoncini peppers + 1/4 cup of their jar juice
3 lbs usda choice beef chuck roast

instructions: Place the chuck roast in the slow cooker fat-side up.
Sprinkle the Italian dressing mix all over the top and sides of the roast.
Tuck the pepperoncini peppers around the roast.
Cover and cook on LOW for 8 hours.
The meat should shred with zero resistance.
Pull the beef out onto a cutting board.
Return the shredded beef to the pot.
Toast the hoagie rolls under the broiler until just golden, about 2 minutes.
Pile the beef generously onto the rolls.
Serve each sandwich with a small bowl of warm jus for dipping.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Chicken and chorizo paella
instructions: Prepare the vegetables - finely chop the onions, crush the garlic, and chop the tomatoes and peppers.
Place the stock in a small pan along with the saffron and bring to a simmer. Remove from the heat and set aside.
Chop the chorizo into chunks, and chop each chicken thigh into 3 pieces
Heat half of the oil over a medium high heat in the paella pan. Salt and pepper the chicken, then fry in batches until golden brown. Remove and set aside.
Turn down the heat, then add the rest of the oil to the pan, followed by the onion and the garlic. Cook gently for about 10 minutes until soft but not coloured.
Add the chorizo and cook for around 5 minutes until soft and broken down. Add the tomatoes and cook for about 3 minutes, until a tick paste is formed.
Add the rice, and stir for about 1 minute until everything is evenly coated.

Pour in the saffron and stock, stir to combine, then return the chicken and any juices to the pan. Turn up the heat a little to medium-low, and then simmer uncovered for about 20 minutes without stirring. When done, the rice should be cooked but not mushy, and the bottom of the pan should be sticky.
Mix the peppers and parsley into the rice, then cover tightly with foil and leave for 5 minutes to warm through.
Meanwhile, mix the mayonnaise, garlic, and lemon juice to make a quick cheat's aioli.
notes: A basic paella recipe with chicken thighs and chorizo, along with a cheat's aioli sauce that's just mayo and garlic. You can also add some prawns to this recipe – fry them with a little garlic after the chicken, set aside, and return them later along with the chicken.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Chicken and Rice Soup
instructions: Simmer chicken in broth with bay leaf until cooked; shred meat.
Sauté onion, carrot, and celery; return to pot.
Add rice and simmer 15 minutes until tender.
Return shredded chicken, season, and serve.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Chicken Burrito Bowls

ingredients.text: Optional: sour cream, hot sauce, sliced jalapenos, diced avocado

instructions: Shred the rotisserie chicken into bite-sized pieces, discarding skin and bones. You should get about 3-4 cups of meat.
Heat the cilantro lime rice according to package directions. If you want to stretch it further, cook your own rice and toss with chopped cilantro and lime juice.
Drain and rinse the black beans. Warm them in a small saucepan with cumin, chili powder, and a pinch of salt for 3-4 minutes.
Microwave or pan-toast the frozen corn until heated through, about 2-3 minutes.
Divide the rice evenly among 6 meal prep containers.
Top each container with shredded chicken, seasoned black beans, corn, and a sprinkle of shredded cheese.
Add a tablespoon of salsa to each container or pack it in a small side cup to keep things from getting soggy.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Chicken fried rice
instructions: First, cook the rice and set aside to cool.
Chop the chicken into small chunks. Heat the vegetable oil in the wok, and add the chicken along with 1tbsp of the soy sauce. Toss regularly until cooked through and golden brown.
Remove the chicken and set aside. Chop the onions, then add the sesame oil to the pan, followed by the onion, peas and carrots. Toss until tender and starting to take on color.
Manoeuver the vegetables to one side of the wok, then beat the eggs together and pour in. Allow the eggs to cook briefly then scramble them; toss through the vegetables once cooked.

Return the chicken to the pan the add the rice on top, along with the rest of the soy sauce. Stir fry for a few minutes until heated through and starting to take on colour. Add the spring onions and combine, then serve.
notes: Useful with leftover rice or chicken. Important is to make sure the rice is cool before cooking – it won't work with freshly-cooked rice and you'll end up with a mushy mess. You can also omit the chicken, or throw in other ingredients like prawns or ham.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Chicken Karahi
instructions: Prepare the ingredients first. Crush the garlic and half of the ginger together into a thick paste, and crush the cumin and coriander seeds.
Strip the leaves from the coriander and set aside. Julienne the other half of the ginger and also set aside.

Heat the oil in a wok over a high heat. Chop the chicken into bite-sized pieces, and once the oil is hot add to the pan along with a large pinch of salt. Cook for a few minutes, stirring frequently, until the chicken is cooked and golden brown.
Add the garlic and ginger paste and stir to combine. Add the tomatoes and cook down for about 5 minutes, breaking the tomatoes up to form the sauce.
Add all of the dry spices and stir to combine. Continue to cook for another 5–10 minutes until the sauce has reduced and is quite thick.
Chop the chillies into three or four parts each and add to the pan, along with the butter. Stir while the butter melts to combine. You should end up with a smooth and glossy sauce.
Taste and add salt and lemon juice to taste. Add the coriander leaves and ginger and stir to combine. Serve immediately with rice or roti.
notes: This is a straightforward and delicious from-scratch recipe that's become my go-to for curry. The recipe is Pakistani in origin, and the sauce is built from a bit of crushed whole tomato. It's really flavourful and doesn't take long to make at all, considering it's from scratch. It's best with roti in my opinion, but rice is also fine.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Chicken katsu curry
instructions: Fill the pan with oil to a depth of about 4cm and place over a low heat to bring up to temperature. We want to fry at about 170℃.
Slice the onion, then place in a saucepan along with a splash of oil. Cook over a medium heat until soft and starting to brown – about 5 minutes.
Add about 400ml water to the onion and bring to the boil. Reduce the heat, cover, and simmer for about 15 minutes.

Meanwhile, prepare the chicken. Start by preparing a breading station – take three large flat bowls, place the cornflour in one, the egg in the next, and the Panko in the third. Mix the salt with the cornflour, then add a tablespoon of oil to the egg and beat.

Butterfly each breast and flatten it out. One at a time, dip each fillet in the cornflour, them remove and shake off the excess. Dip in the egg mixture until covered, then dip in the breadcrumbs, patting them in to ensure an even coat. Place on a plate.

When the oil is up to temperature, place one chicken breast into the plan, ensuring it's covered in oil. Fry for about two minutes on each side – the coating should be a nice, even golden brown. Repeat with the other breast.
Add the curry sauce mix to the onions and stir until combined. Simmer for 5 minutes until thickened.
Cut each fillet into slices, then serve with white rice and the curry sauce poured over.
notes: This is a recipe for a straightforward chicken katsu curry. It uses a ready-made Japanese curry mix – something like S&B Golden Curry Sauce Mix. You can substitute a ready-to-use curry sauce if you prefer. Canola/rapeseed, sunflower, or corn oil work for frying.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Chicken Katsu with Shredded Cabbage
instructions: Pound chicken thin; season.
Bread with flour, egg, and panko.
Shallow-fry until golden and cooked through.
Slice and serve over cabbage.
Drizzle tonkatsu sauce.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Chicken Lettuce Wraps

ingredients.text: 1 can water chestnuts, drained and finely diced
1 head butter lettuce, leaves separated into cups

instructions: Separate the butter lettuce leaves and set them out on a platter. You want the cup-shaped inner leaves — they're nature's perfect taco shell.
Mix the soy sauce, hoisin, sesame oil, rice vinegar, and sriracha in a small bowl. Set this sauce aside.

Heat a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat with a drizzle of olive oil. Add the ground chicken and break it up with a spatula into small crumbles. Cook for 5–6 minutes until browned and no longer pink.
Add the garlic and ginger, stirring constantly for about 30 seconds until the kitchen smells incredible.
Toss in the diced water chestnuts and pour the sauce over everything. Stir well and cook for another 2–3 minutes until the sauce thickens slightly and coats the chicken.
Remove from heat and stir in most of the green onions, saving some for garnish.
Spoon the chicken mixture into the butter lettuce cups. Top with remaining green onions and a sprinkle of sesame seeds.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Chicken Salad Croissants
instructions: Shred the rotisserie chicken into a large bowl. You should get about 3-4 cups of meat.
Add mayo, Dijon mustard, lemon juice, celery, halved grapes, and chopped pecans. Stir until everything is coated.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Slice croissants in half horizontally.
Add a lettuce leaf if using, then pile chicken salad generously onto each croissant.
Accept compliments graciously.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Chicken Satay Noodles
instructions: Marinate chicken with turmeric and coriander; grill on skewers.
Whisk peanut butter with kecap manis and warm water.
Soak rice noodles; drain.
Serve noodles with satay chicken and peanut sauce.
Garnish with cucumber and fried shallots.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Chicken Tikka Masala
instructions: Place chicken thighs in the slow cooker.
In a bowl, combine diced tomatoes, tomato paste, onion, garlic, ginger, garam masala, cumin, turmeric, paprika, cayenne, and salt. Pour over chicken.
Cover and cook on LOW for 6 hours or HIGH for 3 hours.
Remove chicken and shred or cube it, then return to the sauce.
Stir in heavy cream and let it warm through for 10-15 minutes on HIGH.
Cook jasmine rice according to package directions.
Serve tikka masala over rice, garnished with fresh cilantro.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Chicken Wild Rice Soup
instructions: Cook 1 1/2 cups wild rice blend according to package directions. Set aside.
Shred 3–4 cups of meat from the rotisserie chicken. Snack on a piece or two — chef's privilege.
In a large pot or Dutch oven, melt butter over medium heat. Add diced onion, 3 diced carrots, and 3 diced celery stalks. Cook for 6–7 minutes until softened.
Add garlic and cook 1 minute. Sprinkle in the flour and stir constantly for 2 minutes to form a roux.
Slowly pour in 8 cups chicken broth, stirring to prevent lumps. Add thyme, bay leaf, salt, and pepper.
Bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer for 15 minutes.
Stir in the cooked wild rice, shredded chicken, and 1 cup heavy cream. Simmer 5 more minutes until heated through.
Remove the bay leaf, taste for seasoning, and serve.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Chilli Con Carne

ingredients.text: 1 medium red pepper, deseeded and roughly chopped
1 vegetable stock cube, made up to 250 ml with hot water

instructions: Heat a large pan over a medium heat. When hot, spray with cooking spray, add the mince, increase the heat and cook 4-5 minutes, stirring, until lightly browned.
Stir in the onion, garlic and pepper and cook 4-5 minutes until the onion starts to soften.
Add the chilli powder and cumin and cook 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, kidney beans and stock and season. Bring to a simmer, cover and cook 25-30 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Cook the rice according to packet instructions.
Serve the chilli with rice and a spoonful of yogurt.
author: Marcus Baw (pacharanero/recipes)

title: Chimichurri
instructions: Combine parsley, garlic, oregano, and red pepper flakes in a bowl.
Whisk in vinegar, then slowly whisk in olive oil.
Season with salt and pepper.
Let sit 10 minutes before serving to let flavors meld.
notes: Classic Argentine herb sauce for grilled meats.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Chimichurri Rojo
instructions: Combine parsley, garlic, paprika, chili flakes, and oregano in a bowl.
Whisk in vinegar, then slowly whisk in olive oil.
Season with salt and pepper.
Rest 15 minutes so the paprika blooms and flavors combine.
notes: Spicier, smokier cousin of green chimichurri, popular with grilled sausage and beef.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Chinese Black Vinegar Dressing
instructions: Whisk black vinegar, soy sauce, sesame oil, and sugar.
Stir in garlic and scallions.
Use immediately on dumplings or salads.
Adjust sweetness to taste.
Best used fresh.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Chinese Celery and Tofu Salad

ingredients.text: 200 g firm tofu, julienned and pan-fried

instructions: Pan-fry tofu strips until golden; cool.
Blanch celery 30 seconds; cool.
Whisk soy, vinegar, and sesame oil.
Toss celery and tofu with dressing.
Garnish with scallions and sesame seeds.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Chinese Chicken Cucumber Salad
instructions: Shred warm poached chicken.
Salt cucumbers; drain.
Whisk vinegar, soy, and chili oil.
Toss chicken and cucumber with dressing.
Garnish with scallions, cilantro, and sesame.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Chinese Chili Oil (Homemade)
instructions: Heat aromatics in oil until garlic is golden; remove solids.
Pour hot oil over chili flakes and peppercorns.
Stir in salt.
Cool completely.
Store in jar at room temperature 1 month.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Chinese Dry-Fried Green Beans
instructions: Blister green beans in hot oil until wrinkled.
Add garlic and chilies; stir-fry 1 minute.
Add soy sauce, vinegar, and sugar.
Toss until glazed.
Serve hot.
notes: Sichuan gan bian si ji dou.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Chinese Egg Drop Soup
instructions: Bring broth to gentle simmer.
Thicken lightly with cornstarch slurry.
Stir soup in circular motion; drizzle eggs.
Turn off heat; add sesame oil and white pepper.
Garnish with scallions.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Chinese Hot and Sour Soup
instructions: Simmer broth with mushrooms and tofu.
Season with vinegar, soy, and white pepper.
Thicken lightly with cornstarch slurry.
Drizzle beaten eggs in thin stream.
Garnish with scallions.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Chinese Scallion Pancakes
instructions: Knead flour and water into soft dough; rest 20 minutes.
Roll dough thin; brush sesame oil and scatter scallions.
Roll up and coil; flatten again.
Pan-fry in oil until golden and flaky.
Cut into wedges.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Chinese Smashed Cucumber Salad
instructions: Smash cucumbers with rolling pin; cut into chunks.
Salt lightly; rest 10 minutes; drain.
Whisk soy sauce, black vinegar, and chili oil.
Toss cucumbers with garlic and dressing.
Garnish with scallions and cilantro.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Chinese Steamed Eggplant with Garlic
instructions: Steam eggplant slices 10 minutes until tender.
Mix soy sauce, vinegar, and chili oil.
Top eggplant with raw minced garlic.
Pour hot sauce over to mellow garlic.
Garnish with scallions and cilantro.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Chinese Sweet Soy Dressing
instructions: Whisk all ingredients until smooth.
Warm gently to dissolve sugar.
Cool before use.
Drizzle on cold noodles or salads.
Store refrigerated 1 week.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Chinese Tea Eggs
instructions: Hard-boil eggs; crack shells gently all over.
Simmer soy, spices, tea, and water.
Add eggs; simmer 30 minutes.
Steep off heat 1 hour.
Peel to reveal marble pattern.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Chinese Tomato Egg Noodles
instructions: Scramble eggs in oil; set aside.
Cook tomatoes and garlic until saucy.
Add ketchup, sugar, and splash of water.
Toss cooked noodles in tomato sauce.
Fold in eggs and scallions.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Chinese Wood Ear Mushroom Salad
instructions: Rehydrate wood ear; blanch 2 minutes; slice.
Toss with cucumber.
Whisk vinegar, soy, and chili oil.
Add garlic and dressing.
Garnish with cilantro.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Chipotle Mayo
instructions: Combine all ingredients in a bowl.
Stir until smooth and evenly colored.
Taste and add more chipotle for extra heat.
Chill before serving.
notes: Smoky, spicy mayo for tacos, burgers, and fries.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Chocolate and crisp tart
instructions: Preheat the oven to 160℃, and grease the flan tin with a little butter.

Crush the crisps into the texture of coarse breadcrumbs in a food processor. Melt 100g of the butter in a small saucepan, then add the golden syrup. Combine the crisps and melted butter mixture in a large bowl and mix thoroughly.

Press the crisp and butter mixture into the flan tin, making sure to fill all of the flutes and keep an even thickness. Cover the top with baking paper and fill with the baking beans, then place on an oven tray and bake for about 10 minutes. Remove from the oven, take out the paper and beans, then set to one side.

While the case is baking, prepare the filling – melt the remaining 250g of butter and the chocolate in a double-boiler, stirring gently until the chocolate has melted completely and is combined with the butter. Remove from the heat and let cool a little.

Whisk together the eggs, additional yolks, and the caster sugar in a large bowl. Keep beating the mixture until it starts to thicken, which might take a couple of minutes. Pour over the melted chocolate mixture and mix until it's completely combined, then add half of the peanuts.

Pour the chocolate mixture into the prepared case, then sprinkle over the remaining peanuts. Bake for around 20-25 minutes until the filling is set, with a slight wobble in the middle. Remove the tin from the oven and place on a wire rack to cool. Once it's cooled a little, place in the fridge to chill for about 4 hours.
Carefully remove the tart from the tin, and serve – in very small slices!
notes: This is based on an Nadiya Hussain recipe, and it's amazing. It's a basic rich chocolate tart, but with a base made from crushed-up ready-salted crisps.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Chorizo (Dry Cured) – 5 kg Batch

ingredients.text: 8 g potassium nitrate OR 12 g Prague Powder #1

instructions: Trim meat of tendons; cut into 2 cm cubes. Chill thoroughly (near-freezing) 12 hours or partially freeze until stiff.
Dissolve salt, curing salt (or adjusted nitrate), and spices in cold water (or add dry) then combine evenly with cubed meat.
Grind through 5–6 mm plate. Mix thoroughly until tacky and uniform.
Stuff loosely into prepared casings forming 50 cm rings; avoid overpacking to prevent smearing.
Hang sausages to drain 20–30 minutes refrigerated.
Pre-dry (étuvage) at ≤25°C (77°F) with airflow for ~6 hours to shrink casings.
Dry/cure at 12–15°C (54–59°F), 70–80% RH, with gentle airflow for 12–18 days, rotating for even drying.
Optional: Rub lightly with olive oil for sheen; avoid surface mold development typical of other styles.
Store wrapped in refrigerator several weeks; slice thinly to serve.
author: Marcus Baw (pacharanero/recipes)

title: Choucroute Garnie à l'Alsacienne

ingredients.text: 100ml - vegetable oil, lard, or goose/duck fat

instructions: Up to a day in advance, season the pork loin and shoulder (if using) with salt and leave uncovered in the fridge.

Chop the onion into thin slices. Make a small spice parcel by lightly crushing the garlic cloves and placing on the cheesecloth along with the juniper berries, cloves, caraway and bay leaves, then tying into a small parcel.

Preheat the oven to 120℃. Place two thirds of the oil in a casserole or dutch oven, then place over a medium heat. Add the onions and cook until soft and barely starting to brown – less than ten minutes.
Add the spice parcel along with the wile and stock to the onions. Add the pork shoulder/bacon/pork belly/ham hock as appropriate and nestle it down in the liquid.
Cut a disk out of baking paper that's large enough to sit on top of the ingredients in the pan, then set it directly on top of the contents. Place in the oven and cook for around 90 minutes.
Meanwhile, prepare the pork loin by placing on a separate rack in the oven, until cooked through – the time taken will depend on the size and shape. Once cooked, set aside.
Prepare the salt pork, if using, by boiling gently for about an hour, then transferring to the braising pan in the oven.
Peel and halve the potatoes, then boil in salted water until tender. Drain and set aside.

Prepare the sauerkraut by draining and squeezing out any excess moisture. When the braising pan has been cooking for 90 minutes, add the sauerkraut and mix it all around a little. Re-cover with the baking paper, then return to the oven. Increase the temperature of the oven to 150℃ and leave for about 1 hour.
Prepare the sausages by simmering in boiling water for about 10 minutes.
notes: Alsatian choucroute garnie is the best way to eat cabbage. Make your own sauerkraut if possible – it's a big improvement on the varieties you can easily buy. You can use a variety of different meats, depending on what's available – the goal is to cook with whatever you can get. I've added the specific ones I normally use but you can mix it up depending on what's available, but this is just a general guide! The idea is to independently cook each variety of meat as best suited and add it to the braising pan when it's ready.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Citrus Fennel Quinoa Salad
instructions: Cook quinoa until tender and cool slightly.
Whisk olive oil and lemon juice with a pinch of salt.
Toss quinoa, fennel, orange, spinach, and almonds with dressing.
Finish with feta and extra black pepper.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Classic BBQ Sauce
instructions: Combine all ingredients in a saucepan.
Bring to a simmer over medium heat.
Reduce heat and simmer 15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thickened.
Cool before using; keeps refrigerated for two weeks.
notes: All-American sweet, smoky, tangy sauce for ribs, pulled pork, and grilled chicken.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Classic Chicken Chow Mein
instructions: Boil egg noodles 3 minutes; rinse and drain.
Stir-fry chicken in oil until cooked; set aside.
Stir-fry carrot and garlic 2 minutes.
Return chicken with noodles, oyster sauce, and soy sauce.
Toss in bean sprouts and scallions; serve immediately.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Classic Chicken Noodle Soup
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add onion, carrots, and celery. Cook for 5 minutes until the vegetables start to soften.
Add garlic, thyme, and rosemary. Stir for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Pour in the chicken broth. Add bay leaves, salt, and pepper. Bring to a boil.
Add egg noodles and cook for 8-10 minutes until the noodles are tender.
Stir in the shredded rotisserie chicken and cook 2-3 minutes more until heated through.
Remove bay leaves. Stir in fresh parsley and a squeeze of lemon juice if using. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Ladle into bowls and serve with crusty bread, because that's the law.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Classic Hummus
instructions: Blend chickpeas, tahini, garlic, lemon juice, cumin, and salt until smooth.
Stream in olive oil and water to reach a creamy texture.
Adjust seasoning and serve with vegetables or pita.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Classic Smash Burgers

ingredients.text: 8 buns brioche buns or kirkland hamburger buns

instructions: Divide the beef into 8 equal balls, about 4 oz each. Gently shape them — do NOT overwork the meat. Nobody likes a tough burger.
Mix Worcestershire sauce into the beef before forming balls if you want a little extra savory depth. Totally optional but recommended.
Heat your grill or cast iron skillet to high. You want it ripping hot. If you're using a grill, a flat cast iron griddle on the grates works beautifully.
Place a ball on the cooking surface and immediately smash it flat with a sturdy spatula. Press hard, press once, then leave it alone.
Season the top aggressively with salt and pepper while the bottom develops a deep, dark crust — about 2–3 minutes.
Flip each patty. Immediately lay a slice of cheddar on top. Cook 1–2 minutes more. The cheese should be melty and slightly droopy by the time it's done.
While the cheese melts, toast your buns cut-side down on the grill for about 30 seconds. Watch them — they go from golden to charcoal in a blink.
Assemble: bottom bun, patty with cheese, pickles, onion, lettuce, tomato, ketchup, mustard, top bun. Or however you like — we're not the burger police.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Classic Steak Sauce
instructions: Combine all ingredients in a small saucepan.
Whisk together over low heat until sugar dissolves.
Simmer 8 minutes, stirring occasionally, until slightly thickened.
Cool and store in a jar refrigerated.
notes: Tangy, savory-sweet bottled-style steak sauce, best made a day ahead so flavors meld.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Cocktail Sauce
instructions: Combine all ingredients in a bowl.
Stir until smooth.
Taste and adjust horseradish or hot sauce for heat.
Chill at least 30 minutes before serving.
notes: Classic American dip for shrimp cocktail and oysters.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Coconut and lime chicken
instructions: Chop the chicken breasts into bite-sized pieces. Zest and juice the lime, then combine with the chicken in a large bowl. Set aside and leave to marinade for a couple of hours (or use it straight away if you prefer – it's not that big a deal!)
When you're ready, prepare the rest of the ingredients. Chop the coriander leaves, and slice the spring onions into 3cm shreds.
Heat the oil in a wok, then add the chicken. toss for 3-4 minutes until cooked and golden brown.
Add the chilli and toss for another minute or so, then add the coconut milk, fish sauce, and half of the coriander and spring onions.
Cook for a couple of minutes then serve over some jasmine rice, with the rest of the spring onions and coriander on top.
notes: I have been making this recipe for years. It's kind of a simplified Thai-style curry that I think was originally a Delia recipe. I usually serve it with Thai jasmine rice cooked wth some coconut milk.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Coconut Curry Noodles
instructions: Soak rice noodles until tender; drain.
Fry curry paste in coconut oil 1 minute.
Add coconut milk and soy sauce; simmer 5 minutes.
Add vegetables; cook 3 minutes.
Toss noodles with curry sauce and basil; serve with lime.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Coconut Curry Shrimp

ingredients.text: 1 tsp brown sugar or palm sugar

instructions: Thaw shrimp if frozen: place in a colander under cool running water for 5 minutes. Peel if needed, pat dry with paper towels.
Start your jasmine rice according to package directions (or use a rice cooker).
Heat oil in a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat. Add the curry paste and stir for 30 seconds until fragrant and slightly darkened.
Pour in the coconut milk and stir to dissolve the curry paste. Add the fish sauce and brown sugar. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Add the sliced bell peppers (and zucchini if using). Cook for 3 minutes until the peppers are just tender but still have some snap.
Add the shrimp and garlic in a single layer. Cook for 2–3 minutes per side until the shrimp are pink and curled. Do not overcook.
Remove from heat. Squeeze in the lime juice, scatter the basil leaves on top, and stir gently. The basil will wilt into the sauce.
Serve immediately over steamed jasmine rice. Garnish with green onions and red pepper flakes if you like heat.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Coconut Moong Dal
instructions: Simmer moong dal with turmeric and water until soft.
Stir in coconut milk and simmer 8 minutes.
Temper mustard seeds, curry leaves, and chili in coconut oil.
Pour over dal.
Serve with appam or rice.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Cod with Tomato Olive Braise
instructions: Sauté onion and garlic in oil.
Add tomatoes, olives, capers, and simmer 10 minutes.
Nestle cod into the sauce and cook gently until flaky.
Finish with parsley.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Cold Brew Concentrate

ingredients.text: Milk, cream, or sweetener of choice for serving

instructions: Add coarsely ground coffee to a large jar, pitcher, or French press.
Pour in cold filtered water. Stir gently to make sure all grounds are saturated.
Cover and place in the refrigerator.
Steep for 12-24 hours. Longer = stronger, but anything over 24 hours can get bitter.
Strain through a fine-mesh sieve lined with cheesecloth, a coffee filter, or just use the French press plunger.
Transfer the concentrate to a clean jar or bottle.
To serve, dilute 1:1 with cold water or milk over ice. Adjust the ratio to your caffeine personality.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Cold Sesame Noodles
instructions: Cook noodles; rinse under cold water and drain.
Whisk sesame paste with soy sauce, vinegar, and chili oil.
Toss noodles with sauce until coated.
Top with cucumber and scallions.
Sprinkle sesame seeds before serving.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Cornbread
instructions: Preheat the oven to 220℃. Melt the butter over a low heat or in the microwave.
In a medium bowl, combine the flour, masa harina, salt and backing powder. Separately, whisk together the milk, maple syrup, and eggs.
Whisk two thirds of the melted butter into the liquid ingredients, reserving one third.
Pour the liquid into the dry ingredients, and stir gently to combine just until everything is wet – don't over-mix.
Add the reserved butter to the baking dish and ensure it's covered, then crape in the batter. Spread with a spatula.
At this point, you can add any toppings – then place in the oven for 20–25 minutes. cook until a toothpick poked into the middle comes out clean.
notes: A sweet cornbread recipe which is a good accompaniment to things like chilli or pulled pork. It can also be eaten with plenty of maple syrup and butter. Jamie Oliver's Barbecoa restaurant used to serve a "Devil's Cornbread" dish that was similar to this, but with the addition of lots of melted cheese, herbs, and nduja. You can recreate this by adding about 200g of grated cheddar and mozzarella, some chopped parsley and a bit of nduja to the top of the cornbread immediately before putting it in the oven. Some chopped jalepeños also work well.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Courgette and Arborio Rice Soup
instructions: In a large saucepan heat olive oil over medium-low heat; cook onion and garlic until softened but not browned (≈8 minutes).
Add diced courgettes, salt, pepper, and nutmeg; increase heat to medium and cook, stirring, until courgette is barely tender (≈10 minutes).
Stir in tomatoes, broth, rice, parsley, and basil. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a gentle simmer.
Simmer until rice is tender (≈20 minutes). Adjust seasoning.
Serve hot (or at room temperature) with grated Parmesan. Soup will thicken on standing; loosen with a little stock or water if reheating.
author: Marcus Baw (pacharanero/recipes)

title: Cranberry Sauce
instructions: Combine cranberries, sugar, orange juice, and zest in a saucepan.
Add cinnamon stick if using.
Simmer 12 minutes, stirring occasionally, until cranberries burst and sauce thickens.
Remove cinnamon stick and cool before serving.
notes: Holiday classic for roast turkey, keeps refrigerated for over a week.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Creamy mushroom soup
instructions: Place the porcini mushrooms in a small bowl and cover with boiling water. Set to one side and leave to soak.
Wash the mushrooms and chop into bite-size chunks. Peel and finely chop the onion and garlic.
Heat a large pan with the olive oil and butter, then add the onion, garlic, and thyme leaves. Cook for about 5-7 minutes until the onion just starts to brown, then tip in the mushrooms.

Remove the porcini from the soaking water and add to the pan. Also add the water they were soaking in – pass it through a sieve or a muslin first, as it may contain some grit from the mushrooms. Cook uncovered, stirring occasionally, for about 20 minutes or until the liquid has disappeared and the mushrooms are starting to brown.
Add the stock, then bring to the boil and reduce to a gentle simmer.

Use a stick blender to purée the soup just a little bit. Don't overdo it – you aren't going for mushy mushrooms here, and you still want plenty of texture. Leave for 30 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add the double cream along with the zest and juice of the lemon. Stir to combine, then season to taste and serve – ideally with a swirl of cream and a sprinkle of thyme on top.
notes: This is a wonderful, creamy mushroom soup that's perfect for autumn and winter. Use a mixture of whatever mushrooms you can find – basically, you can't go wrong, and more mushrooms means more flavour! This recipe is vegetarian-friendly if using vegetable stock. Substitute the double cream for a plant-based alternative if you want to make it vegan-friendly too.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Creamy Mushroom & Spinach Pasta

ingredients.text: 1/2 vegetable stock cube, made up to 150 ml

instructions: Lightly mist a deep frying pan with cooking spray and cook the onion over a medium heat for 4-5 minutes until softened. Add the garlic, season well with salt and black pepper, then cook 1 minute.
Add the mushrooms with a splash of water and turn the heat up slightly. Cook 4-5 minutes, stirring often, until golden.
Reduce the heat, add the soft cheese and stir until it melts. Pour in the stock, season with black pepper and cook 8-10 minutes until slightly thickened.
Cook the pasta according to pack instructions. Drain well and stir through the spinach to wilt.
Toss the sauce with the pasta and serve.
author: Marcus Baw (pacharanero/recipes)

title: Creamy Spinach-Stuffed Chicken with Courgette
instructions: Heat oven to 200°C (fan 180°C / gas 6). Pour boiling water over the spinach in a colander to wilt. Cool, squeeze dry and roughly chop.
Mix the soft cheese, Parmesan, mustard and garlic with black pepper and a pinch of salt. Stir in the spinach.
Cut a pocket into the side of each chicken breast and stuff each with a quarter of the mixture.
Peel the courgettes lengthways into wide ribbons. Wrap 10-12 ribbons around each chicken breast, overlapping and tucking underneath.
Put on a lined roasting tray, mist with cooking spray and season. Bake 5 minutes.
Add the cherry tomatoes around the chicken, mist and season, then bake 20 minutes until cooked through.
Serve with rocket drizzled with balsamic vinegar.
author: Marcus Baw (pacharanero/recipes)

title: Creamy Tomato Basil Soup
instructions: Heat olive oil and butter in a large pot over medium heat. Add the diced onion and cook for 5 minutes until softened and translucent.
Add garlic and red pepper flakes, stirring for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in both cans of diced tomatoes (with their juice) and 2 cups chicken broth. Add sugar, salt, and pepper.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer uncovered for 15 minutes.
Remove from heat. Add a generous handful of fresh basil leaves (about 1/2 cup packed).
Blend until smooth using an immersion blender or regular blender (vent the lid!).
Return to low heat. Stir in 3/4 cup heavy cream and warm through for 2–3 minutes.
Taste, adjust seasoning, and serve with a few torn basil leaves on top.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Creamy Tomato White Bean Soup
instructions: Cook onion and garlic in oil until soft.
Add tomatoes, beans, stock, and paprika.
Simmer 15 minutes.
Blend half the soup for body, then return to the pot.
notes: Serve with basil and olive oil.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Crispy Chicken Quinoa Tabouli
instructions: Cook quinoa and let it cool slightly.
Pan-sear chicken until crisp and cooked through.
Mix quinoa with tomato, cucumber, parsley, lemon juice, and olive oil.
Slice chicken and serve over the salad.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Crispy Chickpea Shawarma Bowls
instructions: Roast chickpeas with oil and spices until crisp.
Serve over rice with cucumber yogurt and salad.
Finish with lemon and herbs.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Crispy Smashed Potatoes with Yogurt
instructions: Boil potatoes until tender.
Smash on a tray, drizzle with oil, and roast at 220°C until crisp.
Mix yogurt with garlic and dill.
Serve potatoes with the yogurt spooned underneath.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Cuban Mojo Marinade

ingredients.text: 1/2 cup sour orange juice (or orange + lime juice)

instructions: Whisk citrus juice with garlic, oregano, and cumin.
Slowly whisk in olive oil to emulsify.
Season with salt and pepper.
Use to marinate pork or chicken at least 2 hours before cooking.
notes: Classic Cuban citrus-garlic marinade, also good warmed and poured over roast pork as a sauce.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Cucumber Mint Buttermilk Cooler
instructions: Blend everything until pale green and foamy.
Pour over ice if desired.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Cumberland Sauce
instructions: Melt redcurrant jelly in a small saucepan over low heat.
Stir in orange and lemon zest and juice.
Add port, mustard, and ginger, and simmer 5 minutes.
Cool to room temperature before serving.
notes: Traditional English accompaniment for cold meats, game, and pâté.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Curry Goat (Serves 5–6)

ingredients.text: 3 large tomatoes, skinned and roughly chopped
1–2 Scotch bonnet chillies, deseeded and finely chopped

instructions: Make curry blend: dry-roast coriander seeds, peppercorns, cardamom pods, fenugreek seeds, and cinnamon stick in a dry pan 1–2 minutes until fragrant; grind. Mix with ground ginger and turmeric.
Cut meat into chunky pieces (2–3 cm). Trim only excess hard fat.
In a large bowl combine 2 level tbsp of the curry blend with tomatoes, garlic, onions, chillies, thyme leaves (stripped and bruised), chopped coriander roots/stalks, and optional HP sauce.
Add meat; massage marinade thoroughly into all surfaces. Cover and refrigerate at least 6 hours (overnight preferred).
Remove meat; shake off loose marinade solids (reserve them). Brown meat in clarified butter in batches; transfer to a heavy casserole.
Fry reserved marinade solids until onions soften. Add to casserole. Deglaze pan with a splash of water; add juices to pot. Add just enough water to cover meat lightly and 1 tsp salt (adjust later).
Bring to a gentle simmer (or very low oven 120°C / 250°F). Cook 2.5–3 hours until meat tender and sauce thickened. Add small amounts of water if drying.
Adjust seasoning; sprinkle with chopped coriander leaves. Serve with plain rice, fried plantain, and chutneys.
author: Marcus Baw (pacharanero/recipes)

title: Dal Baati Tadka (Dal Only)
instructions: Simmer all dals with salt until thick and creamy.
Heat ghee; sauté onion until golden.
Add tomatoes and spices; cook 8 minutes.
Combine with dal and simmer 12 minutes.
Finish with cilantro.
notes: Rajasthani mixed dal traditionally served with baati.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Dal Dhokli
instructions: Simmer toor dal with turmeric until soft; add tamarind.
Knead flour with water and pinch of salt into stiff dough; roll and cut into diamonds.
Drop dhokli into simmering dal; cook 12 minutes.
Temper mustard seeds and curry leaves in oil.
Pour over dal, garnish with cilantro.
notes: Gujarati wheat dumplings in lentil broth.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Dal Fry Restaurant Style
instructions: Cook both dals until smooth.
Sauté onion in butter until browned.
Add ginger-garlic and tomato puree; cook 10 minutes.
Add garam masala and kasuri methi.
Simmer with dal 12 minutes until thick.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Dal Makhani (Light)
instructions: Soak urad dal and kidney beans overnight; simmer until very soft, about 40 minutes.
Sauté onion in butter until golden.
Add ginger-garlic paste and garam masala; cook 2 minutes.
Add tomatoes and simmer 10 minutes.
Stir in dal, mash lightly, simmer 15 minutes, finish with kasuri methi.
notes: Creamy Punjabi dal with less cream.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Dal Palak
instructions: Simmer toor dal with turmeric until soft.
Sauté cumin, onion, and green chilies in oil.
Add spinach and cook until wilted.
Stir spinach mixture into dal and simmer 8 minutes.
Finish with lemon juice and salt.
notes: Classic spinach dal from North India.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Dal Tadka
instructions: Rinse lentils and simmer with turmeric and water until soft, about 25 minutes.
Sauté onion, ginger, and garlic in oil until golden.
Add tomatoes and cook until broken down.
Stir tempered aromatics into lentils and simmer 5 minutes.
Garnish with cilantro and serve with rice.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Dan Dan Noodles
instructions: Cook noodles until al dente; drain and divide into bowls.
Brown pork with garlic in oil until crisp.
Whisk sesame paste, soy sauce, vinegar, and chili oil with 3 tbsp noodle water.
Spoon sauce over noodles; top with pork and scallions.
Finish with ground Sichuan pepper.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Dark Chocolate Chia Pudding
instructions: Whisk chia, milk, cocoa, and maple syrup.
Rest 10 minutes, whisk again, then chill for 4 hours.
Top with grated dark chocolate.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Doenjang Jjigae (Korean Soybean Paste Stew)
instructions: Dissolve doenjang in water in pot.
Add potato, onion, and garlic; simmer 10 minutes.
Add zucchini and tofu.
Simmer 8 minutes.
Finish with chili and scallions.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Dry Cured Sausage (Basic Ratio)

ingredients.text: Splash wine or liquor for marinade
Pinch curing salt – follow safety guidelines

instructions: Marinate lean meats in wine 12 hours chilled (optional for flavour).
Mince chilled lean meats through medium plate; dice fat small.
Combine meats with seasoning thoroughly until tacky.
Stuff into natural casings; tie links or coils loosely.
Hang at ≤21°C (70°F) for initial drain, then dry/cure in cool environment (12–15°C / 54–59°F) with airflow until firm and reduced in weight (several months). White surface mould is normal.
author: Marcus Baw (pacharanero/recipes)

title: Dumplings
instructions: Preheat the oven to 190°C (375°F / gas 5).
Put the flour into a mixing bowl.
Using a coarse grater, grate the cold butter into the flour.
Add a pinch of salt and pepper.
Using your fingers, gently rub the butter into the flour until it resembles breadcrumbs.
Add a splash of cold water to bind it into a dough.
Divide the dough into 24 pieces and gently roll each into a round dumpling.

Place the dumplings on top of your fully cooked stew and press down lightly so they are half submerged. If the stew looks dry, add a cup of boiling water and stir, as the dumplings absorb a lot of moisture.
Cook in the oven, or on the hob over a medium heat with the lid on, for 30 minutes.
author: Marcus Baw (pacharanero/recipes)

title: Edamame and Corn Salad
instructions: Blanch edamame and corn 3 minutes; cool.
Combine with diced bell pepper.
Whisk vinegar, sesame oil, and soy sauce.
Toss salad with dressing.
Chill and garnish with scallions.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Egg Fried Noodles
instructions: Cook noodles; drain.
Scramble eggs in a hot wok; set aside.
Stir-fry vegetables, then add noodles and soy sauce.
Return eggs; finish with sesame oil and spring onions.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Egg Muffin Cups

ingredients.text: Cooking spray or olive oil for greasing

instructions: Preheat your oven to 375°F (190°C). Spray a 12-cup muffin tin generously with cooking spray -- don't skip this or the eggs will stick like cement.
Dice the bell peppers into small pieces, about 1/4 inch.
Divide the diced ham, bell peppers, and shredded cheese evenly among the 12 muffin cups, filling each about halfway.
Crack the eggs into a large bowl or measuring cup with a pour spout. Add the milk, garlic powder, onion powder, salt, and pepper. Whisk until smooth and well combined.
Pour the egg mixture evenly over the fillings in each cup, filling to about 3/4 full. Give each cup a gentle stir with a fork to distribute everything.
Bake for 18-22 minutes until the tops are set and slightly golden. A toothpick inserted in the center should come out clean.
Let cool in the pan for 5 minutes, then run a butter knife around the edges and pop them out.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)
