title: Estonian Kringle
instructions: In a mixing bowl, combine the yeast with the sugar and milk, and stir until combined. Add the egg yolk and melted butter.

In another, large bowl, mix the flour and salt, then pour over the milk mixture. Mix together, then start kneading until it pulls together. Shape the dough into a ball, then place into a clean, oiled bowl to rest. Leave for 1 hour in a warm place, until roughly doubled in size.
While rising, mix the softened butter with the sugar and cinnamon, then set to one side.
Preheat the oven to 200℃. Line a large baking sheet with baking paper. On a floured surface, roll the dough to a rectangle about 45cm x 30cm.

Spread the cinnamon filling evenly over the top of the dough, reserving a tablespoon for later. Leave a 1-2cm area clear around the edges. Sprinkle over the ground almonds, then roll the doll into a spiral tube with the filling on the inside.

Slice the rolled dough in half lengthwise, leaving about 1-2cm uncut at one end so that the dough forms a "V" shape. Braid the two legs together, keeping the layers exposed to the top. Pinch the ends together and wrap underneath to form a wreath shape.

Transfer the bread to the prepared baking sheet. Brush with the remaining cinnamon filling, then bake for 20-25 minutes until golden brown. For the last 10 minutes reduce the oven temperature to 180℃. Remove from the oven and cool on a wire rack.
notes: This is a cinnamon-roll style loaf that looks and smells amazing.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Fat Knackers (Stuffed Steak Rolls)
instructions: Slowly cook onions in olive oil over low-medium heat until deeply caramelised; midway add brown sugar and red wine vinegar; cook to a jammy consistency. Cool slightly.
Lay out tenderised steaks; season lightly with salt and pepper. Place a tablespoon of onion mixture near one end; roll up and secure with cocktail sticks.
Grill over medium-high heat (or barbecue) turning until browned and cooked through (≈6–8 minutes) OR bake covered at 180°C / 350°F for 30–40 minutes with a splash of red wine.
Rest briefly; serve hot (also good cold next day).
author: Marcus Baw (pacharanero/recipes)

title: Filipino Atchara (Pickled Papaya)
instructions: Salt papaya and carrot 30 minutes; rinse.
Simmer vinegar, sugar, and salt until dissolved.
Pack vegetables with ginger and garlic in jar.
Pour hot brine over.
Refrigerate 24 hours before serving.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Filipino Calamansi Vinaigrette
instructions: Whisk calamansi juice with vinegar and honey.
Stream in olive oil while whisking.
Add shallot, salt, and pepper.
Rest 10 minutes.
Bright dressing for tropical salads.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Filipino Chicken Adobo
instructions: Combine chicken, soy sauce, vinegar, garlic, bay leaves, and peppercorns.
Simmer covered 30 minutes.
Uncover and reduce sauce until glossy.
Serve over steamed rice.
Spoon pan sauce over chicken.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Filipino Ensaladang Talong
instructions: Grill eggplants until charred; peel and mash lightly.
Combine tomatoes and onion.
Toss with vinegar, salt, and chili.
Mix in eggplant.
Serve at room temperature.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Filipino Pancit Bihon
instructions: Soak bihon until soft.
Stir-fry chicken and garlic.
Add vegetables; cook 3 minutes.
Toss noodles with soy sauce and splash of water.
Finish with calamansi juice.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Flour tortillas
instructions: Combine the flour, salt and baking powder in a mixing bowl. Add the coconut oil and combine using your fingers until the mixture resembled fine breadcrumbs. At the point, it should kind of stick together and hold its form when pressed. Add the water and mix until the dough pulls together into a cohesive ball.

Place the dough on a lightly floured work surface and knead for a few minutes until it becomes smooth and elastic. Divide into 24 equal pieces and roll each into a ball. Leave to sit for around 10 minutes for the gluten to develop.
Use a well-floured rolling pin and a well-floured surface to flatten each tortilla into a flat, round disk. It needs to be pretty thin – maybe the thickness of a 2p coin.

Place a large skillet over a medium-high heat and place each tortilla in turn on the skillet, cooking until bubbly and golden. Flip and continue cooking until golden on both sides. For extra taste and texture, fire each tortilla briefly over a naked flame.
notes: This is an unconventional flour tortilla recipe that that uses coconut oil instead of lard, and it actually works pretty well.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: French Toast Casserole
instructions: Butter a 9x13-inch baking dish generously.
Tear croissants into rough 1.5-inch chunks. Scatter them evenly in the baking dish — it's fine to pile them up a bit.
Whisk together eggs, heavy cream, milk, brown sugar, vanilla, cinnamon, nutmeg, and salt until smooth.
Pour the custard mixture evenly over the croissant pieces. Press the chunks down gently with a spatula so they soak up the liquid.
Cover tightly with plastic wrap and refrigerate overnight (or at least 4 hours).
In the morning: preheat oven to 350°F. Remove the casserole from the fridge and let it sit at room temperature while the oven heats.
Bake uncovered for 40–45 minutes until the top is golden brown, puffed up, and the center is set (not jiggly).
Let cool 5 minutes. Dust with powdered sugar if you're feeling fancy. Serve with a generous pour of Kirkland maple syrup.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Fried mac and cheese bites
instructions: Place mac and cheese into the refrigerator until firm, about 4 hours.
Heat vegetable oil in a large, deep pan over a medium high heat.
Using a small ice cream scoop or similar, roll macaroni and cheese into 4cm-ish balls, forming about 12.
Working one at a time, dip balls into eggs, then dredge in Panko, pressing to coat.
Working in batches, add balls to the oil and cook until evenly golden and crispy, about 3-4 minutes. Transfer to a paper towel-lined plate. Sprinkle with chopped chives to serve.
notes: Kind of like arancini, but with mac and cheese.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Gai Lan with Oyster Sauce
instructions: Blanch gai lan in boiling water 2 minutes; drain.
Heat oil; sauté garlic 30 seconds.
Add oyster sauce, sugar, and water.
Simmer sauce 1 minute.
Pour over gai lan and serve.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Garlic Chili Oil Noodles
instructions: Cook noodles; drain, reserving 2 tbsp water.
Heat oil; fry garlic and chili flakes until fragrant.
Mix soy sauce, vinegar, and noodle water.
Toss noodles with chili oil and sauce.
Garnish with scallions and cilantro.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Garlic Dal (Lehsun Dal)
instructions: Simmer moong dal with turmeric until creamy.
Heat ghee; add cumin, chilies, and garlic.
Cook garlic until fragrant, not burnt.
Pour over dal and simmer 5 minutes.
Serve hot with rice or roti.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Garlic Green Beans with Almonds
instructions: Blanch beans until crisp-tender.
Sauté garlic in olive oil and add almonds.
Toss beans in the pan and finish with lemon zest.
notes: A classic side for fish or chicken.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Garlic Yogurt Chicken Traybake
instructions: Mix yogurt, garlic, cumin, salt, and pepper.
Coat chicken and marinate while the oven heats.
Roast chicken, potatoes, and onion at 210°C for 35 minutes.
Rest 5 minutes before serving.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Gazpacho Soup

ingredients.text: ¼ mild chilli pepper, seeds removed
50 g day-old white bread, crusts removed, soaked then squeezed dry

instructions: Prepare vegetables: skin tomatoes (if using for garnish) and set aside; seed peppers; peel cucumber portion; dice garnish vegetables and reserve chilled.
Soak bread 30 minutes in cold water; squeeze dry.
In a blender combine peppers, cucumber, garlic, coriander leaves, chilli, soaked bread, onion, vinegar, olive oil, and iced water; blend until roughly but uniformly chopped (retain some texture).
Season with salt and black pepper; chill well. Add a few ice cubes if serving immediately.
Fry diced bread for croutons in a little olive oil until golden (if using).
Serve soup cold with separate bowls of diced tomato, pepper, cucumber, and croutons for topping.
author: Marcus Baw (pacharanero/recipes)

title: Ginger Scallion Poached Chicken
instructions: Poach chicken gently in stock with sliced ginger until cooked through.
Shred chicken and toss with spring onion and sesame oil.
Reduce a little of the broth for spooning over.
Serve over warm rice.
notes: Add steamed greens on the side.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Glass Noodle Stir Fry
instructions: Soak glass noodles 10 minutes.
Pan-fry tofu until golden.
Stir-fry garlic and bok choy 3 minutes.
Add noodles, soy sauce, and vegetarian oyster sauce.
Toss with tofu and white pepper.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Gochujang Sauce
instructions: Whisk gochujang, soy sauce, and rice vinegar together until smooth.
Stir in honey, sesame oil, and garlic.
Simmer 3 minutes in a small pan if a glossier, thicker sauce is wanted.
Cool before serving or brushing on grilled meat.
notes: Sticky, spicy Korean sauce for bibimbap, bulgogi, or as a glaze on grilled meat.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Golden Carrot Ginger Soup
instructions: Sauté onion, garlic, and ginger in oil until fragrant.
Add carrots and stock; simmer for 20 minutes until soft.
Blend smooth and stir in coconut milk.
Season with salt, pepper, and lemon zest.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Greek Lemon Chicken Soup
instructions: Poach chicken in broth until cooked; shred and return to pot.
Cook orzo in the broth until tender.
Whisk eggs with lemon juice.
Temper eggs with hot broth, then stir back into soup off heat.
Season and serve.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Greek Style Moussaka

ingredients.text: 4 medium aubergines, sliced into 1 cm rounds

instructions: Heat oven to 200°C (fan 180°C / gas 6). Lay aubergine slices on baking trays, season, mist with cooking spray and bake 15-20 minutes until golden and nearly dried out.
Mist a frying pan with cooking spray and sauté the onions and garlic 5 minutes, adding a little water if they stick. Add the mince and stir to break up and brown.
Add the Worcestershire sauce, tomatoes, cinnamon, parsley and seasoning. Bring to the boil, then simmer, uncovered, 20 minutes until thick.
Beat together the fromage frais, quark, mustard and egg.
Layer the aubergines with the mince mixture in an ovenproof dish. Pour over the cheese sauce.
Bake 45 minutes until bubbling and golden.
author: Marcus Baw (pacharanero/recipes)

title: Green Curry Tofu and Vegetables
instructions: Brown tofu cubes in oil.
Add curry paste and cook 1 minute.
Stir in coconut milk and vegetables.
Simmer until vegetables are crisp-tender and serve with rice.
notes: A squeeze of lime wakes it up.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Green Goddess Chicken Salad
instructions: Blend yogurt, avocado, herbs, lemon juice, salt, and a splash of water into a creamy dressing.
Arrange lettuce, chicken, and cucumber on a platter.
Spoon over dressing and serve chilled.
notes: Great in wraps the next day.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Green Goddess Dressing
instructions: Combine all ingredients in a blender or food processor.
Blend until smooth and vibrant green.
Thin with a splash of water if too thick.
Season with salt and chill before serving.
notes: San Francisco classic from the 1920s, named for a hit play of the same era.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Green Kiwi Spinach Smoothie
instructions: Peel the kiwis.
Blend all ingredients until silky smooth.
Serve immediately.
notes: Use frozen banana for extra chill.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Green Moong Dal
instructions: Soak green moong 2 hours; simmer with turmeric and salt until tender.
Heat oil; toast cumin seeds.
Sauté onion until golden; add coriander powder.
Combine with dal and simmer 10 minutes.
Garnish with cilantro.
notes: Whole mung bean dal with more texture.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Grilled Chicken and Vegetable Skewers
instructions: Marinate chicken and vegetables with oil and spices.
Thread onto skewers.
Grill 10-12 minutes, turning, until chicken is cooked.
Serve with lemon wedges.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Guacamole
instructions: Mash avocados in a bowl to your preferred texture.
Fold in onion, tomato, jalapeño, and cilantro.
Add lime juice and salt, and mix well.
Taste and adjust seasoning before serving.
notes: Best served immediately, or with a lime-covered pit pressed in to slow browning if not eating right away.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Gujarati Makai Sabji
instructions: Bring a large pan of water to the boil. Remove any husk from the corn, then split the cobs in half lengthwise. Add the corn to the water and boil for about 8 minutes or until tender. Drain and set aside.
Crush the peanuts to a fine powder in a food processor (or by hand, if you need to)

Heat the oil into a large frying pan until medium hot, then add the flour. Stir vigorously to smooth out any lumps and prevent it from burning. After 3-4 minutes it will turn a reddish-brown; when this happens, turn the heat to a minimum and stir in the peanuts. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring frequently.
Add the yoghurt, salt, turmeric, chilli powder, sugar, and juice of the lemon to the pan. Mix to a thick paste, then slowly start adding 600ml of water, stirring continuously to form a smooth sauce.

Place the cooked corn in the pan, cover and leave to on a low heat for about 10 minutes. Transfer to individual bowls, and scatter with the chilli flakes and some extra lightly-crushed peanuts, if you like.
notes: This corn-on-the-cob curry doesn't use tomatoes, onions or cream, but cooked nuts mean it has a lovely deep flavour.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Gyro Bowls

ingredients.text: Fresh dill or parsley for garnish

instructions: Cook rice according to package directions and fluff with a fork.
Dice the cucumber, tomatoes, and thinly slice the red onion.
Heat a skillet over medium-high heat with olive oil. Cook the gyro meat slices for 2-3 minutes per side until warmed through and slightly crispy on the edges.
Divide rice among 6 bowls. Top with gyro meat, tomatoes, cucumber, red onion, and crumbled feta.
Drizzle tzatziki over each bowl and season with salt and pepper.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Hakka Noodles
instructions: Boil hakka noodles; rinse cold.
Stir-fry vegetables in oil over high heat.
Add noodles, soy sauce, and vinegar.
Toss 3 minutes until smoky.
Season with white pepper and scallions.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Ham Béchamel Croquettes

ingredients.text: 30 g finely grated Manchego or Parmesan

instructions: Infuse Milk (Optional but recommended): Place milk, bay leaf and diced onion in a saucepan. Bring just to a simmer, switch off heat, cover and steep 10 minutes. Remove bay. (Strain out onion if you want an ultra-smooth interior; otherwise leave the very fine dice.)
Make Roux: Melt butter over medium heat in a wide heavy saucepan. Stir in flour and cook 2–3 minutes, stirring, until it smells toasty but not browned.

Build Béchamel: Off the heat, add about 1/4 of the milk and whisk vigorously until smooth. Return to gentle heat and add the rest in 3–4 additions, whisking each fully lump‑free before the next. Cook 4–6 minutes, stirring with a spatula, until thick, glossy and slow to fall from the spoon (thicker than a sauce; it should hold a line when you drag the spatula).
Season & Enrich: Fold in ham, cheese (if using), nutmeg, pepper and most of the salt (reserve a little, taste and adjust). The mixture should be savoury but not aggressively salty.

Chill Firm: Spread the mixture 1.5–2 cm thick in a shallow tray (lined with baking paper or lightly oiled). Press cling film directly on the surface to prevent a skin. Chill at least 3 hours (overnight best) until fully set.
Shape: Flour your hands. Cut slab into bars or scoop portions (about 30 g). Roll into cylinders or ovals. If mixture softens, return pieces to the fridge briefly.

Crumb Coat: Arrange three shallow dishes: seasoned flour, beaten eggs, breadcrumbs. Dredge each croquette in flour (shake excess), dip in egg, then breadcrumbs. For an extra crisp shell, rest 5 minutes and repeat egg + breadcrumb step (double coating).

Fry: Heat oil to 180°C. Fry in small batches (don’t crowd) 2–3 minutes until deep golden. Turn gently for even colour. Remove with a spider to paper towel. Keep batches warm in a low oven (100°C) if needed.
Serve: Sprinkle with parsley, add a squeeze of lemon if desired, and serve hot while the centre is creamy.
author: Marcus Baw (pacharanero/recipes)

title: Harissa

ingredients.text: 6 dried red chiles, stemmed and seeded

instructions: Soak dried chiles in hot water 15 minutes until softened, then drain.
Toast cumin, coriander, and caraway in a dry pan 1 minute until fragrant.
Blend chiles, garlic, toasted spices, and lemon juice into a paste.
Stir in olive oil and season with salt.
notes: North African chili paste, used as a condiment or stirred into stews and marinades.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Harissa Roasted Vegetable Couscous
instructions: Toss chopped vegetables with olive oil and harissa.
Roast at 220°C until tender and charred.
Prepare couscous with hot water and fluff.
Fold through vegetables and mint.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Herb Roasted Salmon with Asparagus
instructions: Place salmon and asparagus on a tray.
Mix oil, lemon zest, dill, garlic, salt, and pepper.
Brush over salmon and asparagus.
Roast at 200°C for 14-16 minutes.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Hoisin-glazed Tuna with Asparagus & Rice Noodles
instructions: Prepare the rice noodles according to pack instructions, then refresh under cold running water. Drain and toss with the coriander, vinegar and soy sauce. Set aside.

Mist the asparagus and tuna with cooking spray and season with a pinch of salt. Cook on a heated pan about 4 minutes, turning the asparagus occasionally and the tuna once, until the asparagus is tender and the tuna is medium-rare.
Brush each side of the tuna with 1/4 tsp hoisin sauce and cook for a few seconds each side until glazed.
Slice the tuna, drizzle with the remaining hoisin sauce and sprinkle over the sesame seeds. Serve with the asparagus and noodles.
author: Marcus Baw (pacharanero/recipes)

title: Hollandaise Sauce

ingredients.text: Salt and cayenne pepper to taste

instructions: Whisk egg yolks with water and lemon juice in a heatproof bowl over simmering water.
Whisk constantly until pale and thickened, about 3 minutes.
Remove from heat and slowly drizzle in melted butter, whisking constantly until emulsified.
Season with salt and a pinch of cayenne.
Serve immediately while warm.
notes: Classic French emulsion for eggs Benedict and steamed asparagus; does not hold or reheat well.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Homemade Tofu
instructions: Combine water and lemon juice (coagulant). Heat soymilk in a large pot to 71°C / 160°F, stirring to prevent scorching (or bring just to a boil then cool slightly 2–3 minutes while stirring).
Off heat, stir in half the coagulant 1–2 minutes. Stop stirring; add remaining coagulant and gently stir in a figure-eight until curds begin forming.
Cover pot; let stand 10–15 minutes until separation complete. Liquid (whey) should be yellowish-clear; add a few drops more lemon juice only if still milky.
Line a colander or steaming basket with several layers of cheesecloth over a bowl. Ladle curds into cloth.
Gather cloth; drain excess liquid. Shape curds into a loaf; press with a board and ~1 kg (2–3 lb) weight for 30–60 minutes (longer press = firmer tofu).
Unwrap and place tofu block in very cold water to firm further. Use immediately or store submerged in water (change daily) up to 1 week; can freeze for different texture.
author: Marcus Baw (pacharanero/recipes)

title: Honey Garlic Pork

ingredients.text: 1 tbsp Sriracha or red chili flakes

instructions: Place the pork shoulder in the slow cooker fat-side up.
In a small bowl, whisk together the honey, soy sauce, minced garlic, ketchup, and sriracha.
Cover and cook on LOW for 8 hours or HIGH for 4 hours.
Carefully remove the pork to a cutting board.
Return the shredded pork to the slow cooker.
In a small cup, mix the cornstarch and cold water into a smooth slurry.
Cook on HIGH with the lid off for 15 more minutes.
Give it one final stir and let it sit with the lid on for 10 minutes.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Honey Mustard
instructions: Whisk mustard and honey together until smooth.
Stir in mayonnaise and vinegar.
Season with a pinch of salt.
Chill before serving as a dip or dressing.
notes: Sweet-tangy dip for chicken tenders, pretzels, and salads alike.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Horse Gram Dal (Kollu)
instructions: Soak horse gram 4 hours; pressure-cook or simmer until tender.
Heat coconut oil; pop mustard seeds and curry leaves.
Sauté onion and garlic until soft.
Add cooked dal and turmeric; simmer 15 minutes.
Season and serve with rice.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Horseradish Cream
instructions: Whip cream to soft peaks.
Fold in horseradish, mustard, and vinegar.
Season with salt and pepper.
Chill at least 15 minutes before serving.
notes: Classic English accompaniment for roast beef.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Huli Huli Chicken
instructions: In a bowl, mix the pineapple juice, brown sugar, ketchup, soy sauce, ginger, and garlic. Reserve half of the marinade in a separate bowl and set aside.
Chop the chicken thighs into thirds, then add to the remaining marinade. Cover and refrigerate for 30 minutes.

Heat a cast iron pan or wok over a medium heat, and add the oil. Add the chicken to the pan and cook for 7–8 minutes until cooked through, adding about half of the reserved marinade while cooking. The chicken should be sticky and golden brown, and the sauce should be starting to thicken.
Remove from the heat and serve with the remaining reserved marinade.
notes: I use this Hawaiian-style chicken for tacos, usually with a pineapple salsa made with fresh pineapple, coriander, tomatoes, and lime juice.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Hungarian Beef Goulash

ingredients.text: ½ green bell pepper, deseeded & crushed or finely chopped
450 g beef chuck or shank, cubed
¼ tsp hot pepper flakes or cayenne
800 g canned tomatoes, crushed by hand

instructions: Heat oil in heavy casserole. Add onions and bell pepper; cover and sweat until translucent (do not brown). Add garlic; cook 1 minute.
Add beef; season lightly with salt; cover and sweat several minutes until exterior is no longer raw.
Add paprika, black pepper, hot pepper, caraway, and bay leaves; cook gently 10–15 minutes so meat absorbs spices.
Add crushed tomatoes; bring to a gentle simmer. Cover and cook, stirring occasionally, until meat is tender (~1 hour). Adjust seasoning; remove bay leaves.
Serve with buttered egg noodles (optional).
author: Marcus Baw (pacharanero/recipes)

title: Hyderabadi Khatti Dal
instructions: Simmer toor dal with turmeric until soft.
Add tomatoes and tamarind; cook 10 minutes.
Temper mustard seeds, curry leaves, and chilies in oil.
Pour over dal.
Adjust sourness and salt.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Indian Aloo Gobi
instructions: Par-cook potatoes in salted water.
Toast cumin seeds in oil; add turmeric.
Add cauliflower and potatoes; cook 10 minutes.
Add tomatoes and coriander powder; simmer 8 minutes.
Garnish with cilantro.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Indian Cucumber Raita
instructions: Grate cucumber and squeeze out excess water.
Whisk yogurt until smooth.
Fold in cucumber, cumin, mint, and chaat masala.
Season with salt.
Chill 15 minutes before serving with dal or curry.
notes: Cooling yogurt side for spicy meals.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Indian Jeera Rice
instructions: Rinse rice and soak 15 minutes.
Toast cumin in ghee until fragrant.
Add rice, bay leaves, water, and salt.
Simmer covered 15 minutes.
Rest 5 minutes and fluff.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Indian Kachumber Salad
instructions: Dice cucumber, tomato, and onion uniformly.
Toss with lemon juice and chaat masala.
Season with salt.
Fold in cilantro.
Serve immediately with dal or curry.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Indian Mint Chutney Dressing
instructions: Blend mint, cilantro, chili, lime, and water.
Toast and grind cumin; stir in.
Season with salt.
Thin to dressing consistency.
Use on salads and grilled proteins.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Indonesian Bakmi Goreng
instructions: Boil bakmi briefly; drain.
Stir-fry chicken until cooked.
Add noodles, kecap manis, and oyster sauce.
Wok-fry over high heat 3 minutes.
Serve with pak choi, shallots, and pickles.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Indonesian Gado Gado Salad

ingredients.text: Peanut sauce (4 tbsp peanut butter, 2 tbsp kecap manis, lime)

instructions: Blanch all vegetables separately.
Pan-fry tofu until golden.
Whisk peanut butter, kecap manis, and lime into sauce.
Arrange vegetables and tofu on platter.
Drizzle peanut sauce; serve with krupuk.
notes: Indonesian vegetable salad with peanut dressing.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Indonesian Mie Goreng
instructions: Boil noodles; drain well.
Scramble eggs in wok; set aside.
Stir-fry chicken and garlic until cooked.
Add cabbage, noodles, kecap manis, and sambal; toss 3 minutes.
Top with scrambled egg and fried shallots.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Indonesian Peanut Sauce
instructions: Whisk peanut butter with warm water until smooth.
Add kecap manis, lime, sambal, and garlic.
Simmer gently 5 minutes.
Cool to room temperature.
Thin with water if needed.
notes: Rich peanut dressing for gado gado.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Indonesian Tempeh Stir Fry (Tempe Orek)
instructions: Pan-fry tempeh until golden and crisp.
Sauté shallots, garlic, and lime leaves.
Add kecap manis and sambal.
Toss tempeh in glaze until sticky.
Serve with rice.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Italian Wedding Soup

ingredients.text: 1/4 cup grated parmesan, plus extra for serving
1/2 cup orzo or acini di pepe pasta
Squeeze of fresh lemon juice for finishing

instructions: In a medium bowl, combine the ground meat, breadcrumbs, 1 egg, grated parmesan, Italian seasoning, and a generous pinch of salt and pepper.
Mix gently with your hands — overworking the mixture makes tough, dense meatballs and nobody invited those to the wedding.
Roll the mixture into 1-inch meatballs. You should get about 30-35 tiny beauties. Yes, it's tedious. Put on a podcast or rope in a helper.

Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Sauté the onion, carrots, celery, and garlic for 5-6 minutes until the vegetables start to soften and smell like someone's Italian grandmother's kitchen.
Pour in the chicken broth and bring to a steady simmer. Add red pepper flakes if using.
Carefully drop the meatballs into the simmering broth one at a time. Don't stir for the first 3 minutes — let them set on the outside before gently swirling the pot.
Cook the meatballs for 10 minutes total until cooked through and bobbing at the surface.
Add the orzo or acini di pepe and cook for another 8-10 minutes until the pasta is tender. The pasta will keep absorbing broth, so don't worry if it looks a little soupy at this stage.
Stir in the baby spinach handfuls at a time and let it wilt, about 1-2 minutes.
Beat the remaining egg in a small bowl. Slowly drizzle it into the soup in a thin stream while stirring in a circular motion. This creates those gorgeous wispy egg ribbons floating through the broth.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Japanese Avocado and Crab Salad

ingredients.text: 150 g imitation crab or real crab

instructions: Cube avocado and toss with lemon juice.
Shred crab and dice cucumber.
Fold gently with Japanese mayo.
Chill 10 minutes.
Serve topped with tobiko or sesame seeds.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Japanese Chawanmushi
instructions: Whisk eggs with dashi, soy, and mirin; strain.
Divide chicken, mushrooms, and ginkgo into cups.
Pour egg mixture through sieve.
Steam covered on low 15 minutes.
Garnish with mitsuba.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Japanese Daikon and Carrot Salad
instructions: Salt daikon and carrot; rest 15 minutes; rinse.
Dissolve sugar and salt in vinegar.
Toss vegetables with vinegar dressing.
Chill 30 minutes.
Garnish with chili threads.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Japanese Goma Dressing
instructions: Grind half the sesame seeds.
Blend tahini, vinegar, soy, mirin, and ginger.
Thin with water to pourable consistency.
Stir in remaining sesame seeds.
Refrigerate up to 1 week.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Japanese Goma Wakame Salad
instructions: Soak wakame in water 5 minutes; drain and squeeze.
Grind half the sesame seeds.
Whisk soy sauce, vinegar, sesame oil, and ginger.
Toss wakame with dressing and ground sesame.
Top with whole sesame seeds.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Japanese Gyoza (Pan-Fried)
instructions: Mix pork, cabbage, soy, ginger, and garlic.
Fill wrappers and pleat edges.
Pan-fry in oil until golden on bottom.
Add water and cover; steam 5 minutes.
Uncover and crisp bottoms again.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Japanese Gyudon (Beef Bowl)
instructions: Simmer onion in dashi, soy, mirin, and sugar.
Add beef; cook 3 minutes.
Serve over rice.
Top with onsen egg and pickled ginger.
Drizzle remaining sauce.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Japanese Hijiki Seaweed Salad
instructions: Rehydrate hijiki; drain.
Simmer hijiki, carrot, and aburaage with soy and mirin 10 minutes.
Cool to room temperature.
Toss with sesame oil.
Sprinkle sesame seeds.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Japanese Kake Udon (Clear Broth)
instructions: Heat mentsuyu broth.
Blanch udon in boiling water 2 minutes.
Place udon in bowls.
Ladle hot broth over.
Garnish with scallions, shichimi, and daikon.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Japanese Kitsune Udon
instructions: Simmer aburaage in dashi, soy, and mirin 5 minutes.
Blanch udon in boiling water.
Place udon in bowls.
Ladle hot broth and tofu on top.
Garnish with scallions and shichimi.
notes: Sweet fox udon with fried tofu.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Japanese Mazesoba
instructions: Cook ramen; drain well.
Brown pork with soy sauce and mirin.
Place noodles in bowl with minimal tare sauce.
Top with pork, egg, menma, nori, and scallions.
Toss at the table before eating.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Japanese Miso Soup with Tofu and Wakame
instructions: Heat dashi to just below boiling.
Rehydrate wakame in warm water.
Dissolve miso in ladle of dashi; stir into pot.
Add tofu and wakame; heat gently.
Serve with scallions.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Japanese Nasu Dengaku (Miso Eggplant)
instructions: Score eggplant halves and pan-sear until tender.
Whisk miso, mirin, and sugar.
Broil eggplant with miso glaze 3 minutes.
Drizzle sesame oil.
Garnish with sesame seeds and scallions.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Japanese Ozoni (New Year Mochi Soup)
instructions: Simmer dashi with soy and mirin.
Poach chicken and root vegetables.
Grill or toast mochi until puffed.
Place mochi in bowls.
Ladle soup over with vegetables and yuzu zest.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Japanese Ponzu Sauce
instructions: Warm soy sauce, citrus, mirin, and vinegar.
Steep kombu and bonito 10 minutes.
Strain and cool.
Bottle and refrigerate.
Use within 1 week.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Japanese Potato Salad (Light)
instructions: Boil potatoes until tender; cube while warm.
Blanch carrot briefly.
Salt cucumber; drain excess water.
Mix mayo, vinegar, and mustard.
Fold vegetables together; season with pepper.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Japanese Salmon Shioyaki
instructions: Salt salmon generously; rest 20 minutes.
Pat dry and grill or pan-sear skin-side down.
Cook until medium inside.
Serve with grated daikon and lemon.
Pair with rice.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Japanese Sunomono Cucumber Salad
instructions: Salt cucumbers; rest 10 minutes; squeeze dry.
Rehydrate wakame in warm water.
Dissolve sugar and salt in rice vinegar.
Toss cucumbers and wakame with vinegar.
Chill and garnish with sesame seeds.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Japanese Tsukemono (Quick Pickles)
instructions: Salt vegetables 10 minutes; squeeze.
Toss with vinegar, sugar, and kombu.
Rest 20 minutes.
Serve chilled.
Light palate-cleansing pickles.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Japanese Wafu Dressing
instructions: Grate onion and squeeze out excess liquid.
Whisk soy, oil, vinegar, sugar, and onion.
Season with white pepper.
Rest 15 minutes.
Classic Japanese Western-style dressing.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Japanese Yuzu Kosho Dressing
instructions: Whisk yuzu kosho with vinegar and soy.
Stream in olive oil.
Sweeten lightly with honey.
Use sparingly; very aromatic.
Excellent on seafood salads.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Khichdi with Moong Dal
instructions: Rinse rice and dal together.
Heat ghee; add cumin and ginger.
Add rice, dal, turmeric, water, and salt.
Simmer covered on low 25 minutes until soft and porridge-like.
Rest 5 minutes, fluff, and garnish with cilantro.
notes: Comfort one-pot rice and lentil dish.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Kimchi Jjigae
instructions: Sauté pork and kimchi 5 minutes.
Add broth and gochugaru; simmer 15 minutes.
Add tofu cubes.
Simmer 5 more minutes.
Garnish with scallions.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Kimchi Udon Stir Fry
instructions: Blanch udon; drain.
Stir-fry kimchi in oil 2 minutes.
Add udon, kimchi juice, gochujang, and soy sauce.
Toss over high heat 3 minutes.
Finish with sesame oil and scallions.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Korean Bean Sprout Salad (Kongnamul Muchim)
instructions: Blanch sprouts 3 minutes; drain well.
Mix garlic, soy sauce, sesame oil, and gochugaru.
Toss warm sprouts with seasoning.
Garnish with scallions and sesame seeds.
Serve warm or chilled.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Korean Bibim Guksu
instructions: Cook somen; rinse cold.
Whisk gochujang, vinegar, sesame oil, and sugar.
Toss noodles with spicy sauce.
Top with cucumber, kimchi, and egg.
Sprinkle sesame seeds.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Korean Bibimbap
instructions: Blanch and season each vegetable separately.
Stir-fry beef with soy sauce.
Fry egg sunny-side up.
Arrange rice with vegetables and beef.
Serve with gochujang and sesame oil.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Korean Cucumber Salad (Oi Muchim)
instructions: Salt cucumbers lightly; rest 10 minutes; drain.
Mix gochugaru, vinegar, sesame oil, sugar, and garlic.
Toss cucumbers with spicy dressing.
Chill 15 minutes.
Sprinkle sesame seeds before serving.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Korean Dak Galbi
instructions: Marinate chicken with gochujang, gochugaru, soy, and sugar.
Stir-fry chicken over high heat.
Add cabbage, sweet potato, and rice cakes.
Cook until vegetables tender.
Serve wrapped in perilla leaves.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Korean Dubu Jorim (Braised Tofu)
instructions: Pan-fry tofu until golden.
Simmer with soy, gochugaru, maple syrup, garlic, and onion.
Reduce until sauce glazes tofu.
Garnish with scallions and sesame.
Serve with rice.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Korean Gamja Jorim (Braised Potatoes)
instructions: Par-boil potatoes 5 minutes.
Simmer with soy sauce, maple syrup, garlic, and splash of water.
Reduce until glaze coats potatoes.
Drizzle sesame oil.
Garnish with scallions and sesame seeds.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Korean Gochujang Vinaigrette
instructions: Whisk gochujang with vinegar until smooth.
Add sesame oil, soy sauce, sugar, and garlic.
Emulsify with fork or blender.
Rest 10 minutes.
Store refrigerated 1 week.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Korean Japchae
instructions: Boil glass noodles 6 minutes; drain and cut.
Blanch spinach; squeeze dry.
Stir-fry carrot and mushrooms until tender.
Toss noodles with soy sauce, sugar, garlic, and sesame oil.
Combine vegetables and noodles; garnish with sesame seeds.
notes: Celebratory Korean sweet potato noodle dish.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Korean Japchae Banchan (Small Batch)
instructions: Boil noodles; cut into short lengths.
Blanch spinach; squeeze dry.
Stir-fry carrot briefly.
Toss everything with soy, sesame oil, and sugar.
Garnish with sesame seeds.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Korean Jjajangmyeon
instructions: Dice vegetables and blanch potato briefly.
Fry pork in oil; add chunjang and sugar.
Add vegetables and 300 ml water; simmer 15 minutes.
Thicken with cornstarch slurry.
Serve sauce over boiled noodles.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Korean Pan-Fried Tofu (Dubu Jorim Prep)
instructions: Pat tofu dry; pan-fry until golden both sides.
Mix soy sauce, sesame oil, and gochugaru.
Brush sauce on tofu slices.
Simmer 2 minutes until glazed.
Garnish with scallions and sesame seeds.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Korean Radish Salad (Mu Saengchae)
instructions: Julienne radish into matchsticks.
Massage with salt 10 minutes; drain.
Mix gochugaru, vinegar, sugar, fish sauce, and garlic.
Toss radish with spicy dressing.
Garnish with scallions; serve chilled.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Korean Seasoned Spinach (Sigeumchi Namul)
instructions: Blanch spinach 30 seconds; squeeze dry.
Toss with soy, sesame oil, and garlic.
Season lightly with salt.
Form into small mounds.
Sprinkle sesame seeds.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Korean Sesame Soy Dressing
instructions: Whisk soy sauce, vinegar, sesame oil, and sugar.
Add minced garlic.
Sprinkle sesame seeds before serving.
Use on blanched vegetables.
Store refrigerated 5 days.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Korean Spinach Side Salad (Sigeumchi Namul)
instructions: Blanch spinach 30 seconds; plunge in ice water.
Squeeze spinach dry thoroughly.
Mix garlic, soy sauce, sesame oil, and salt.
Toss spinach with seasoning.
Sprinkle sesame seeds.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Kung Pao Chicken (Light)
instructions: Stir-fry chicken until cooked; set aside.
Fry chilies, peppercorns, ginger, and garlic.
Return chicken with soy, vinegar, and sugar.
Toss in peanuts and scallions.
Serve immediately.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Lanzhou Beef Noodle Soup

ingredients.text: 400 g hand-pulled or fresh wheat noodles

instructions: Simmer beef shank with spices and daikon 2 hours until tender.
Slice beef thin.
Boil noodles separately.
Ladle clear spiced broth over noodles.
Top with beef, cilantro, and chili oil.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Lemon Chicken Orzo Soup
instructions: Sauté onion, carrots, and celery in oil.
Add stock and bring to a simmer.
Cook orzo until tender, then add chicken.
Finish with lemon juice, zest, and parsley.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Lemon Coriander Dal
instructions: Simmer masoor dal with turmeric and salt until creamy.
Heat oil; toast cumin and dried chilies.
Pour tempering over dal.
Stir in lemon juice and most of the coriander.
Serve garnished with remaining coriander.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Lemongrass Tofu Rice Noodles
instructions: Pan-fry tofu until golden.
Stir-fry lemongrass; add soy sauce and maple syrup.
Coat tofu in lemongrass glaze.
Soak rice noodles; drain.
Serve with sprouts, cilantro, and peanuts.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Lentil and Vegetable Soup
instructions: Sauté onion, carrot, and celery in oil for 8 minutes.
Add lentils, tomatoes, broth, thyme, and bay leaves.
Simmer 30 minutes until lentils are tender.
Season and serve with crusty bread.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Lentil Miso Soup
instructions: Simmer lentils with carrot and ginger in broth until soft.
Partially blend for creamy texture.
Whisk miso in ladle of broth; stir in.
Heat gently without boiling.
Top with scallions and nori.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Light Miso Ramen Broth Bowl
instructions: Simmer dashi; whisk in miso off boil.
Cook ramen noodles separately.
Place noodles in bowls.
Ladle miso broth over.
Top with egg, corn, nori, scallions, and bamboo.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Maa Ki Dal (Slow Black Dal)
instructions: Simmer urad dal with salt until very soft, about 45 minutes.
Sauté onion in butter until caramelized.
Add ginger-garlic and tomatoes; cook 10 minutes.
Combine with dal and simmer 20 minutes.
Finish with garam masala and a swirl of cream.
notes: Creamy black dal without heavy cream.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Malaysian Ayam Goreng Berempah
instructions: Blend spices, garlic, ginger, and lemongrass into paste.
Marinate chicken 1 hour.
Simmer chicken in coconut milk until tender.
Pan-fry or bake until skin crisps.
Garnish with fried shallots.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Malaysian Hokkien Mee
instructions: Stir-fry pork and garlic until browned.
Add both noodles and dark soy; toss 2 minutes.
Pour in stock; simmer until absorbed and caramelized.
Add shrimp and cabbage; cook 3 minutes.
Serve with lime and sambal.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Malaysian Laksa Lemak Noodles
instructions: Fry laksa paste in a little oil 2 minutes.
Add coconut milk; simmer 10 minutes.
Poach shrimp in broth.
Blanch rice noodles.
Assemble bowls with broth, noodles, sprouts, fish cake, and laksa leaves.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Malaysian Rojak Buah
instructions: Cut all fruit into bite cubes.
Whisk tamarind, palm sugar, and rojak sauce.
Toss fruit gently with dressing.
Plate and scatter peanuts.
Top with torch ginger if available.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Malaysian Roti Canai (Simple Pan Version)
instructions: Knead flour, water, salt, and 1 tbsp ghee into smooth dough.
Rest 30 minutes.
Divide and stretch into thin rounds.
Fold into squares.
Pan-fry in ghee until golden and flaky.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Malaysian Sambal Dressing
instructions: Dissolve palm sugar in warm water.
Whisk in sambal, lime, and soy.
Add minced shallot.
Rest 10 minutes.
Spicy dressing for noodle salads.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Mango Lassi
instructions: Add frozen mango chunks, Greek yogurt, milk, honey, and cardamom to a blender.
Blend on high until smooth and frothy, about 60 seconds.
Taste and adjust sweetness -- ripe mangoes may need less honey.
Pour into glasses. If feeling traditional, sprinkle a tiny pinch of cardamom on top.
Close your eyes, take a sip, and pretend you're somewhere tropical.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Mango Salsa
instructions: Combine mango, red onion, bell pepper, and jalapeño in a bowl.
Stir in cilantro and lime juice.
Season with salt and toss gently.
Chill 10 minutes before serving.
notes: Sweet-and-spicy salsa that pairs well with grilled fish or pork.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Mango Turmeric Lassi
instructions: Blend mango, yogurt, milk, turmeric, honey, and ice until frothy.
Pour into cold glasses.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Mapo Tofu (Light)
instructions: Brown pork with doubanjiang and garlic.
Add broth and gently simmer tofu 5 minutes.
Thicken with cornstarch slurry.
Dust with Sichuan pepper powder.
Garnish with scallions.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Marinara Sauce
instructions: Warm olive oil in a saucepan and sauté garlic until fragrant, 1 minute.
Add crushed tomatoes, oregano, and red pepper flakes.
Simmer 20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until slightly thickened.
Stir in basil leaves and season with salt.
Use immediately or cool and refrigerate.
notes: Simple Italian tomato sauce, the base for countless pasta dishes and pizzas.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Masoor Dal with Spinach
instructions: Simmer rinsed masoor dal with turmeric and water until creamy, about 20 minutes.
Heat oil; toast cumin seeds.
Sauté onion until soft; add tomatoes and coriander powder.
Fold in spinach until wilted.
Combine with dal, season, and serve with lemon.
notes: Protein-rich red lentil dal with greens.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Mediterranean Baked Fish
instructions: Sauté onion in olive oil until soft.
Add tomatoes, olives, and oregano; simmer 10 minutes.
Nestle fish into sauce.
Bake at 190°C for 15 minutes until fish is cooked.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Mediterranean Chickpea Salad
instructions: Halve tomatoes and dice cucumber.
Mix chickpeas, tomatoes, cucumber, olives, and onion.
Dress with olive oil, vinegar, oregano, salt, and pepper.
Rest 10 minutes before serving.
notes: Fold in herbs like mint or parsley.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Mee Siam (Tangy Rice Vermicelli)
instructions: Soak vermicelli; drain.
Simmer tamarind, sugar, and soy sauce into a tangy gravy.
Pan-fry tofu cubes.
Toss vermicelli with gravy and tofu.
Serve with egg, sprouts, shallots, and sambal.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Mexican Beef & Rice Casserole

ingredients.text: 1 chicken stock cube, made up to 400 ml

instructions: Mist a large deep nonstick pan with cooking spray and fry the beef and onion over a medium-high heat for 5 minutes, until browned and softened.
Add the fajita seasoning and cook, stirring, 1 minute.
Stir in the rice, beans, sweetcorn, peppers, tomatoes and stock. Season, bring to the boil, then reduce the heat and simmer, covered, 10 minutes.
Remove from the heat, stir in half the coriander and scatter over the cheese. Cover and stand 3-5 minutes until the cheese melts.
Scatter over the remaining coriander and serve with soured cream and lime wedges.
author: Marcus Baw (pacharanero/recipes)

title: Mignonette Sauce
instructions: Combine vinegar and shallot in a small bowl.
Stir in cracked pepper and sugar if using.
Let sit at least 15 minutes so the shallot mellows.
Spoon over freshly shucked oysters.
notes: Classic French accompaniment for raw oysters, sharper and lighter than cocktail sauce.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Minestra (Vegetable Bean Soup)

ingredients.text: 150 g dried kidney beans OR 1 can cooked beans, drained

instructions: In a pressure cooker or large pot combine diced vegetables (courgette, aubergine, pumpkin, onion, kohlrabi, turnips) with stock and 1 tbsp oil. Pressure cook 8–10 minutes or simmer 60 minutes until very soft.
Purée cooked vegetables until smooth.
Pound basil leaves with 6 garlic cloves and 1 tbsp oil to a coarse paste; stir into purée; season with salt and pepper.
Boil soaked kidney beans briskly 20 minutes; then simmer 60–90 minutes until tender (or use canned). Add to soup.
Cook pasta separately until al dente; add to soup and adjust seasoning.
Serve with grated Parmesan or hard cheese.
author: Marcus Baw (pacharanero/recipes)

title: Mint Sauce
instructions: Chop mint finely and place in a bowl with sugar.
Pour over boiling water and stir until sugar dissolves.
Stir in malt vinegar.
Let sit 10 minutes before serving.
notes: Traditional English condiment for roast lamb.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Miso Ginger Dressing
instructions: Blend miso with vinegar and water.
Whisk in sesame oil, ginger, and honey.
Adjust thickness with water.
Refrigerate until use.
Great on green salads and noodles.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Miso Glazed Salmon Rice Bowl
instructions: Whisk miso, soy, and honey.
Brush over salmon and bake at 210°C for 12 minutes.
Divide rice into bowls and add vegetables.
Top with salmon and any pan glaze.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Miso Mushroom Noodle Soup
instructions: Sauté mushrooms, garlic, and ginger in sesame oil.
Add water and simmer 5 minutes.
Whisk in miso off the heat.
Cook noodles separately, divide into bowls, and ladle over broth.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Mixed Dal with Drumstick

ingredients.text: 100 g each toor and moong dal

instructions: Cook dals and drumsticks with water and salt until tender.
Add sambar powder and tamarind; simmer 10 minutes.
Temper mustard seeds and curry leaves in oil.
Pour over dal.
Serve with steamed rice.
notes: South Indian dal with moringa pods.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Mojo Verde
instructions: Combine cilantro, garlic, cumin, and chile in a food processor.
Add vinegar and pulse to combine.
With the motor running, drizzle in olive oil until emulsified.
Season with salt and serve at room temperature.
notes: Canary Islands green sauce traditionally served with boiled wrinkly potatoes (papas arrugadas).
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Simplified Mole Sauce

ingredients.text: 3 dried ancho chiles, stemmed and seeded

instructions: Toast ancho chiles in a dry pan 1 minute, then soak in hot water 15 minutes.
Sauté onion and garlic until soft, then add tomato and cook 5 minutes.
Blend softened chiles, onion mixture, raisins, peanut butter, and cinnamon with stock until smooth.
Return to the pan, stir in chocolate, and simmer 15 minutes until thickened.
Season with salt and serve warm over chicken or enchiladas.
notes: Weeknight version of Oaxacan mole, skipping the long ingredient list of a traditional mole negro.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Moong Dal Tadka
instructions: Rinse moong dal and simmer with turmeric, salt, and water until soft, about 25 minutes.
Heat ghee; add cumin seeds until they pop.
Sauté onion, ginger, and garlic until golden.
Add tomatoes and garam masala; cook 5 minutes.
Stir tempering into dal, simmer 5 minutes, garnish with cilantro.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Moroccan Chickpea Stew
instructions: Sauté onion and carrots in oil.
Add spices and stir 30 seconds.
Add tomatoes, chickpeas, and 250 ml water.
Simmer 20 minutes; finish with cilantro.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Muhammara
instructions: Combine roasted peppers, walnuts, breadcrumbs, and garlic in a food processor.
Add pomegranate molasses, cumin, and Aleppo pepper.
Blend until mostly smooth, then drizzle in olive oil while blending.
Season with salt and let rest 10 minutes before serving.
notes: Syrian walnut and red pepper dip, tangy-sweet from pomegranate molasses.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Mung Bean Dal with Bottle Gourd

ingredients.text: 300 g bottle gourd (lauki), peeled and cubed

instructions: Simmer moong dal with bottle gourd, turmeric, and salt until both are tender.
Heat oil; toast cumin and green chili.
Pour tempering over dal.
Simmer 5 more minutes.
Garnish with cilantro.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Mushroom Barley Risotto
instructions: Sauté onion, garlic, and mushrooms.
Add barley and toast briefly.
Add stock in batches, stirring occasionally, until the barley is tender.
Finish with parmesan and black pepper.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Mushroom risotto
instructions: Place the porcini in a bowl and cover with 600ml of boiling water, then set aside to soak.

Prepare the pickle by tearing the wild mushrooms into bite-sized pieces and placing into a bowl. Heat the vinegar and sugar in a small pan until everything has dissolved, the pour over the mushrooms and set aside while you finish the risotto.
Heat the oil in a large frying pan. Finely the onion and celery, then add to the pan. cook gently for about 10 minutes until soft but not browned.
Add the chestnut mushrooms to the pan and fry for about 10 minutes, until the mushrooms have dried out and are starting to turn golden brown.
Strain the porcini soaking liquid into a jug and add the vegetable stock. Chop the rehydrated porcini and set aside.

Stir the garlic and rice into the pan and fry for a couple of minuutes until it starts going transparent around the edges. Add the wine and allow to cook down for a minute, then start adding the stock mixture. Add a ladleful at a time, allowing each addition to be absorbed before adding the next.
When all the stock has been added, check the risotto and add an extra splash of hot water and cook for a couple of minutes if required – the rice should be tender.
Add the zest and juice of the lemon, along with the chopped porcini. Chop the parsley and add as well. Cover, remove from the heat and set aside for 5 minutes.
Drain the pickled mushrooms and serve on top of the risotto.
notes: Thi sis a vegan risotto recipe. It doesn't have quite the same creaminess as one loaded with cheese, but the pickled mushrooms are great.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Mushroom Sauce
instructions: Melt butter and sauté mushrooms over high heat until browned, 6 minutes.
Add shallot and garlic, and cook 2 minutes.
Add white wine and simmer until nearly evaporated.
Stir in cream and simmer 4 minutes until thickened.
Season with salt and pepper.
notes: Rich creamy sauce for steak, chicken, or pork chops.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Nepali Dal Bhat Lentil Soup
instructions: Simmer split peas with turmeric and salt until smooth.
Heat ghee; toast cumin and dried chilies.
Add tomato to tempering; cook 3 minutes.
Stir into dal and simmer 8 minutes.
Serve with rice and cilantro.
notes: Everyday Nepali lentil component of dal bhat.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: No-Bake Cheesecake

ingredients.text: 1 sleeve + 2 sheets honey maid graham crackers

instructions: Crush the graham crackers into fine crumbs — you need about 2 cups. Mix with the melted butter and 2 tablespoons of sugar until it feels like wet sand.
Press the crust firmly into the bottom of a 9-inch springform pan, pushing it slightly up the sides. Refrigerate while you make the filling.
Beat the cream cheese with a hand mixer or stand mixer until completely smooth, about 3 minutes. Scrape down the bowl often — lumps are the enemy here.
Add the remaining sugar, vanilla, lemon juice, and salt. Beat until combined, another 2 minutes.
In a separate cold bowl, whip the heavy cream to stiff peaks. This takes about 3-4 minutes on high speed.
Fold one-third of the whipped cream into the cream cheese mixture to lighten it. Then gently fold in the remaining whipped cream, being careful not to deflate it.
Pour the filling over the crust and smooth the top with an offset spatula or the back of a spoon.
Cover with plastic wrap and refrigerate for at least 6 hours, or overnight for best results.
Release the springform ring, slice with a knife dipped in hot water, and serve.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Okinawa Soba
instructions: Simmer pork belly in dashi with awamori 20 minutes.
Season broth with soy sauce.
Cook Okinawa soba separately; divide into bowls.
Ladle hot broth and pork over noodles.
Top with fish cake, scallions, and pickled ginger.
notes: Hearty Okinawan wheat noodle soup bowl.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Olive Oil Béchamel Sauce

ingredients.text: Small piece onion, studded with 2 cloves
1–2 tbsp finely grated Parmesan or Manchego

instructions: (Optional infusion) Place milk with bay leaf and/or clove-studded onion in a saucepan. Bring just to a bare simmer, cover, and steep 10 minutes. Remove aromatics. Cool slightly so milk is warm, not hot.
Heat olive oil in a heavy saucepan over medium heat. Sprinkle in flour and stir continuously 2–3 minutes until foamy and slightly blond (do not brown). This cooks out raw flour taste.

Off the heat, whisk in about 150–200 ml of the milk until a smooth paste forms. Return to gentle heat and gradually add remaining milk in 4–6 additions, whisking each time until lump-free before adding more.

Once all milk is incorporated, switch to a silicone spatula and cook, stirring and scraping the bottom, 6–8 minutes until the sauce is thick enough to coat the back of a spoon (nappe) and a line drawn with a finger holds.
Season with salt, pepper and nutmeg. Add cheese now if using; stir until melted and smooth. Taste and adjust salt/pepper.
Use immediately, or cover the surface directly with baking parchment or cling film to prevent a skin if holding. For later use, cool quickly and refrigerate up to 3 days.
author: Marcus Baw (pacharanero/recipes)

title: One-Pot Lasagna

ingredients.text: 8 oz lasagna noodles, broken into rough pieces

instructions: Brown the ground beef in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat, breaking it into crumbles. Drain any excess fat.
Add garlic and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Pour in the marinara sauce and water. Stir in Italian seasoning, salt, pepper, and red pepper flakes.

Add the broken lasagna noodles, pushing them down into the liquid. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to medium-low. Cover and simmer for 15-18 minutes, stirring occasionally, until noodles are tender.
Drop spoonfuls of ricotta across the top. Sprinkle mozzarella over everything. Cover and cook 3-4 more minutes until the cheese is melted and gooey.
Let it rest for 5 minutes before serving. Garnish with fresh basil if you're feeling fancy.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Onion Bhaji

ingredients.text: 1 large onion, halved and thinly sliced
1 green chilli, deseeded and finely chopped

instructions: In a bowl whisk gram flour, chilli powder, turmeric, baking powder, cumin, and salt.
Add sliced onion, chilli, and coriander; toss to coat evenly.
Gradually add cold water, stirring, until a thick clinging batter forms (not runny).
Heat oil to 180°C / 350°F. Drop heaped tablespoons of mixture into oil; fry 3–4 minutes, turning, until deep golden.
Drain on kitchen paper and serve hot with chutney. Makes 10–12 bhajis.
author: Marcus Baw (pacharanero/recipes)

title: Pad Thai

ingredients.text: Crushed red pepper flakes to taste

instructions: Soak the rice noodles in warm water for 15–20 minutes while you prep everything else. You want them pliable but still slightly firm — they'll finish cooking in the wok. Drain well.
Mix the tamarind paste, fish sauce, brown sugar, and rice vinegar in a small bowl. This is your sauce. Taste it — it should be a tangy-sweet-salty trifecta. Adjust to your preference.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large wok or nonstick skillet over high heat. Sear the shrimp for about 1–2 minutes per side until just pink. Remove and set aside.
Add the remaining 1 tbsp oil to the wok. Toss in the garlic and cook for 15 seconds until fragrant. Push it to one side, crack in the eggs, and scramble them roughly, breaking into small pieces.
Add the drained noodles and pour the sauce over everything. Toss constantly with tongs for 2–3 minutes until the noodles are coated and tender.
Return the shrimp to the wok along with the bean sprouts and half the green onions. Toss for another 30 seconds just to warm through.
Serve immediately, topped with chopped peanuts, remaining green onions, cilantro, a squeeze of lime, and red pepper flakes.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Pad Thai with Shrimp
instructions: Soak rice noodles in warm water 20 minutes; drain.
Stir-fry garlic and shrimp in peanut oil until pink.
Push aside; scramble eggs in the wok.
Add noodles, fish sauce, tamarind, and palm sugar; toss 3 minutes.
Fold in bean sprouts; serve with peanuts and lime.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Pan-fried gnocchi with garlic and sage
instructions: Peel and cut the potatoes into medium-sized chunks - maybe 3-4cm in size.
Rinse the potatoes in clean water, then drop into the sauce pan. Fill with water, until there's at least 2-3cm covering the potatoes. Add a teaspoon of salt.
Set the heat to high and bring to a boil. Reduce the heat to a simmer, then cover. Cook for 15–20 minutes, until you can poke through the potatoes with a fork.
When the potatoes are cooked, remove from the heat and drain. Rinse with cold water and drain again, then mash with a potato masher or a fork – or ideally, if you have one, a potato ricer.
Mix the flour and salt together and tip out into a pile a flat work surface. Make a well in the middle of the flour and drop in the egg and extra yolk. Add the mashed potato on top.
Start combining the ingredients with your fingers. Bring the dough together until it's consistent and dry – it shouldn't stick to your fingers. Roll into a rough log shape.

Clean and lightly flour your work surface, then cut the gnocchi dough into six equal parts. One at a time, roll each part out into a rope-like shape—about 2cm across—then cut each rope into roughly equal gnocchi-sized pieces.

As you cut each piece from the dough, you can roll it lightly with the back of a fork to give it more of a traditional gnocchi shape. Of course, if you have a gnocchi board, that's even better. Move each completed dumpling to one side.
Bring a pot of clean, salted water to a boil. Add gnocchi, working in batches if required. When they rise to the surface, remove them with a slotted spoon and place in a clean bowl.
At this point, the gnocchi is ready – if you want to use it in some other recipe, stop here.
notes: This is a a recipe for basic gnocchi, along with a simple fried preparation. For the potatoes, most of them are going to work fine – King Edwards or Roosters seem to do totally fine, though. You can use this recipe just for the gnocchi and combine it with a different sauce to taste. I've just included them both here for convenience.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Panchmel Dal

ingredients.text: 50 g each: moong, masoor, chana, toor, urad dal

instructions: Rinse all dals; simmer together with turmeric and salt until creamy.
Heat ghee; toast cumin seeds.
Sauté onion until golden; add tomatoes and spices.
Cook masala 8 minutes.
Combine with dal, simmer 10 minutes, garnish with cilantro.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Papas a lo Pobre (Slow-Cooked Potatoes)
instructions: Heat olive oil in large frying pan over low heat. Add onions and whole garlic cloves; cook gently.
Add potatoes; cook slowly, stirring occasionally.
Add peppers and chillies; continue slow cooking until potatoes very tender and mixture soft and cohesive (can take 1–2 hours). Season with salt.
Serve warm with crusty bread.
author: Marcus Baw (pacharanero/recipes)

title: Paprika Chicken with Peppers
instructions: Brown chicken pieces in olive oil.
Add onion, peppers, and paprika.
Pour in stock and simmer until chicken is cooked.
Stir in cream and season.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Pasta Aglio e Olio
instructions: Cook spaghetti in salted boiling water until al dente; reserve 120 ml pasta water.
Gently sauté garlic and pepper flakes in olive oil until fragrant, not brown.
Toss drained pasta with garlic oil and a splash of pasta water.
Finish with parsley and serve immediately.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Pasta Bolognese
instructions: Mist a pan with cooking spray and put over a medium heat. Add the onion, carrot, celery and fennel seeds and cook 6-8 minutes until softened.
Add the mince and cook about 5 minutes until browned. Add the garlic and cook 1 minute.

Add the tomatoes, tomato purée, oregano and bay leaves. Crumble in the stock cube and add 375 ml water. Bring to the boil, then reduce to a gentle simmer. Cover and cook 40 minutes until thick. Season to taste.
Cook the pasta according to pack instructions. Drain and serve with the sauce, Parmesan and basil.
author: Marcus Baw (pacharanero/recipes)

title: Pasta with Salmon and Asparagus
instructions: Snap off the woody ends of the asparagus. Cut each stalk crosswise diagonally into 2.5 cm pieces.
Heat cooking spray in a nonstick frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add garlic and chilli flakes and sauté 30 seconds. Add the salmon and cook 3 minutes each side.

Cook the pasta in lightly salted boiling water according to pack instructions, adding the asparagus 3 minutes before the end. Drain well, return to the pan, add lemon juice and soft cheese, and stir over a low heat for 1 minute.
Break the salmon into bite-sized chunks, removing any skin and bones. Add to the pasta, toss gently and serve sprinkled with black pepper and dill.
author: Marcus Baw (pacharanero/recipes)

title: Patatas a lo Pobre (Andalusian Potatoes)

ingredients.text: 1 green pepper, chopped or in thick strips

instructions: Heat oil in deep frying pan over medium-high; add potatoes and salt; fry 5 minutes turning.
Reduce heat low; cover 10 minutes.
Add pepper and onion; stir; cover and fry gently another 10 minutes, checking occasionally.
Continue until potatoes tender with some crisp edges (add few minutes if needed). Adjust salt; drain excess oil if desired. Serve hot.
author: Marcus Baw (pacharanero/recipes)

title: Peanut Butter Cookies
instructions: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees. Line two baking sheets with parchment paper. That's half the cleanup already done.
In a medium bowl, mix the peanut butter, sugar, and egg together until smooth and fully combined. It'll look a bit oily and loose — that's normal. Stir in the vanilla if using.
Scoop the dough into tablespoon-sized balls and place them on the baking sheets about 2 inches apart. You should get about 24 cookies.
Press each ball with the back of a fork to make that classic crosshatch pattern, pressing down gently until about 1/2 inch thick. Rotate 90 degrees and press again.
Sprinkle each cookie with a tiny pinch of flaky sea salt if you're feeling fancy. (You should be feeling fancy.)
Bake for 10–12 minutes, until the edges are set and just starting to turn golden. The centers will look slightly underdone — that's what you want. They firm up as they cool.
Let the cookies cool on the baking sheet for 5 minutes before transferring to a wire rack. They're fragile when hot but sturdy once cool.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Peanut Noodles with Cucumber
instructions: Cook noodles; rinse cold.
Whisk peanut butter with soy sauce, vinegar, ginger, and 3 tbsp warm water.
Toss noodles with peanut sauce.
Top with cucumber and scallions.
Sprinkle crushed peanuts.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Peppercorn Sauce
instructions: Melt butter and sauté shallot until soft, 3 minutes.
Add crushed peppercorns and cook 1 minute.
Remove from heat, add brandy, then return to heat and simmer until nearly evaporated.
Add stock and simmer until reduced by half.
Stir in cream and simmer 3 minutes until thickened. Season with salt.
notes: Classic sauce au poivre for steak, traditionally flamed with brandy.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Peruvian Aji Verde
instructions: Combine cilantro, peppers, garlic, and mayonnaise in a blender.
Add lime juice and queso fresco if using.
Blend until smooth and bright green.
Season with salt and refrigerate until serving.
notes: Creamy green sauce served with Peruvian rotisserie chicken (pollo a la brasa).
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Picada Catalana (Nut-Herb Paste)
instructions: In a mortar pound saffron, garlic, salt, almonds, hazelnuts, cinnamon, and parsley to a fine paste.
Gradually work in dry sherry to desired spoonable consistency. Add to soups, meat, or fish midway through cooking as a flavour enhancer.
author: Marcus Baw (pacharanero/recipes)

title: Pico de Gallo
instructions: Combine tomatoes, onion, jalapeño, and cilantro in a bowl.
Add lime juice and salt, and stir gently.
Let sit 10 minutes for flavors to combine.
Drain excess liquid before serving if needed.
notes: Fresh uncooked salsa, best made the day you plan to eat it.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Pide
instructions: Combine the flour, yeast, sugar and salt in a bowl, then add the water. Stir until it comes together into a wet dough.
Turn out the dough on on to a floured surface. Knead for about 15 minutes, until smooth.
Place the dough in a clean, oiled bowl. Cover with a damp towel, then set aside in a warm place for 60–90 minutes until roughly doubled in size.

Turn the dough out onto a floured surface and cut in half. Flatten each half out slightly, then place onto two separate pieces of floured baking paper – each large enough to cover the baking trays. Cover with a damp towel and leave for about 15 minutes.

Preheat oven to about 230℃, then stretch each piece of dough out until it's roughly the size of the baking sheet. Take care to leave a little bit of volume around the edges – this will help it to form a nice light texture in the oven. Leave on the baking paper, cover with the damp towel again and set aside for 15 minutes.

Combine the egg yolk and oil in a small bowl, then brush all over both flatbreads. Use your fingers to make some small indentations all over each of them – then combine the nigella and sesame seeds and sprinkle evenly on top.

Place each flatbread on a baking tray and into the oven. Cook for about 8–10 minutes, until cooked and golden brown. Remove to a wire rack and allow to cook for a few minutes, before slicing into rough rectangles.
notes: This is a Turkish bread that's great for making things like a yogurtlu kebab – or just as a general BBQ side.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Pierogi
instructions: Start by preparing the filling. Peel and chop the potatoes into 2cm cubes, then add to a pot of salted water. Bring to the boil and cook until they are tender – you should be able to break them apart with light pressure.
Drain the potatoes and spread out on a cutting board. Mash with a fork, then sprinkle over the grated cheese, butter, and chives. Mix until combined, being careful not to over-mix. Set aside.
Next prepare the dough. Add the flour to a large bowl, then mix the eggs and milk together until combined and pur on top. Add the oil and salt, then mix into a loose dough. Set aside for 10 minutes.
Turn the dough out onto a floured surface and knead for about 10 minutes until smooth and elastic.

Roll the dough out until it's quite thin - about 3–4mm. Cut a series of small circles (about 5cm diameter) using whatever you have to hand – a cookie cutter, small bowl, or anything else. When you're done, combine the scraps, roll them out again, and keep cutting until you've used up all of the dough.
Add a spoonful of the filling to each circle, then fold the dough over, flatten into a pierogi shape, and crimp the edges with a fork. Repeat until you've prepared all of the pierogis.

Bring a large pot of salted water to the boil. Drop in a couple of pierogis at a time and allow them to cook. They will float to the top – once they start to float, leave them to cook for two minutes then remove them to a slotted spoon. Repeat until they're all done.

You can refrigerate or freeze the pierogis at this stage. When ready to serve, place a large skillet over a medium heat with some butter and thinly-sliced onions. Cook for about 10 minutes until the onions and sticky and brown. Add the pierogis and turn occasionally until lightly browned, then serve with the onions and a generous dollop of sour cream.
notes: Pierogis are a perfect comfort food. This recipe is for a basic pierogi dough stuffed with potato and cheese – first they are boiled, and then fried with some onions.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Pizza Bagels
instructions: Set oven rack to the upper-middle position and turn on the broiler to high.
Place bagel halves cut-side up on a baking sheet.
Spread about 1 tablespoon of Rao's marinara on each bagel half.
Top each with a generous handful of shredded mozzarella and 5-6 pepperoni slices.
Sprinkle with Italian seasoning and red pepper flakes if you're feeling fancy.
Broil for 3-5 minutes, watching closely, until cheese is bubbly and edges are golden.
Let cool for 2 minutes. Serve to the swarm of hungry humans who appeared out of nowhere.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Poached Eggs on Spinach
instructions: Wilt spinach in olive oil; keep warm.
Simmer water with vinegar; poach eggs 3 minutes.
Toast bread.
Serve eggs over spinach with toast.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Pork Chops with Creamy Leeks & New Potatoes

ingredients.text: 700 g new potatoes, halved or quartered if large
500 g pork loin chops , fat trimmed
3 large leeks, trimmed and thinly sliced
Zest of 1 lemon, plus wedges to serve
1 tbsp fresh parsley, roughly chopped, plus extra to serve

instructions: Cook the potatoes in boiling water 12-15 minutes until just tender, then drain and set aside.

Mist a large pan with cooking spray over a medium heat. Add the pork chops and garlic and cook 3 minutes, then turn and cook 2 minutes until golden and cooked through. Transfer to a plate and set aside.
Mist the pan with more cooking spray, add the leeks and cook 4-5 minutes until softened. Stir in both mustards, the crème fraîche and the lemon zest.
Season, bring to a simmer, stir in the parsley, then remove from the heat.
Scatter over extra parsley and serve with leeks, new potatoes and lemon wedges.
author: Marcus Baw (pacharanero/recipes)

title: Prawn & Chorizo Paella

ingredients.text: 1/4 tsp saffron threads, soaked in 2 tsp cold water
1 chicken stock cube, made up to 500 ml

instructions: Mist a large lidded pan with cooking spray and fry the onion and chorizo 5 minutes over a medium heat. Add the pepper and cook 5 minutes.
Stir in the garlic, paprika, saffron and rice and cook 1 minute. Pour in the stock, bring to the boil, then reduce the heat and simmer, covered, 15 minutes.
Stir in the prawns, peas and half the parsley, cover and cook 5 minutes.
Remove the lid and cook 3-4 minutes until the stock is absorbed. Season, scatter over the remaining parsley and serve with lemon wedges.
author: Marcus Baw (pacharanero/recipes)

title: Quick Brown Sauce
instructions: Melt butter and sauté onion and carrot until softened and lightly browned, 8 minutes.
Stir in tomato paste and flour, and cook 2 minutes.
Gradually whisk in beef stock, add bay leaf, and simmer 12 minutes until thickened.
Strain through a sieve, pressing on the solids.
Season with salt and pepper.
notes: Home-cook shortcut for classic French sauce espagnole, skipping the multi-day stock reduction.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Quick Chicken Korma

ingredients.text: 1 chicken stock cube, made up to 400 ml

instructions: Mist a large deep nonstick pan with cooking spray and set over a high heat. Season the chicken, then cook, stirring often, for 5 minutes until golden. Transfer to a plate and set aside.

Put the onion, ginger and garlic into a food processor with 2 1/2 tbsp water and blitz to a smooth paste. Add the onion mixture to the pan, along with the cinnamon and cardamom, and cook 2-3 minutes until fragrant. Stir in the korma paste and cook 1 minute.
Add the stock and ground almonds and whisk until combined. Return the chicken (and any resting juices) to the pan and simmer 10 minutes until cooked through.
Remove from the heat and stir through the chutney and yogurt until combined.
Cook the beans in boiling water for 4-5 minutes until tender. Cook the rice to pack instructions.
Serve the chicken on a bed of rice with flaked almonds scattered over and green beans on the side.
author: Marcus Baw (pacharanero/recipes)

title: Quick Cucumber Kimchi
instructions: Salt cucumbers 15 minutes; drain.
Mix gochugaru, fish sauce, sugar, and garlic.
Toss cucumbers with paste.
Add scallions.
Chill 1 hour; garnish with sesame seeds.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Quinoa Power Salad

ingredients.text: 2 tablespoons fresh parsley or dill, chopped

instructions: Cook 1 1/2 cups quinoa according to package directions. Spread on a sheet pan to cool quickly (about 10 minutes).
While the quinoa cools, dice the cucumbers, halve the cherry tomatoes, thinly slice half the red onion, and roughly chop 1/2 cup kalamata olives.
Make the lemon vinaigrette: whisk together lemon juice, olive oil, red wine vinegar, Dijon mustard, minced garlic, salt, and pepper.
In a large bowl, combine the cooled quinoa with all the chopped vegetables and olives.
Crumble 1 cup of feta cheese over the top.
Pour the vinaigrette over everything and toss gently to combine.
Taste and adjust seasoning. Garnish with fresh herbs if using.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Quinoa Salad with Chickpeas
instructions: Cook quinoa and cool.
Combine with chickpeas, cucumber, and tomatoes.
Dress with olive oil, lemon, and mint.
Season and serve chilled.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Rajma-Style Kidney Bean Dal
instructions: Soak kidney beans overnight; simmer until tender.
Sauté onion in oil until golden.
Add ginger-garlic and spice powders; cook 2 minutes.
Add tomato puree and simmer 10 minutes.
Stir in beans and cook 15 minutes; garnish with cilantro.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Ranch Dressing
instructions: Whisk mayonnaise, sour cream, and buttermilk together until smooth.
Stir in chives, dill, garlic powder, and onion powder.
Season with salt and pepper.
Chill at least 20 minutes for flavors to develop.
notes: America's favorite all-purpose dressing and dip, thin with extra buttermilk if needed.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Ratatouille
instructions: Sauté onion and garlic in olive oil.
Add aubergine and cook 8 minutes.
Add peppers, courgettes, and tomatoes.
Simmer 25 minutes until vegetables are tender.
Finish with basil.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Red Wine Jus

ingredients.text: 1 tsp cold butter, extra, for finishing

instructions: Melt butter and sauté shallot until softened, 3 minutes.
Add red wine and thyme, and simmer until reduced by half.
Add beef stock and simmer 15 minutes until syrupy and coats the back of a spoon.
Strain, then whisk in cold butter off the heat for shine.
Season with salt and pepper.
notes: Simple pan-style jus for steak or roast beef, built from stock rather than a multi-day demi-glace.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Remoulade
