instructions: Whisk mayonnaise and mustard together.
Stir in capers, cornichons, and paprika.
Add lemon juice and hot sauce.
Chill at least 20 minutes before serving with crab cakes or fried seafood.
notes: Tangy French-Louisiana hybrid sauce, at home with crab cakes, po'boys, or fries.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Rice Noodles with Lemongrass Pork
instructions: Marinate pork with lemongrass, fish sauce, and sugar 20 minutes.
Grill or stir-fry pork until charred.
Soak vermicelli in hot water; drain.
Serve noodles with pork, lettuce, and herbs.
Sprinkle peanuts on top.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Ricotta Lemon Honey Cups
instructions: Whisk ricotta with lemon zest and honey until smooth.
Spoon into small glasses.
Top with blueberries and almonds.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Roast potatoes
instructions: Heat the oven to 200℃. Add the oil to a large roasting tray and place in the oven.

Peel the potatoes, chop into the appropriate size, and place into a pan of cold water. Rinse a couple of times, then fill with fresh water until the potatoes are just covered. Salt the water with a couple of teaspoons.
turn on the heat and bring to the boil. After the water starts boiling, wait for five minutes then turn off the heat.
Drain the potatoes in a colander, and toss them around so they're fluffy around the edges. Sprinkle the semolina over them and toss again. Leave to steam dry for a couple of minutes.
Remove the hot pan from the oven and carefully add the potatoes one by one. Turn each one to ensure they're coated in oil.
Return to the oven and roast for 45 minutes to 1 hour. Turn every 15 minutes and baste with hot oil.
When they're done, remove from teh oven and toss with some fresh sea salt to serve.
notes: Everyone has their own approach to roast potatoes – mine is similar to Gordon Ramsay's and uses semolina. I use Rooster potatoes for pretty much everything, and they work fine for roasting.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Roast Salmon with Peas, Potatoes & Chorizo

ingredients.text: 3 medium red onions, cut into wedges

instructions: Put the potatoes in a pan of cold water. Bring to the boil and simmer 30-35 minutes until cooked. Drain and steam-dry 2 minutes, then halve.
Heat oven to 200°C (fan 180°C / gas 6). Toss the potatoes, chorizo, onions, herbs, paprika and olive oil in a roasting tray. Season and roast 20 minutes, tossing halfway through.
Scatter over the peas, top with the salmon and season. Mist with cooking spray and roast 12-15 minutes until the fish is cooked through and flakes easily.
Grind over black pepper and serve.
author: Marcus Baw (pacharanero/recipes)

title: Roasted Beet Lentil Salad
instructions: Roast wrapped beets at 200°C until tender, then peel and cube.
Whisk oil, vinegar, mustard, salt, and pepper.
Combine beets, lentils, rocket, onion, and walnuts.
Dress just before serving.
notes: Add goat cheese for a richer version.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Roasted Carrot Hummus Dip
instructions: Roast carrots until soft and lightly caramelized.
Blend with chickpeas, tahini, lemon juice, garlic, and salt.
Loosen with water until creamy.
Serve with crudités or crackers.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Roasted Cauliflower Tahini Pitas
instructions: Roast cauliflower with oil, cumin, salt, and pepper at 220°C until browned.
Mix yogurt and tahini.
Fill warm pitas with cauliflower, sliced cucumber, and sauce.
Finish with herbs.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Roasted green veg with burrata
instructions: Preheat the oven to 220℃.
Wash the vegetables. Slice the leek and courgette into thin slices, then chunk the asparagus and pepper. Boil the peas for a couple of minutes and set aside.
Add the leek, courgette, and pepper to a roasting tray; add half of the olive oil and a pinch of salt, and toss to coat. Roast for 15 minutes.
Add the asparagus to the roasting tray and return to the oven for another 10 minutes.
Add the garlic, basil, juice of the lemon, and the rest of the olive oil to a good processor and blend to a smooth paste.
Remove the veg from the oven and transfer to a large bowl. Add the basil sauce and toss to coat.

Meanwhile, tear the bread into chunks, toss with a bit more olive oil, and pop in the oven for about 10 minutes until crisp. Whizz in the food processor along with the chilli and some salt, along with a bit of olive oil, until you have a fine crumb.

Assemble the dish – pile the veg on a plate, then top with the burrata. Slice a cross into the top so that it opens out like a flower, then sprinkle the chilli crumb on top. Add some sea salt and a drizzle of olive oil to serve.
notes: A tasty, simple, and eyecatching veggie meal that's quick to prepare – based on a recipe from Mob Kitchen. Make the crumb with any leftover bread product.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Roasted Pumpkin Red Lentil Soup
instructions: Roast pumpkin with oil at 210°C until caramelized.
Cook onion and garlic until soft.
Add lentils, stock, cumin, and roasted pumpkin.
Simmer until lentils break down, then blend.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Roasted tomato pasta sauce
instructions: Preheat the oven as hot as it will go – 220℃ or so
Slice the tomatoes in half (or smaller if they're absolutely massive) and place them cut-side down in a roasting tin. Add the olive oil and cover everything thoroughly.

Pop the roasting tin in the oven. The tomatoes will start to cook and release their juice – you want to cook them for about 30–45 minutes, until the juice is just starting to brown on the base of the tin.
While the tomatoes are cooking, dice the shallot and the garlic. Add to the roasting tin for about 4–5 minutes until just starting to brown.
Remove the roasting tin from the oven, and remove the tomato skins – they'll be burned and should just pop off the top of the tomatoes
Start combining the tomatoes, shallots, and garlic into a thick sauce. Deglaze the pan with the sauce – you can add a splash of wine of vinegar at this stage if you want.
Add the butter and allow it to melt, stirring to combine. This will result in a thick and glossy sauce.
Serve with pasta and a generous helping of parmesan.
notes: A simple roasted tomato sauce which is great with fresh tomatoes from the garden.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Roasted tomatoes with burrata
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180℃. Toast the pine nuts in a dry pan and set aside.

Chop the garlic and half the tomatoes. Add both to a small baking tray with of 1tbsp of the olive oil and season with salt and pepper. Roast for 45 minutes. Drizzle over the vinegar and set aside to cool.
Zest and juice the lemon, then add to a food processor along with a handful of the basil. Add the rest of the olive oil and a pinch o salt, then whizz until combined.

Split the tomato mixture between 2 plates; add a burrata on top of each, then scatter with the pine nuts and basil mixture. Scatter with some extra basil and a little salt and freshly-ground pepper, then serve.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Roasted Veg in Yoghurt Sauce

ingredients.text: 250 g baby parsnips, peeled and halved if large

instructions: Heat oven to 200°C (fan 180°C / gas 6). Bring a large pan of water to the boil and cook the parsnips 1 minute, then the carrots 1 minute, then the cauliflower 1 minute. Drain, reserving a cup of the cooking water.
Put the parsnips, carrots and red onion in a roasting tin and drizzle with olive oil. Roast 15 minutes.
Add the cauliflower, dried coriander, coriander seeds and lemon juice. Toss and roast 10 minutes.
Blend the yogurt, garlic, turmeric, honey, mint and lemon juice to a smooth sauce. Loosen with a little reserved cooking water until drizzling consistency; season to taste.
Transfer veg to a platter, drizzle with sauce and scatter over mint and pomegranate seeds.
author: Marcus Baw (pacharanero/recipes)

title: Roasted Vegetable Soup
instructions: Toss vegetables with oil, thyme, salt, and pepper.
Roast at 200°C for 25 minutes.
Simmer roasted vegetables in broth 10 minutes.
Blend until smooth and adjust seasoning.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Rolitos (Stuffed Veal Rolls)

ingredients.text: 2 tsp gravy powder or cornstarch to thicken

instructions: Lay veal slice; place ham half, egg quarter, and two olive halves; roll and secure with toothpicks. Repeat.
Sauté garlic and onion until soft; add stock and thickener; bring to simmer.
Add veal rolls; simmer gently until cooked through and flavours meld (~25–30 minutes). Adjust seasoning.
Serve with mashed potatoes and sauce.
author: Marcus Baw (pacharanero/recipes)

title: Romesco Sauce
instructions: Combine roasted peppers, tomato, almonds, bread, and garlic in a food processor.
Blend until mostly smooth.
Add vinegar and paprika, and blend again.
With the motor running, drizzle in olive oil until emulsified.
Season with salt and serve at room temperature.
notes: Catalan roasted pepper and almond sauce, classic with grilled vegetables and fish.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Root Veg Crisps with Houmous

ingredients.text: 150 g roasted red peppers in brine, drained

instructions: Heat oven to 180°C (fan 160°C / gas 4). Trim the vegetables and slice very thinly. Pat dry with kitchen paper.
Toss the veg slices with the oil and paprika. Lay on lined baking trays and bake 16-18 minutes until crisp and golden (remove pieces as they’re done). Season and cool on a rack.
Blitz the chickpeas with roasted peppers, chilli, cayenne, tahini, garlic and lemon juice until smooth. Loosen with a little reserved chickpea liquid if needed. Season to taste.
Serve the houmous with the crisps for dipping.
author: Marcus Baw (pacharanero/recipes)

title: Rosto (Pork Pasta Stew)

ingredients.text: 400 g tomato passata or crushed tomatoes

instructions: Fry garlic and onion in olive oil until soft.
Add fresh tomatoes; cook 5 minutes; add pork loin and brown.
Add passata, wine, potatoes, and carrots; simmer until meat and vegetables tender.
Add mushrooms last 10 minutes. Season with salt, pepper, and a pinch sugar.
Cook pasta separately until al dente; slice meat; serve meat, vegetables, and sauce over pasta with cheese.
author: Marcus Baw (pacharanero/recipes)

title: Rouille
instructions: Whisk egg yolk with garlic, paprika, and saffron if using.
Drizzle in olive oil slowly while whisking constantly until thick and emulsified.
Season with salt and cayenne.
Serve dolloped on fish soup or spread on toasted baguette.
notes: Provençal saffron-chili mayonnaise, the traditional garnish for bouillabaisse.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Salsa Golf
instructions: Whisk mayonnaise and ketchup together until smooth and pale pink.
Add lemon juice and Worcestershire sauce if using.
Whisk in cayenne if desired for a little heat.
Chill before serving.
notes: Argentine and Uruguayan classic for shrimp cocktail and fries.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Salsa macha

ingredients.text: 250ml light olive, sunflower, or vegetable oil
2tbsp apple cider or white wine vinegar

instructions: The basic idea is to toast the chillies by frying them in the oil, then blending he whole lot. Start by removing any stems and seeds from the chillies, then chop them into small pieces (about 1cm).
Add the peanuts, garlic, sesame seeds and the oil to the saucepan, then heat over medium-high – cook for a few minutes until the garlic is starting to crisp up but not burn.
Add the chillies, then remove from the heat and leave to toast while cooling for 10 minutes.
Stir in the vinegar, sugar, salt, and oregano and leave until cool enough to process further.
Add to a food processor and pules until combined. You're not aiming to over-process it – you want crispy bits of nuts and chilli rather than a puree.
Jar and keep in the fridge, using as needed.
notes: Salsa Macha is very distinctive Mexican sauce made from toasted chillies, peanuts, and oil ground into a fine paste. It's extremely savoury and satisfying, and useful for things like tacos, nachos, huevos rancheros etc. You can sub out the chillies for whatever you can get access to really – anything like chipotle peppers or other "workhorse chillies" will be great.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Salsa Roja

ingredients.text: 2 dried guajillo chiles, stemmed and seeded

instructions: Toast guajillo chiles in a dry pan 1 minute, then soak in hot water 10 minutes.
Char tomatoes, onion, and garlic under a broiler or in a dry pan until blistered.
Blend tomatoes, onion, garlic, drained chiles, and lime juice until smooth.
Season with salt and simmer 5 minutes to deepen the flavor.
notes: Cooked red table salsa, milder and smokier than fresh pico de gallo.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Salsa Verde
instructions: Boil tomatillos, jalapeño, onion, and garlic 8 minutes until soft.
Drain and transfer to a blender with cilantro and lime juice.
Blend until mostly smooth with a little texture.
Season with salt and cool before serving.
notes: Tangy Mexican tomatillo salsa, great on tacos or enchiladas.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Sardine and Tomato Toast
instructions: Toast bread.
Top with tomato slices.
Lay sardines over tomatoes.
Finish with lemon, parsley, and pepper.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Sarmale
instructions: First, prepare the filling. Dice the onions, then heat the oil in a frying pan over a medium heat. Cook the onion for about 10 minutes until soft. Stir in the paprika and tomato paste, the turn off the heat. Stir in the rice until combined, then add the beef and pork along with the salt, and pepper. Chop the dill, reserve about 3-4tbsp, and add the rest to the meat mixture. Stir until well combined and set aside.
Prepare the cabbage – peel apart the leaves, then cut out the large veins and slice each leaf into small triangles of about 6-7cm across. Chop the veins and any offcuts, and reserve in a bowl.

Start making the cabbage rolls. Place about 1tbsp of the filling on a slice of the cabbage leaf, placed in the middle bottom. Fold in the sides and then roll up and set aside. Repeat until the filling has all been used.
Take any remaining cabbage leaves or offcuts, chop them, and add them to the reserved cabbage bowl. Combine with the reserved dill along with a bit of salt and pepper.

Place the thyme sprigs in the stock pot, then add half of the chopped cabbage on top. Add the cabbage rolls to the pot one at a time, working in circles until one layer is complete, then move onto the next one. Once all of the rolls are used, spread the remaining chopped cabbage on top, then add the chopped tomatoes.
Pour hot, salted water on top until the cabbage rolls are almost submerged, then place the stockpot over a medium heat until it starts to boil. Turn the heat to low and then simmer for about 1 hour.
Remove the cabbage rolls and serve the the chopped cabbage, along with sour cream, polenta, and dill.
notes: These are traditional Romanian cabbage rolls, eaten at Christmas, Easter, and other special occasions. I can't get enough of them – serve them with some polenta, along with a generous serving of sour cream and dill. The pickled cabbage can be a bit of a specialty ingredient in the UK, but should be available from various Eastern European stores. Look for something like "Keseli Kupus"
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Sauce Vierge
instructions: Combine tomatoes with olive oil and lemon juice in a bowl.
Stir in garlic, basil, and chives.
Season with salt and pepper.
Let sit at room temperature 10 minutes before serving over fish.
notes: Uncooked French "virgin sauce," a light olive oil and herb dressing for grilled fish.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Sauerkraut
instructions: Clean the bowl and jar thoroughly with boiling water – it's important to make sure everything is spotless, or you will spoil your sauerkraut.
Clean the cabbage and remove and tough or torn outer leaves, Split and remove the core. Strip and retain one of the large cabbage leaves to the side.

Finely shred the cabbage—ideally in a food processor—then add to the large bowl. Cover with salt, then rub into the cabbage with your hands for about 5 minutes. Leave to sit for about 5 minutes, then massage the cabbage for about 5 minutes. You should end up with a bowl of salty cabbage in brine.

Mix in the caraway and peppercorns, then transfer the cabbage along with the brine to the fermentation jar. Place the reserved cabbage leaf on top, to act as a kind of "lid" – then weigh down the cabbage as much as possible. You want all of the cabbage to be under the level of the brine. It will generate carbon dioxide as it ferments, so don't cover the jar with an airtight lid – you can cover it with some muslin or cheesecloth secured with a rubber band to keep any insects out.
Set the jar aside and leave at room temperature for about a week – out of direct sunlight. You can continue fermenting it for up to a month for more flavour.
When you're happy with it, transfer it to smaller clean jars and store in the fridge for up to six months.
notes: I usually end up making sauerkraut whenever I have leftover cabbage, because i hate throwing anything away.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Sausage & Bean Casserole

ingredients.text: 2 yellow peppers, deseeded and thinly sliced
2 large cans butter beans, drained and rinsed

instructions: Mist a deep nonstick pan with cooking spray and set over a medium-high heat. Add the sausages, onion and peppers and cook 6-8 minutes until the sausages are cooked through and the vegetables are tender.
Stir in the tomatoes and Worcestershire sauce and season well. Bring to the boil, then reduce the heat and simmer 10 minutes until thickened. Stir in the beans and simmer 2 minutes.
Set a griddle pan over a high heat. Mist the bread with cooking spray, then griddle 1-2 minutes each side. Remove and rub the cut sides with the garlic.
Serve the casserole with the toast on the side and parsley scattered over.
author: Marcus Baw (pacharanero/recipes)

title: Sauteed Greens with Garlic
instructions: Wash greens and remove tough stems.
Sauté garlic in oil until fragrant.
Add greens in batches until wilted.
Season with salt, pepper flakes, and lemon.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Seitan steak
instructions: First, cook the lentils (if required) according to the instructions and allow to cool. Any variety of lentils are fine.

Add the gluten, lentils, yeast, tomato puree, liquid smoke and spices to a food processor along with 100ml of water and half of the soy sauce. Pulse until combined - if you don't have a food processor, you can do this by hand.

Turn the dough out onto your work surface and start kneading. It will start off quite dry and crumbly, but as you knead it, it will start to come together. After a few minutes, you will have a taut ball – stop at this point.
Split the dough into four equal chunks, then roll each out into rough steak shapes using a rolling pin. It will be quite tight and stretchy, so you might need to use a bit of force.

Add a bit of water to a pan that's suited to using with your steamer basket, then bring to the boil. Once boiling, place the steaks in the basket and cover. Steam for about 25–30 minutes, flipping halfway through and making sure the pan doesn't boil dry. The steaks should roughly double in size.

While steaming, combine the remaining soy sauce with the maple syrup, olive oil, and 60ml of water in a large bowl. Remove the steamed steaks and add to the bowl, turning to coat them all over. Leave them to marinade for an hour or so – or overnight.
When ready to cook, heat a frying pan or grill pan, and fry the steaks for a couple of minutes on each side. Slice and serve.
notes: This is a recipe for making steak-like seitan patties from scratch. They're pretty tasty and I often use them as the base for something like tacos.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Sesame chicken

ingredients.text: 2 tbsp - cider or white wine vinegar

instructions: First, prepare the sauce – just combine all of the ingredients thoroughly and set aside.
Prepare the batter – whisk together the cornflour, salt and egg, and season with pepper. Cut the chicken thighs into bite-sized pieces, drop into the batter, and mix well.

In the frying pan, heat about 1 tablespoon of oil. Place the chicken into the pan, piece by piece, making sure it makes good contact with the pan. Leave plenty of space for each piece – you will want to do this in two or three batches, adding more oil as required. Turn each piece a couple of times, until they are golden brown and cooked through.
When all of the chicken is cooked, add it all back to the pan, whisk the sauce to ensure it's still combined, and then pour it over the chicken.
Simmer on a gentle heat, stirring periodically, until the sauce has thickened. Remove from the heat and serve.
notes: This is a Korean-style chicken recipe – the chicken is coated in a light batter and fried, then cooked in a sweet and sticky soy-based sauce. It's pretty sweet and salty, so not one for every day – but it's delicious.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Sesame Ginger Beef and Broccoli
instructions: Sear beef quickly in sesame oil.
Add garlic, ginger, and broccoli with a splash of water.
Stir in soy sauce and honey and cook until glossy.
Serve immediately.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Shakshuka

ingredients.text: Fresh parsley or cilantro for garnish

instructions: Heat olive oil in a large, deep skillet over medium heat. Add onion and cook for 4-5 minutes until softened.
Add garlic, cumin, paprika, chili powder, salt, pepper, and cayenne. Stir for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Pour in both cans of diced tomatoes. Stir and let the sauce simmer for 5 minutes until it thickens slightly.
Use a spoon to make 6 small wells in the sauce. Crack one egg into each well.
Cover the skillet, reduce heat to medium-low, and cook for 5-7 minutes until the egg whites are set but the yolks are still runny (or longer if you prefer them firm).
Crumble feta over the top, garnish with fresh herbs, and serve straight from the skillet with crusty bread for scooping.
notes: Eggs poached in spiced tomato sauce — fancy brunch energy on a Tuesday budget.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Shanghai Scallion Oil Noodles
instructions: Cook noodles until al dente; drain.
Slowly fry scallions in oil until deeply golden.
Mix dark soy, light soy, and sugar into scallion oil.
Toss hot noodles with sauce until coated.
Serve immediately while glossy.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Sheet Pan Chicken Fajitas

ingredients.text: Optional toppings: sour cream, guacamole, shredded cheese, salsa

instructions: Preheat oven to 425F. Line a large sheet pan with foil or parchment paper.
Slice chicken thighs into thin strips. Slice bell peppers and onion into similar-sized strips.

Toss chicken, peppers, and onion on the sheet pan with olive oil, cumin, chili powder, garlic powder, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper. Spread in a single layer (use two pans if needed — crowding is the enemy of crispy edges).
Roast for 20 minutes, tossing halfway through, until chicken is cooked through and vegetables have some nice charred spots.
Squeeze fresh lime juice over everything. Serve in warm tortillas with your favorite toppings.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Sheet Pan Gnocchi with Sausage and Broccoli
instructions: Spread gnocchi, sliced sausage, broccoli, and onion on a tray.
Toss with oil, fennel seeds, salt, and pepper.
Roast at 220°C for 22-25 minutes, stirring once.
Finish with parmesan if desired.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Shredded chicken thighs
instructions: Add the oil to the saucepan over a medium heat. Add the chicken thighs, trying to keep them in contact with the base of the pan as much as possible. Cook for a few minutes undisturbed, until starting to brown, then flip and repeat.
Peel and cut the shallots into quarters lengthwise, then throw them along with the rest of the ingredients into the pot. Add enough water to just cover the chicken.
Bring to a boil, then reduce and simmer until tender – about 30 minutes.
Remove the thighs to a bowl and shred with two forks. Continue cooking the stock until it's reduced by about half.
Spoon a couple of tablespoons of the stock over the chicken and toss to keep it moist.
Keep the chicken for up to three days in the fridge. Reserve the stock in the fridge as well - the fat will separate out and can be scraped off for use in other recipes.
notes: This recipe is a basic shredded chicken that's useful for things like chicken fried rice, tacos, enchiladas etc. – it produces plenty of stock and schmalz as well.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Sichuan Hot Dry Noodles (Re Gan Mian)
instructions: Cook alkaline noodles; drain well.
Whisk sesame paste with soy, vinegar, and chili oil.
Toss hot noodles vigorously with sauce.
Top with pickled mustard stems.
Garnish with scallions.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Simple Green Salad with Lemon Vinaigrette
instructions: Wash and dry salad leaves.
Whisk olive oil, lemon, mustard, salt, and pepper.
Toss vegetables with dressing just before serving.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Singapore Curry Noodles
instructions: Soak vermicelli until soft; drain.
Stir-fry chicken and shrimp in oil until cooked.
Add curry powder and bell pepper; cook 2 minutes.
Add coconut milk and fish sauce; simmer 5 minutes.
Toss in noodles, garnish with cilantro and lime.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Sinigang na Baboy (Filipino Sour Pork Soup)

ingredients.text: 1 packet tamarind soup base or fresh tamarind

instructions: Simmer pork ribs until tender, about 30 minutes.
Add tamarind, tomato, and daikon.
Add string beans; cook 5 minutes.
Season with fish sauce.
Finish with spinach off heat.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Skillingsbolle (Cinnamon Rolls)
instructions: In mixing bowl combine flour, 100 g of the sugar, and softened margarine/butter.
Dissolve fresh yeast in lukewarm milk; add to flour mixture; mix and knead to soft dough. Cover and rise 1 hour until doubled.
Mix remaining 100 g sugar with cinnamon.
Divide dough into two; roll each to roughly 40×40 cm (16×16 in) square. Sprinkle evenly with cinnamon sugar; roll up tightly.
Slice each log into 12 pieces. Place cut-side down on lined tray; rise until puffy (~30–40 minutes).
Brush with lightly beaten egg white; sprinkle with sugar. Bake at 165°C / 325°F for 15–17 minutes until golden.
author: Marcus Baw (pacharanero/recipes)

title: Skordalia
instructions: Mash boiled potatoes until smooth while still warm.
Crush garlic cloves to a paste with a pinch of salt.
Beat garlic paste into potatoes, then drizzle in olive oil while beating.
Thin with vinegar and warm water until spreadable.
Season with salt and serve at room temperature.
notes: Greek garlic and potato dip, traditionally served with fried fish or bread.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Slow Cooker French Dip Sandwiches
instructions: Place the sliced onion in an even layer on the bottom of the slow cooker. This is your roast's little bed — treat it right.
Set the chuck roast on top of the onions.
Pour beef broth over the roast, then add Worcestershire sauce, garlic, Italian seasoning, thyme, salt, and pepper.
Cover and cook on LOW for 8 hours, until the beef is fall-apart tender and practically shreds itself.
Remove the roast and shred with two forks. It should put up absolutely no resistance.
Return the shredded beef to the slow cooker and stir it into the cooking liquid. Let it soak for a few minutes — this is where the magic happens.
Scoop shredded beef onto hoagie rolls and top each with a slice of provolone.
Broil open-faced in the oven for 1-2 minutes until the cheese is melted and bubbly.
Ladle the remaining cooking liquid through a fine mesh strainer into small bowls for dipping — that's your au jus, and it's liquid gold.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Soba with Tsuyu and Nori
instructions: Cook soba according to package; rinse cold.
Warm mentsuyu with 200 ml water.
Divide soba into bowls.
Pour hot tsuyu over noodles.
Top with nori, scallions, wasabi, and daikon.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Somen with Ginger Soy Dressing
instructions: Cook somen 2 minutes; plunge into ice water.
Mix soy sauce, mirin, and ginger.
Drain somen well.
Drizzle ginger soy dressing.
Top with nori and scallions.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Soto Ayam (Indonesian Chicken Soup)
instructions: Simmer chicken with lemongrass, turmeric, and galangal until cooked.
Shred chicken; strain golden broth.
Blanch noodles.
Assemble bowls with chicken, noodles, and sprouts.
Top with egg, shallots, and lime.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Soup Dumplings
instructions: Make the dipping sauce: stir together soy sauce, rice vinegar, grated ginger, sesame oil, and chili oil. Set aside. Taste it. Add more chili oil. Good.
Line your bamboo steamer with parchment paper or cabbage leaves — this prevents sticking and heartbreak.
Arrange dumplings about an inch apart. They expand, and crowded dumplings are stuck dumplings.
Bring a pot or wok of water to a rolling boil. Set the steamer on top.
Steam for 8–10 minutes. Don't peek for the first 7 minutes.
Bring a few inches of water to a boil in a wide pot.
Lightly oil a heat-safe plate that fits inside the pot with room around the edges for steam to circulate.
Arrange dumplings on the plate with space between them.
Carefully set the plate on top of the pot (or rest it on a small rack or crumpled foil ring inside the pot). Cover with a lid.
Steam for 8–10 minutes.
notes: Fifty dumplings for fifteen bucks. This is why we have a Costco membership.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Sourdough
instructions: Make the leaven the night before baking the loaves. Mix the active starter with the warm water and stir to disperse. Add the white and whole wheat flours, and combine well. Cover with a damp cloth and allow to sit at room temperature for about 12 hours. To test its readiness, drop a tablespoon into a bowl of room-temperature water. If it floats, it's ready – otherwise you'll need to give it more time.

To make the bread, combine 200g of leaven with 700g of the warm water and stir to disperse. Reserve the remaining leaven for other uses. Add the white bread flour and whole wheat flour, and mix until no dry material remains. Cover the bowl with a towel and leave to rest for 30-45 minutes at room temperature.

Add the sea salt and a further 50g of warm water. Use your hands to thoroughly mix the salt and water into the dough – it will start to fall apart but if you keep mixing it will come back together. Cover with a towel and transfer to a warm environment at about 25-27℃ and leave for 30 minutes.

After the dough has risen, fold it by taking hold of the underside of the dough ball at each corner and stretching it over the rest of the dough. Do this four times – once for each corner. Repeat the folding action for another 2.5 hours, every 30 minutes. After this, the dough should be light and about 30% larger in volume.

Transfer the dough to a work surface and dust with flour. Use a scraper to split into two parts, and flip them over so they are flour-side down. Fold the cut side up on itself, so that the flour remains on the outside. Work into tight rounds, then cover with a towel and rest for 30 minutes.
Line two bread-proofing baskets with towels and flour them using some of the rice flour.

Dust the rested rounds with some whole wheat flour. Use the dough scraper to flip them over so that the floured sides are facing down again. Fold the four corners into the middle of the dough again, so the flour is on the outside. Flip so that the fold is on the bottom, then shape into a smooth round ball. Repeat with the other round.
Transfer rounds to the prepared baskets, seam-side up. Cover and return to the warm environment for another three to four hours, or alternatively leave in the fridge for 10-12 hours.

Pre-heat the oven 30 minutes before baking. Use a dutch oven or other heavy, lidded pot, and heat to 260℃ or as close as you can get. Prepare a sheet of baking paper large enough to hold the loaf. Turn the loaf out on to the prepared sheet of baking paper, seam side down, then score the top using a lame to allow the crust to expand.

Carefully remove the dutch oven and place the baking paper and loaf directly into the pan, then cover and transfer to the oven. Immediately reduce the temperature to 230℃. Bake for 20 minutes covered, then remove the lid and bake for another 20 minutes. The load is ready when the crust is a rich brown shade.
notes: I am pretty bad at making sourdough – I don't have the patience for it. But I've had some good loaves out of this recipe, which I think came from an old NYT article or something.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Sourdough pizza
instructions: Combine starter, water, flour, and salt in a large bowl. Stir well until a rough, loose, sticky dough is formed.
Turn out onto a lightly floured surface, then knead thoroughly—adding a little more flour if needed—until a smooth and elastic ball of dough is formed. This should take about 10 minutes.
Store in the fridge, and leave to rise for at least 8 hours. The dough can be prepared up to 4 days in advance.

After the proof has completed, and 5 hours before baking, divide the dough into four equal portions and shape into tight balls. Place in a lightly oiled proofing container, like a high-walled baking dish, and leave on the counter.

When ready to bake, preheat the oven to the hottest you can make it. Make sure your topping ingredients are ready, then gently remove the proofed dough balls from the container and place on a lightly floured work surface.
Prepare the tomato sauce – drain the tomatoes and place into a blender, reserving the liquid for other recipes. Add the oil, salt, and oregano, and blend until smooth. Taste and season as required.

With each ball in turn, lay out a sheet of baking paper and lightly scatter with polenta. Gradually flattening out the ball into a pizza-sized disc, taking care to avoid pressing the air out of a crust at the rim – this is the bit you want to be puffy.
Add the toppings, and immediately place in the oven. Bake until cooked to your liking, then remove from the oven and serve.
notes: These need to be baked at as high a temperature as possible! This recipe includes a basic tomato sauce to which you can add whatever toppings you want. The sourdough starter is better the less well-fed it is.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: South Indian Rasam
instructions: Simmer tomatoes and tamarind in 500 ml water 10 minutes.
Add cooked dal and rasam powder.
Temper mustard seeds, curry leaves, and chilies in oil.
Pour tempering into rasam.
Garnish with cilantro.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Spaghetti alla Carbonara

ingredients.text: 200 g pancetta or smoked streaky bacon, cut into small lardons
2 garlic cloves, peeled and lightly crushed
50 g Pecorino Romano cheese, finely grated, plus extra to serve
50 g Parmesan cheese, finely grated, plus extra to serve
Sea salt, for the pasta water

instructions: Bring a large pan of salted water to the boil and cook the spaghetti until al dente according to the packet instructions. Reserve a mug of the cooking water before draining.

While the pasta cooks, heat a large frying pan over a medium heat. Add the pancetta and garlic and cook for 5–6 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the fat renders and the meat turns crisp and golden. Discard the garlic cloves.
In a mixing bowl whisk together the eggs, egg yolks, Pecorino, Parmesan, and a generous amount of black pepper until smooth.

Tip the drained spaghetti into the pan with the pancetta and toss to coat in the rendered fat. Remove the pan from the heat, pour over the egg and cheese mixture, and stir vigorously, loosening with a little reserved cooking water as needed to create a silky sauce that clings to the pasta.
Season to taste with additional pepper, divide between warm bowls, and serve immediately with extra grated cheese.
author: Marcus Baw (pacharanero/recipes)

title: Spaghetti Carbonara
instructions: Start cooking the pasta, according to the instructions, until al dente. This takes around 10 minutes. Don't drain it when done – we want to keep the cooking water.
Dice the pancetta if required and add to a largish cold frying pan or cast iron. Turn the heat on to medium low and allow the fat to render out.
Peel and lightly crush the clove of garlic with your hand, then drop it whole into the pan with the pancetta.
Finely grate the parmesan and combine with the egg yolks in a small bowl. Beat until combined, and season with a little pepper.

When the pasta is ready, remove the garlic from the pancetta and discard. Use a pair of tongs to grab the spaghetti and drop it into the pan with the pancetta – you should end up with a good amount of pasta water in there too.Mix it around to coat it with the fat.
Remove the pan from the heat and pour in the eggs and cheese. Stir gently until a smooth, glossy sauce develops, adding a couple of spoonfuls of pasta water as you go.
Serve with some extra black pepper and parmesan.
notes: It doesn't get much simpler than this. A go-to meal for me if I don't have much time. It's made most traditionally with pancetta, but regular bacon, ham, or even chorizo are pretty good too. You can skip the meat for a veggie option, and a couple of pinches of smoked paprika still captures the flavour of cooked bacon.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Spanish Tortilla
instructions: Gently fry potatoes and onion in olive oil until tender.
Drain excess oil and cool slightly.
Beat eggs with salt; mix with potatoes.
Cook in a nonstick pan 8 minutes per side until set.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Spiced Roasted Chickpeas
instructions: Dry the chickpeas thoroughly.
Toss with oil and spices.
Roast at 210°C until crisp, shaking once.
Cool fully for maximum crunch.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Spicy Korean Ramyeon Upgrade
instructions: Boil noodles with spice packet 4 minutes.
Crack egg into broth; poach 1 minute.
Add kimchi and gochugaru.
Top with cheese off heat.
Garnish with scallions and sesame seeds.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Spicy Sichuan Noodles
instructions: Cook noodles; drain and cool slightly.
Whisk chili oil, soy sauce, vinegar, and garlic.
Toss noodles with sauce.
Top with cucumber and peanuts.
Dust with Sichuan pepper powder.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Spinach and Ricotta Ravioli
instructions: Make dough: mix flour and eggs into a ball; knead briefly until smooth; wrap and rest 30 minutes.
Roll small portions through pasta machine repeatedly to thin sheets.
Blanch spinach 3 minutes; drain and squeeze dry; chop. Process spinach with egg yolk and ricotta; season.
Cut pasta sheets into rounds (or squares). Place 1 tsp filling on half the pieces; lightly moisten edges; top with second piece and seal well, expelling air.
Boil ravioli 3–5 minutes in salted water until al dente. Drain; serve drizzled with olive oil or sauce of choice.
author: Marcus Baw (pacharanero/recipes)

title: Spinach Chana Dal
instructions: Cook chana dal until tender.
Sauté cumin and onion in oil; add ginger.
Add spinach and cook until wilted.
Stir in dal and garam masala.
Simmer 10 minutes and season.
notes: Hearty spinach and split chickpea dal.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Spinach Feta Egg Muffins
instructions: Whisk eggs with milk, salt, and pepper.
Fold in spinach, feta, and onion.
Divide into an oiled muffin tray.
Bake at 190°C for 15-18 minutes.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Spinach Ricotta Stuffed Peppers
instructions: Halve and seed the peppers.
Mix ricotta, spinach, rice, parmesan, and garlic.
Fill peppers and bake at 200°C for 30 minutes.
Broil briefly for extra color.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Sri Lankan Red Lentil Curry (Parippu)
instructions: Rinse lentils and simmer in water until soft.
Blend half the cooked lentils smooth.
Sauté onion, garlic, cinnamon, and curry leaves in coconut oil.
Add curry powder, blended lentils, whole lentils, and coconut milk.
Simmer 10 minutes until creamy.
notes: Coconut red lentil staple of Sri Lanka.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Sriracha Mayo
instructions: Whisk mayonnaise and sriracha together until smooth.
Stir in lime juice and sesame oil if using.
Adjust sriracha to taste for more heat.
Chill before serving.
notes: Versatile spicy mayo for sushi rolls, poke bowls, and fries.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Steamed Bok Choy with Garlic
instructions: Halve bok choy and steam 5 minutes.
Heat oils; fry garlic until fragrant.
Add soy sauce off heat.
Drizzle garlic soy over bok choy.
Serve immediately.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Steamed Broccoli with Lemon
instructions: Steam broccoli 5-6 minutes until bright green and tender.
Toss with olive oil, lemon juice, salt, and pepper.
Serve immediately.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Steamed Edamame with Sea Salt
instructions: Boil edamame in salted water 4 minutes.
Drain and toss with sea salt.
Drizzle lightly with sesame oil.
Serve warm in pods.
Sprinkle extra salt at table.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Steamed Fish with Ginger and Scallion

ingredients.text: 400 g whole sea bass or fillets

instructions: Score fish and place on steaming plate.
Top with ginger and half the scallions.
Steam 10-12 minutes until flaky.
Drizzle soy and wine over.
Top with remaining scallions and pour hot oil.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Steamed Noodles with Scallion and Soy
instructions: Steam noodles until just cooked.
Heat oil until smoking; pour over scallions.
Add soy sauce and sugar to scallion oil.
Toss steamed noodles with sauce.
Season with white pepper.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Steamed Vegetable Bao
instructions: Make soft yeast dough; rise 1 hour.
Stir-fry bok choy and mushrooms with soy and sesame oil.
Divide dough; fill with vegetable mixture.
Steam bao 12 minutes.
Serve warm.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Sweet Potato Black Bean Tacos
instructions: Roast sweet potato with oil and cumin at 220°C until soft.
Warm black beans with a pinch of salt.
Fill tortillas with sweet potato, beans, and avocado.
Serve with lime.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Sweet Potato with Masala-Spiced Baked Beans

ingredients.text: 2-inch piece fresh ginger, peeled and grated
2 large cans cannellini beans, drained and rinsed

instructions: Heat oven to 200°C (fan 180°C / gas 6). Mist sweet potatoes with cooking spray, season, and place in a roasting tin. Bake about 60 minutes until tender when pierced.
Midway through roasting, mist a large non-stick frying pan and cook onion over medium-low heat 6–8 minutes until softened; add a splash of water if it starts to stick.
Add chilli, ginger, and garlic; cook 1 minute. Stir in coriander, cumin, turmeric, and tomato puree; cook 1 further minute to bloom spices.
Add cannellini beans, cinnamon stick, and about 400 ml water. Stir, bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer 10 minutes until sauce thickens slightly. Remove cinnamon stick.
Split each baked sweet potato (cut a cross and squeeze). Spoon over spiced beans. Top each with a spoon of yogurt and scatter with fresh coriander.
author: Marcus Baw (pacharanero/recipes)

title: Tabbouleh
instructions: Soak bulgur in boiling water 20 minutes; drain well.
Combine parsley, mint, tomatoes, and spring onions.
Dress with lemon, olive oil, and salt.
Fold in bulgur and chill before serving.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Tahini Broccoli Crunch Salad
instructions: Steam broccoli 2 minutes then cool.
Whisk tahini, lemon juice, maple syrup, and 2 tbsp water.
Mix broccoli, carrot, cabbage, seeds, and raisins.
Coat with dressing and serve.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Taiwanese Beef Noodle Soup
instructions: Braise beef with doubanjiang, tomato, and spices 90 minutes.
Cook noodles separately.
Blanch bok choy.
Ladle braising liquid and beef over noodles.
Serve with pickled mustard greens.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Tartare Sauce
instructions: Combine mayonnaise, capers, gherkins, and parsley in a bowl.
Stir in lemon juice and mustard.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Chill at least 15 minutes before serving.
notes: Classic accompaniment for fried or battered fish.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Teriyaki Beef Stir Fry

ingredients.text: 500 g lean beef sirloin steak, thinly sliced
300 g green beans, trimmed and cut into 2 cm pieces

instructions: Put the steak in a bowl, add the chilli flakes, season and toss to combine. Set aside.
Cook the noodles according to pack instructions, then drain and set aside.
Heat the oil in a large wok or frying pan and stir-fry the ginger over a high heat for 30 seconds. Add the beans and stir-fry 3-5 minutes, then remove and set aside.
Increase the heat to high and stir-fry the beef in batches for 1-2 minutes.
Return the beans to the wok along with the noodles and teriyaki sauce. Toss to combine and stir-fry 1-2 minutes until hot.
author: Marcus Baw (pacharanero/recipes)

title: Teriyaki Salmon Bowl
instructions: Pan-sear salmon skin-side down 4 minutes.
Flip; glaze with teriyaki and cook 3 minutes.
Steam broccoli.
Serve salmon over rice with broccoli.
Garnish with ginger and sesame seeds.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Teriyaki Sauce (Homemade)
instructions: Combine all ingredients in saucepan.
Simmer over medium heat 8 minutes until glossy.
Cool completely.
Store in jar refrigerated.
Use for grilling or stir fries.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Thai Basil Beef (Pad Kra Pao)
instructions: Stir-fry garlic and chilies.
Add beef; cook until browned.
Season with oyster sauce, soy, and fish sauce.
Fold in Thai basil off heat.
Serve over rice with fried egg.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Thai Basil Chicken Noodles
instructions: Soak rice noodles; drain.
Stir-fry garlic and chilies.
Add minced chicken; cook through.
Toss noodles with fish sauce and oyster sauce.
Finish with Thai basil off heat.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Thai Cashew Chicken (Gai Pad Med Mamuang)
instructions: Stir-fry chicken until golden; set aside.
Fry dried chilies and garlic.
Return chicken with bell pepper and sauces.
Toss in cashews off heat.
Garnish with scallions.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Thai Chili Garlic Sauce (Nam Jim)
instructions: Dissolve sugar in warm water.
Stir in vinegar, chili, garlic, and soy.
Rest 15 minutes for flavors to bloom.
Adjust heat with more chili if needed.
Refrigerate up to 2 weeks.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Thai Coconut Lime Noodles
instructions: Cook rice noodles; drain.
Warm coconut milk with ginger.
Add soy sauce and lime juice.
Toss noodles with coconut lime sauce.
Top with snow peas, basil, and chili.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Thai Coconut Mushroom Soup
instructions: Simmer broth with lemongrass and lime leaves.
Add mushrooms; cook 5 minutes.
Stir in coconut milk gently.
Season with soy and lime.
Finish with Thai basil.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Thai Coconut Rice
instructions: Rinse rice until water runs clear.
Combine rice, coconut milk, water, salt, and pandan.
Simmer covered on low 18 minutes.
Rest 10 minutes off heat.
Fluff and serve.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Thai Corn and Tomato Salad
instructions: Char corn kernels in dry pan 3 minutes.
Combine with tomatoes and shallots.
Whisk lime, soy, and palm sugar.
Toss with Thai basil.
Serve warm or room temperature.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Thai Cucumber Relish
instructions: Dice cucumbers finely.
Dissolve sugar in vinegar.
Toss with shallot and chili.
Fold in cilantro.
Serve with satay or curries.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Thai Drunken Noodles (Pad Kee Mao)
instructions: Soak wide rice noodles until pliable.
Stir-fry garlic and chilies in oil.
Add chicken; cook until done.
Toss noodles with oyster sauce, fish sauce, and soy sauce.
Finish with Thai basil off heat.
notes: Spicy basil rice noodle stir fry.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Thai Glass Noodle Salad (Yum Woon Sen)
instructions: Blanch glass noodles; rinse cold.
Whisk fish sauce, lime, and palm sugar.
Toss noodles with shrimp and tomatoes.
Add dressing and mint.
Garnish with peanuts and shallots.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Thai Green Curry with Chicken
instructions: Fry curry paste in thick coconut cream 2 minutes.
Add chicken; cook 5 minutes.
Add remaining coconut milk and vegetables.
Simmer 12 minutes.
Season with fish sauce and palm sugar; finish with basil.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Thai Green Papaya Salad (Som Tum)
instructions: Pound chilies and palm sugar in mortar.
Add green beans and tomatoes; bruise lightly.
Toss shredded papaya with fish sauce and lime.
Pound briefly to combine flavors.
Serve topped with peanuts.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Thai Grilled Fish with Herb Salad

ingredients.text: 400 g whole mackerel or sea bass

instructions: Score fish; marinate with fish sauce, lime, and lemongrass.
Grill or broil 8 minutes per side.
Mix herb salad with shallots and chilies.
Serve fish with herb salad and rice.
Drizzle extra lime.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Thai Larb Gai (Chicken)
instructions: Cook ground chicken in dry pan until done.
Toss with lime, fish sauce, shallots, and chilies.
Add herbs and rice powder.
Serve in lettuce cups.
Eat immediately while warm.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Thai Larb Salad (Mushroom)
instructions: Dry-toast rice until golden; grind to powder.
Sauté mushrooms until lightly browned; cool.
Toss mushrooms with lime, soy, shallots, and chilies.
Add herbs and rice powder.
Serve in lettuce cups.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Thai Mango Salad

ingredients.text: 1 tbsp fish sauce or soy sauce

instructions: Slice mangoes and cucumber.
Whisk lime, fish sauce, and palm sugar.
Arrange fruit and herbs on plate.
Drizzle dressing.
Top with crushed peanuts.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Thai minced beef
instructions: First prepare the sauce - chop the chillies, slice the garlic very finely, then combine with the fish sauce, lime juice, and coriander. Mix and set aside.

Heat the oil in the wok over a high heat. Finely chop the chillies for the beef, along with the garlic and a pinch of salt. Add to the hot pan and toss for a couple of minutes without letting it burn.
Meanwhile, heat about 4cm of oil in your other frying pan for the eggs.
Add the beef and stir fry for a couple of minutes until only just cooked. You don't want to overdo it.
Add the sugar and fish sauce along with a couple of tablespoons of water. Turn the heat down and cook for a couple of minutes.
Chop the Thai basil and add to the beef, stirring to combine.
Fry the eggs – drop them into the hot oil. Just drop the egg straight in and fry until the white is crispy and the yolk is still runny. It should take less than 60 seconds.
Serve the beef with jasmine rice, a fried egg, and with the sauce poured over.
notes: This is my attempt to recreate a specific chilli beef dish that's available from Busaba. It's pretty faithful – the most important thing is the Thai basil. This can be quite hard to come by, but specialist shops should offer it. It's best served with jasmine rice and the fried egg on top. A regular fried egg is also fine, if you don't want the faff of deep frying!
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Thai Pad See Ew
instructions: Soak wide rice noodles until soft.
Stir-fry garlic and chicken until cooked.
Push aside; scramble eggs in wok.
Add noodles, oyster sauce, and dark soy; char over high heat.
Toss in Chinese broccoli briefly.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Thai Peanut Lime Dressing
instructions: Whisk peanut butter with warm water.
Add lime juice, soy sauce, maple syrup, and ginger.
Blend until silky.
Adjust sweetness with maple syrup.
Use on salads and slaws.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Thai Pomelo Salad (Yam Som O)
instructions: Segment pomelo into bite pieces.
Whisk fish sauce, lime, and palm sugar.
Toss pomelo with shrimp and shallots.
Add dressing and mint.
Top with coconut and peanuts.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Thai Rice Noodle Salad (Yum Woon Sen)
instructions: Soak and blanch glass noodles; cool.
Whisk fish sauce, lime, and palm sugar.
Toss noodles with shrimp, tomatoes, and shallots.
Dress and fold in mint.
Top with peanuts.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Thai Stir-Fried Morning Glory

ingredients.text: 2 tbsp oyster sauce or vegetarian oyster sauce

instructions: Cut morning glory into 8 cm lengths.
Stir-fry garlic and chilies in hot oil.
Add morning glory; toss over high heat 2 minutes.
Add oyster sauce and splash of water.
Serve immediately while crisp-tender.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Thai Tamarind Dressing
instructions: Dissolve tamarind and palm sugar in 3 tbsp warm water.
Add fish sauce, lime, garlic, and chili.
Simmer 3 minutes until glossy.
Cool before use.
Perfect for papaya salad.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Tofu Broccoli in Black Bean Sauce
instructions: Pan-fry tofu until golden.
Blanch broccoli 2 minutes.
Stir-fry garlic and black bean sauce.
Add tofu, broccoli, and soy with splash of water.
Thicken with cornstarch slurry.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Tom Kha Gai (Coconut Chicken Soup)
instructions: Simmer broth with lemongrass and lime leaves 8 minutes.
Add chicken and mushrooms; cook 5 minutes.
Stir in coconut milk; do not boil hard.
Season with fish sauce and lime.
Serve with chilies.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Tom Yum Goong (Hot and Sour Shrimp Soup)
instructions: Simmer broth with lemongrass, lime leaves, and galangal 10 minutes.
Add mushrooms and shrimp; cook 3 minutes.
Season with fish sauce and lime juice.
Adjust sour-spicy balance.
Serve immediately.
notes: Classic Thai hot and sour soup.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Tomato and Basil Bruschetta
instructions: Combine tomatoes, basil, garlic, oil, vinegar, and salt.
Rest 10 minutes.
Toast bread.
Top bread with tomato mixture and serve.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Tomato chutney
instructions: Peel and finely slice the onions, roughly chop the tomatoes and finely slice the chilli.
Put everything in a pan, season to taste and stir well. Simmer for 30 to 40 minutes until sweet and sticky. Pour into a sterilised jar and leave to cool.
notes: This is what I do with tomatoes if I have loads of them left over at the end of the season – particularly if they're a bit under-ripe.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Tomato Dal (Tamatar Dal)
instructions: Simmer masoor dal with turmeric until soft.
Sauté mustard seeds, curry leaves, and chilies in oil.
Add tomatoes and cook until broken down.
Stir into dal and simmer 10 minutes.
Adjust salt and serve.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Toor Dal Sambar
instructions: Cook toor dal until soft; mash lightly.
Simmer vegetables in water with sambar powder and tamarind until tender.
Add cooked dal and simmer 10 minutes.
Temper mustard seeds, curry leaves, and dried chili in oil.
Pour tempering over sambar and serve with rice.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Torta de Acelga (Chard Pie)
instructions: Remove and reserve chard stems for other use; wash leaves thoroughly. Boil until tender; drain well; chop. Sauté briefly in olive oil; cool.
Beat eggs; mix with breadcrumbs, cheese, garlic, parsley, salt, and pepper; combine with chard.
Line pie dish with pastry; add filling; cover with remaining pastry (if available) or leave open.
Bake at 150°C / 300°F about 30 minutes until golden and set.
author: Marcus Baw (pacharanero/recipes)

title: Trail Mix
instructions: Grab your biggest mixing bowl.
Dump in almonds, cashews, chocolate chips, dried cranberries, and coconut flakes.
Mix it all together with your hands or a big spoon.
Portion into bags or containers.
Resist the urge to eat half the batch while portioning.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Tuna and White Bean Salad
instructions: Combine tuna and beans in a bowl.
Add onion, olive oil, vinegar, and oregano.
Toss gently and season with pepper.
Serve on greens or with bread.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Turkey Meatballs in Herbed Tomato Sauce
instructions: Mix turkey, egg, breadcrumbs, parsley, garlic, salt, and pepper.
Shape into meatballs and brown in a pan.
Add passata and simmer until cooked through.
Serve with courgette ribbons or pasta.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Turmeric Scrambled Eggs with Tomatoes
instructions: Whisk eggs with milk, turmeric, salt, and pepper.
Burst tomatoes in butter over medium heat.
Add eggs and stir gently until softly set.
Finish with parsley.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Tuscan Ragu

ingredients.text: Salt and freshly ground black pepper
1 celery stalk, finely chopped or grated
A few sprigs of rosemary, sage, and bay

instructions: Heat the olive oil in a heavy casserole over medium-high heat. Add the meat, season with salt and pepper, and brown until deeply caramelised on all sides.

Reduce the heat to low. Add the celery, carrot, and onion, stirring to coat in the fat. Drop in the rosemary, sage, and bay leaves (and a pinch of nutmeg, if using). Cover and let the vegetables sweat gently for a few minutes.
Stir in the tomato paste, then pour in the red wine. Turn the heat to its lowest setting, cover, and move the pot to the smallest burner.
Simmer very gently for about 2 hours. Check occasionally; if the pot looks dry, add a splash of water and stir to prevent sticking.
The ragu is ready when the meat pulls away from the bone with a fork. If it still feels tough, continue cooking until tender.
Cook your pasta in salted water. Off the heat, toss with the ragu and finish with plenty of Parmigiano Reggiano.
author: Marcus Baw (pacharanero/recipes)

title: Tzatziki
instructions: Grate cucumber, salt lightly, and squeeze out excess liquid in a clean towel.
Combine cucumber with yogurt, garlic, olive oil, and lemon juice.
Stir in dill and season with salt.
Chill at least 20 minutes before serving.
notes: Cooling Greek yogurt dip for gyros, grilled meats, and pita.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Udon in Light Curry Broth
instructions: Simmer onion in dashi 5 minutes.
Dissolve curry roux into broth.
Blanch udon; place in bowls.
Ladle curry broth over noodles.
Top with fish cake, egg, and scallions.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Ultimate Roast Potatoes

ingredients.text: 100g duck or goose fat , or 100ml/3½fl oz olive oil

instructions: Heat the oven to 200C/fan 180C/gas 6 with a roasting tin inside large enough for the potatoes in a single layer.
Peel the potatoes and cut into 5cm chunks (2–3 pieces for smaller potatoes, 4 for medium).
Put the potatoes in a large pan and add just enough water to barely cover.
Salt the water, bring to a rolling boil, reduce the heat, and simmer uncovered for 2 minutes.
Put the fat or oil in the hot roasting tin and return to the oven for a few minutes until very hot.
Drain the potatoes in a colander, shaking to rough up the edges.
Sprinkle over the flour and shake again to coat evenly.
Carefully add the potatoes to the hot fat, turning to coat, and spread in a single layer.
Roast for 15 minutes, turn the potatoes, roast another 15 minutes, then turn again.
Continue roasting for 10–20 minutes more, until unevenly golden and crisp.
author: Marcus Baw (pacharanero/recipes)

title: Urad Dal with Fenugreek
instructions: Simmer urad dal with turmeric until creamy.
Heat oil; toast fenugreek seeds briefly.
Sauté onion and ginger-garlic paste.
Combine with dal and simmer 10 minutes.
Garnish with cilantro.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Vegetable Fried Rice
instructions: If you forgot to make rice yesterday, spread freshly cooked rice on a sheet pan and refrigerate uncovered for 30 minutes. You need dry, cold rice — fresh hot rice turns into a gummy, steamy mess in the wok.

Heat the vegetable oil in a large wok or nonstick skillet over high heat until it's just starting to smoke. Add the frozen stir-fry vegetables and cook for 3–4 minutes, stirring frequently, until thawed and any moisture has evaporated. Move them to one side of the pan.
Crack the eggs into the empty side of the wok and scramble them quickly into small curds, about 1 minute. Mix them into the vegetables.
Add the garlic and ginger, stirring for 15 seconds until fragrant.

Add the cold rice, breaking up any clumps with your spatula. Spread it in a single layer and let it sit without stirring for 30–45 seconds to get some crispiness on the bottom. Then toss and repeat. This is where the magic happens.
Drizzle the soy sauce and rice vinegar over the rice and toss everything together. Cook for another 1–2 minutes.
Remove from heat, drizzle with sesame oil, and toss one final time. Serve topped with green onions, white pepper, and sriracha if you like heat.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Vegetable Stir Fry with Tofu
instructions: Pan-fry tofu until golden; set aside.
Stir-fry garlic and ginger in oil.
Add vegetables and cook until crisp-tender.
Return tofu with soy sauce and sesame oil.
Serve over rice.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Velouté Sauce

ingredients.text: Salt and white pepper to taste

instructions: Melt butter in a saucepan over medium heat.
Whisk in flour and cook 2 minutes to form a blond roux, without browning.
Gradually whisk in stock, a little at a time, until smooth.
Simmer 10 minutes, whisking occasionally, until thickened.
Season with salt, white pepper, and a squeeze of lemon if desired.
notes: One of the French mother sauces, the base for many creamy chicken and fish preparations.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Vietnamese Beef Salad (Bo Luc Lac)
instructions: Marinate beef with soy, fish sauce, and oyster sauce.
Sear beef cubes over high heat 2 minutes.
Arrange lettuce, tomato, and cucumber.
Top with beef and onion.
Serve with lime-pepper salt.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Vietnamese Canh Chua (Sour Soup)
instructions: Simmer tamarind and tomatoes 10 minutes.
Add pineapple and okra.
Add fish; cook 5 minutes.
Season with fish sauce.
Finish with sprouts and herbs off heat.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Vietnamese Cao Lau Style Bowl
instructions: Marinate pork with soy sauce and five-spice 30 minutes.
Grill pork until charred; slice.
Blanch thick rice noodles.
Layer noodles with pork, sprouts, and mint.
Crush rice crackers on top.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Vietnamese Caramelized Pork (Thit Kho)
instructions: Caramelize sugar until amber.
Add pork and garlic; brown.
Add fish sauce and coconut water.
Simmer covered 45 minutes.
Add eggs last 10 minutes; serve with rice.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Vietnamese Chicken Salad (Goi Ga)
instructions: Shred poached chicken while warm.
Combine cabbage, carrot, and herbs.
Whisk fish sauce, lime juice, and sugar.
Toss chicken and vegetables with dressing.
Top with shallots and peanuts.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Vietnamese Lemongrass Chicken
instructions: Marinate chicken with lemongrass, fish sauce, sugar, and garlic 30 minutes.
Grill or pan-sear until charred and cooked.
Rest and slice.
Serve over rice with pickles.
Garnish with chili.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Vietnamese Lemongrass Dressing
instructions: Mince tender inner lemongrass finely.
Whisk with vinegar, soy, maple syrup, and oil.
Add minced garlic.
Steep 15 minutes.
Strain if desired before dressing salads.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Vietnamese Lotus Root Salad
instructions: Blanch lotus root slices 2 minutes; cool in vinegar water.
Combine with carrot.
Whisk vinegar, sugar, and soy sauce.
Toss with herbs.
Top with peanuts.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Vietnamese Mi Quang
instructions: Simmer pork with turmeric and fish sauce until tender.
Cook turmeric noodles.
Use minimal broth for saucy noodles.
Top with pork, peanuts, and banana blossom.
Serve with herbs and crushed rice crackers.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Vietnamese Nuoc Cham
instructions: Dissolve sugar in warm water.
Whisk in fish sauce and lime juice.
Add garlic and chili.
Taste and adjust sweet-sour-salty balance.
Store refrigerated 2 weeks.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Vietnamese Papaya and Shrimp Salad
instructions: Shred papaya into thin strips.
Whisk fish sauce, lime, and sugar.
Toss papaya with shrimp and herbs.
Dress and plate.
Top with peanuts and fried shallots.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Vietnamese Pho Bo
instructions: Simmer bones with charred onion and spices 2 hours.
Strain broth; season with fish sauce.
Blanch rice noodles.
Top with raw beef slices; ladle hot broth.
Serve with herbs, sprouts, and lime.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Vietnamese Pho Ga (Chicken Pho)
instructions: Simmer chicken with charred onion, ginger, and star anise 90 minutes.
Shred chicken; strain broth.
Season broth with fish sauce.
Blanch noodles; assemble bowls.
Top with chicken, herbs, and lime.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Vietnamese Pickled Carrot and Daikon
instructions: Massage carrot and daikon with salt 15 minutes.
Rinse and squeeze dry.
Dissolve sugar in vinegar.
Cover vegetables with pickling liquid.
Refrigerate 2 hours before use.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Warm Halloumi Peach Salad
instructions: Slice peaches and halloumi.
Sear halloumi in a dry pan until golden.
Whisk oil, honey, and lemon juice.
Layer leaves, peaches, halloumi, and pistachios, then dress.
notes: Swap peaches for nectarines out of season.
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: Warm tomato and mozzarella dip
instructions: Pre-heat the oven to 200℃
Combine cream cheese, mozzarella, and half of the vinaigrette in a medium, oven-safe dish. Mix thoroughly to make sure everything is evenly distributed. Even out the surface with a spatula.
Chop the cherry tomatoes in half, and arrange cut-side-down on top of the dip. Drizzle remaining vinaigrette and season.
Bake for 15 minutes, or until the tomatoes have started to soften and the dip is heated through.
Sprinkle the parmesan on top and return to the oven until melted and slightly golden.
Serve with some crusty white bread.
notes: A very simple dip recipe, which looks great!
author: Hermanni Mäkitalo (KitchenGadget8000)

title: White bean and chicken chilli
instructions: Dice the onion, then finely chop the fresh jalapeño. Heat the oil over a medium heat in a large pot, then add the onion and jalapeño. Cook until soft – about 5 minutes.
Mince the garlic and add to the pot along with the oregano and cumin. Cook for about a minute until starting to become fragrant, then add the drained jalapeño slices.
Cut the chicken breasts into thirds (if you're using pre-cut chunks or mini-fillets then don't bother) and add to the pot along with the stock. Bring to a boil then reduce to a simmer and cover.

When tender and cooked (about 10–12 minutes) transfer the chicken to a plate and shred using two forks, like pulled pork. Transfer back to the pot and add the cannellini beans and sweetcorn, then bring to a simmer and cook for about 10 minutes.
Use your spoon to mash about a quarter of the beans. If it's still a bit watery then leave to reduce for a little longer. Turn off the heat then add the sour cream and stir.
Season to taste with salt and pepper, then serve in bowls garnished with coriander, cheese and some crushed tortilla chips.
notes: A quick white chilli recipe with chicken and cannellini beans. You can use other beans too if you like, and you can also use tinned, frozen, or fresh sweetcorn. The amounts aren't that important.

title: White Bean and Escarole Soup
instructions: Sauté onion and garlic in olive oil.
Add broth, beans, and rosemary; simmer 10 minutes.
Stir in escarole until wilted.
Simmer 8 minutes, season, and serve.

title: White Chicken Chili

ingredients.text: 2 cans great northern white beans, drained and rinsed
Sour cream, shredded cheese, tortilla chips for topping

instructions: Add shredded rotisserie chicken, white beans, green chiles, onion, garlic, cumin, oregano, cayenne, and chicken broth to the slow cooker. Stir.
Cover and cook on LOW for 4 hours or HIGH for 2 hours.
Cut the cream cheese into cubes and stir into the chili during the last 30 minutes of cooking. Stir occasionally until fully melted and creamy.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve topped with sour cream, shredded cheese, and crushed tortilla chips.
notes: Creamy, slightly spicy, and suspiciously easy for something this comforting.

title: Wonton Soup
instructions: Mix pork with ginger, soy, and sesame oil.
Fill wontons and pleat.
Simmer broth; add bok choy.
Poach wontons in broth 5 minutes.
Serve garnished with scallions.

title: Worcestershire Marinade Sauce
instructions: Whisk all ingredients together in a bowl.
Pour over steak or chicken and marinate at least 30 minutes.
Reserve leftover marinade and simmer 3 minutes if using as a basting sauce.
Discard any marinade that touched raw meat unless boiled first.
notes: All-purpose savory marinade built around Worcestershire's fermented depth.

title: Yaki Udon with Mushrooms
instructions: Blanch udon in boiling water 2 minutes; drain.
Stir-fry mushrooms and cabbage over high heat 4 minutes.
Add udon, soy sauce, and mirin; toss 3 minutes.
Drizzle sesame oil and top with nori.
Serve with pickled ginger.

title: Yakisoba
instructions: Stir-fry pork in oil until browned.
Add cabbage and carrot; cook 3 minutes.
Add noodles and yakisoba sauce; toss 4 minutes.
Serve with pickled ginger.
Sprinkle aonori on top.

title: Yellow Dal with Cumin Rice Pairing
instructions: Simmer dal with turmeric and salt until smooth.
Heat ghee; toast cumin and green chili.
Pour tempering over dal.
Add lemon juice.
Garnish with cilantro and serve with jeera rice.

title: Yogurt Berry Frozen Bark
instructions: Mix yogurt with honey.
Spread on a lined tray and scatter berries and pistachios.
Freeze until solid, then break into shards.

title: Yorkshire puddings
instructions: Preheat the oven to as high a temperature as you can - 230℃ or so.

Pour a little sunflower oil into each hole in a large yorkshire pudding tin – you're looking for it to be about 5mm deep depending on the size and depth of the tin. Pop it in the oven and allow it to heat up.
Meanwhile, prepare the batter. Beat the eggs into the flour then add the milk, continuing to beat until you've got a smooth batter. Pour into a jug.
Once the oil is up to temperature, remove the tin from the oven and pour the batter into the holes, distributing it evenly – remember, this recipe is for 12 puddings, so don't over-fill the holes!
Place immediate back into the oven and leave to cook for about 20 minutes until puffy and brown. Remove and serve immediately.
notes: This recipe usually comes out perfect – just get the oven as hot as you can and don't open it – and make sure the oil is hot before you start cooking! This recipe makes enough for 12 large puddings – so you'll need to work in batches or use multiple tins.

title: Zha Jiang Mian
instructions: Cook noodles; drain and rinse.
Brown pork with garlic in oil.
Add sweet bean paste, soy sauce, wine, and sugar; simmer 10 minutes.
Spoon meat sauce over noodles.
Top with julienned cucumber.
notes: Beijing noodles with fermented bean sauce.

title: Zucchini Fritters with Dill
instructions: Grate courgettes, salt lightly, and squeeze out excess moisture.
Mix with egg, flour, feta, and dill.
Pan-fry spoonfuls in a little oil until golden.
Serve warm.
